_note: Major NT→OT citations and allusions with source identification. Curated. Expand as chapters are added. Format: { 'MRK 1:2': { 'type': 'citation'|'allusion', 'source': 'MAL 3:1', 'greek_matches': 'LXX'|'MT'|'paraphrase', 'notes': '...' }}
_source: NA28 marginal references + scholarly consensus (Beale & Carson NT Use of the OT, UBS GNT apparatus).

1TH 5:3.notes: Echo of OT prophetic critique of false prophets who proclaim ‘peace, peace’ (LXX Jer 6:14, 8:11 ‘εἰρήνη εἰρήνη, καὶ ποῦ ἐστιν εἰρήνη’; Ezek 13:10 ‘λέγοντες· εἰρήνη, καὶ οὐκ ἦν εἰρήνη’). Paul applies the prophetic indictment to those who trust the imperial Pax-et-Securitas slogan rather than Christ. Composite allusion; no single direct quotation.

1TH 5:8.notes: Lexical echo of LXX Isa 59:17 (καὶ ἐνεδύσατο δικαιοσύνην ὡς θώρακα καὶ περιέθετο περικεφαλαίαν σωτηρίου): θώρακα + περικεφαλαίαν + σωτηρ-stem all preserved. Paul substitutes faith/love for righteousness, hope-of-salvation for helmet-of-salvation, and casts the believer (rather than YHWH) as the one armoring up. Cf. Eph 6:14-17 for Paul's expanded armor metaphor.

1TI 2:13.notes: Adam formed first, then Eve — order-of-creation argument.

1TI 5:18.notes: Deuteronomy 25:4 gives the prohibition against muzzling a threshing ox, with the verb of muzzling first. First Timothy places the ox and participle first. The worker’s wages parallel Luke 10:7, where γάρ connects the saying to its setting. The verbal agreement does not settle priority.

1TI 6:7.notes: 'Brought nothing in, take nothing out' echoes Job.

2TI 4:17.notes: ἐρρύσθην ἐκ στόματος λέοντος echoes LXX Ps 21:22 (= MT Ps 22:21) σῶσόν με ἐκ στόματος λέοντος. Paul applies the Davidic-Messianic suffering-Psalm motif to his own deliverance-from-trial. The lion-mouth-rescue is the Psalmist's prayer in the canonical-suffering-and-vindication template; Paul's first-defense survival is read as analog. Combined with v.18's eschatological-deliverance-into-kingdom, the Davidic-rescue + heavenly-vindication frame closes Paul's farewell.

TIT 2:14.notes: λαὸν περιούσιον is a direct lexical echo of the LXX covenant-people-of-special-possession formula. EXO 19:5 LXX 'ἔσεσθέ μοι λαὸς περιούσιος ἀπὸ πάντων τῶν ἐθνῶν'; DEU 7:6, 14:2, 26:18 same lemma περιούσιος in identical covenant-formula context. Paul applies the OT-Israel covenant-vocabulary to the Christ-redeemed people. Compare 1 Pet 2:9 (λαὸς εἰς περιποίησιν) for a parallel NT-application using a near-equivalent expression. Reflects NT-covenant-extension theology (church-as-grafted-into-Israel-promises, ROM 11:17-24), not supersessionism.

2TH 1:9.notes: ἀπὸ προσώπου τοῦ κυρίου echoes LXX Isa 2:10, 19, 21 (ἀπὸ προσώπου τοῦ φόβου κυρίου 'from the face of the fear of the Lord'). Same prepositional construction. The Isaiah parallel-context is theophanic-judgment (people hiding 'from the face of the Lord'), supporting the SEPARATION reading of ἀπό at 2 Thess 1:9 (vs. SOURCE reading).

JAS 1:10.notes: ὡς ἄνθος χόρτου παρελεύσεται echoes LXX Isa 40:6-7 (πᾶσα σὰρξ χόρτος, καὶ πᾶσα δόξα ἀνθρώπου ὡς ἄνθος χόρτου). The grass-and-flower-fading imagery for the brevity of human life (esp. wealth) is the OT-source James develops at 1:10-11. Same OT-text echoed at 1 Pet 1:24 (where it is more explicitly cited).

JAS 1:11.notes: In Greek Isaiah 40:7 the grass withers and the flower falls. James makes the sun with its scorching heat the cause of the withering and adds “its” to the flower. He applies the image to the rich person. Compare 1 Peter 1:24 for another use of the Isaiah passage.

JAS 1:18.notes: James calls those whom God brought forth “a kind of firstfruits,” ἀπαρχήν τινα. ดุจ expresses the comparison. Deuteronomy 26:2 describes taking from the firstfruits and verse 10 describes bringing them. The firstfruits allusion draws on the offering image. James neither uses λαβών nor gives a timetable for the renewal of creation.

JAS 2:8.notes: The citation reproduces the neighbor-love clause of Greek Leviticus 19:18. Thai จงรักเพื่อนบ้านของท่านเหมือนรักตนเอง states the command. Leviticus 19:15 also forbids partiality in judgment, a parallel to James’s setting. Jesus gives the neighbor command in Matthew 22:39 and Mark 12:31. In Luke 10:27 the legal expert gives it in answer to Jesus.

JAS 2:11.notes: This composite citation adapts the prohibitions of adultery and murder. James in SBLGNT and NA28 uses μή with aorist subjunctives. RP has future forms. Greek Exodus and Deuteronomy use οὐ with futures. In Rahlfs–Hanhart Greek, the two prohibitions are at Exodus 20:13 and 20:15, and Deuteronomy 5:17–18, adultery first. Hebrew Exodus 20:13–14 and Deuteronomy 5:17–18 put murder first. Thai อย่าล่วงประเวณี and อย่าฆ่าคน follow James’s order.

JAS 2:19.notes: The allusion draws on the confession that God is one. Deuteronomy 6:4 and Mark 12:29 use the Lord formula. Mark’s Thai says องค์พระผู้เป็นเจ้าทรงเป็นหนึ่งเดียว. James says พระเจ้าทรงเป็นองค์เดียว. Luke 18:19 uses พระเจ้าองค์เดียว when speaking of goodness. The Greek order varies in James: SBLGNT, Tregelles and NA28 have εἷς ἐστιν ὁ θεός, WH moves θεός before the verb, and RP begins with ὁ θεός. Even the demons share the stated belief and tremble.

JAS 2:21.notes: The allusion is to Genesis 22. Abraham puts Isaac on the altar, is stopped before killing him, and sacrifices a ram in his place. James describes Abraham offering his son, ถวายอิสอัค, to illustrate faith at work. Hebrews 11:17–19 recalls that offering too. Romans 4:3 explicitly quotes Genesis 15:6, the earlier declaration about Abraham’s faith.

JAS 2:23.notes: The citation of Genesis 15:6 introduces the reckoning of Abraham’s faith as righteousness. James includes δέ after ἐπίστευσεν. The following designation “friend of God,” เพื่อนของพระเจ้า, is a separate allusion. The Hebrew descriptions in Isaiah 41:8 and 2 Chronicles 20:7 express Abraham’s loving relationship with God. Greek Isaiah speaks of Abraham whom God loved, and Greek Chronicles calls him beloved. Neither has James’s exact phrase φίλος θεοῦ.

JAS 2:25.notes: Alludes to JOS 2:1-21 — Rahab’s reception of the Israelite spies (NOT angels; ἀγγέλους here = ‘messengers/spies’) at Jericho + her aiding their escape on a different route. Same event cited at HEB 11:31. The pairing of Abraham (vv.21-23) + Rahab (v.25) gives a male+female / patriarch+prostitute / Jew+Gentile-convert pair as justified-by-works examples — James’s argument deliberately spans social-categories.

1PE 1:2.notes: ῥαντισμὸν αἵματος Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ alludes to the OT-Sinai-covenant blood-sprinkling at EXO 24:8 (Moses sprinkles the people with blood and declares ‘ἰδοὺ τὸ αἷμα τῆς διαθήκης’ — ‘behold the blood of the covenant’). Peter recasts the covenant-inauguration imagery for the new-covenant-in-Christ’s-blood. Same Sinai-blood-of-covenant imagery cited at HEB 9:18-21 explicitly. Thematic dependence; not a direct quotation.

1PE 2:3.notes: Peter recalls Greek Psalm 33:9 (Psalm 34:8 in common English numbering). The psalm invites its hearers to ‘taste and see’; Peter speaks of readers who have tasted the Lord’s goodness.

1PE 2:6.notes: Direct citation of ISA 28:16 LXX (ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ ἐμβαλῶ εἰς τὰ θεμέλια Σιὼν λίθον ... ἀκρογωνιαῖον ἔντιμον — Peter opens with ἰδοὺ τίθημι, shortens the description, and retains Isaiah’s closing promise). The cornerstone-in-Zion Messianic-prophecy. Same OT-text cited at ROM 9:33 (combined with ISA 8:14) + ROM 10:11.

1PE 2:7.notes: Greek Psalm 117:22 (Psalm 118:22 in common English numbering) begins λίθον, accusative. The SBLGNT of 1 Peter begins λίθος, nominative, and retains the building and cornerstone language. The case difference does not change the Thai image. See also Matthew 21:42, Mark 12:10, Luke 20:17 and Acts 4:11.

1PE 2:8.notes: Peter draws on Isaiah 8:14. His stone and rock expressions parallel Romans 9:33. Rahlfs Isaiah uses negative comparisons and πέτρας πτώματι. Combined-with-ISA-28:16 also at ROM 9:32-33 (Pauline-application). The two-fold stumbling-stone Petrine-application: stone-of-stumbling + rock-of-offense for those-who-disobey-the-word.

1PE 2:9.notes: Composite OT-citation. γένος ἐκλεκτόν from ISA 43:20 LXX. βασίλειον ἱεράτευμα + ἔθνος ἅγιον from EXO 19:6 LXX (verbatim — the Sinai-covenant identity-formula for Israel). λαὸς εἰς περιποίησιν paraphrase of ISA 43:21 LXX (λαόν μου ὃν περιεποιησάμην) + DEU 7:6 covenant-people frame. The four-fold Israel-formula applied to the church — strongest NT-Petrine ecclesiology of church-as-new-Israel-covenant-people. Cf. Tit 2:14 περιούσιος same OT-Israel-applied-to-church frame.

1PE 2:10.notes: Compare Hosea 1:9 and 2:1, 3, 25 in Rahlfs. The reversal in Greek Hosea 2:25 corresponds to Hosea 2:23 in common English numbering. Peter brings together the descriptions ‘not a people’ and ‘God’s people’ with the reversal concerning mercy. Romans 9:25–26 also draws on Hosea, with its own wording and argument.

1PE 4:8.notes: ἀγάπη καλύπτει πλῆθος ἁμαρτιῶν echoes the sense of Hebrew Proverbs 10:12. Rahlfs has a different object (πάντας δὲ τοὺς μὴ φιλονεικοῦντας καλύπτει φιλία ‘love-covers-all-non-quarrelers’). Same OT-text echoed at JAS 5:20 (‘will-cover-multitude-of-sins’). Peter and James share the OT-proverb application — early-Christian-tradition love-covers-sins formula. Per RULES §5b: direct-speech in curly Thai-quotes preserves the citation-form.

1PE 4:14.notes: τὸ τῆς δόξης καὶ τὸ τοῦ θεοῦ πνεῦμα ἐφ’ ὑμᾶς ἀναπαύεται echoes ISA 11:2 LXX (καὶ ἀναπαύσεται ἐπ’ αὐτὸν πνεῦμα τοῦ θεοῦ — ‘the Spirit of God will rest upon him’) — Messianic-prophecy of the Spirit-resting-on-the-Branch-of-Jesse. Peter applies this Messianic-anointing to suffering-Christians (since they share-in-Christ’s-sufferings per v.13). The δόξης-addition is Petrine — the Spirit-of-glory-and-of-God doublet.

1PE 4:17.notes: ὁ καιρὸς τοῦ ἄρξασθαι τὸ κρίμα ἀπὸ τοῦ οἴκου τοῦ θεοῦ alludes to (1) EZK 9:6 LXX (the divine-judgment-vision begins-with-the-temple-elders before reaching the city); (2) JER 25:29 LXX (the cup-of-wrath that Yahweh begins-pouring-at-Jerusalem). The principle: divine-judgment begins with God’s own people first, then extends to outsiders — applied here to the persecution-as-purifying-judgment for the Christian community. Thematic dependence on the OT-judgment-begins-at-temple tradition.

1PE 4:18.notes: Close citation of PROV 11:31 LXX (εἰ ὁ μὲν δίκαιος μόλις σῴζεται, ὁ ἀσεβὴς καὶ ἁμαρτωλὸς ποῦ φανεῖται). Peter introduces the quotation with καί and omits μὲν. The a-fortiori judgment-argument: if-righteous-barely-saved, what-of-ungodly. Combines with v.17 to underscore the seriousness of the judgment-begins-at-house-of-God principle.

1PE 5:5.notes: Direct citation of PROV 3:34 LXX (κύριος ὑπερηφάνοις ἀντιτάσσεται, ταπεινοῖς δὲ δίδωσιν χάριν), with κύριος → ὁ θεός substitution. Same verse cited at JAS 4:6 with the same κύριος→θεός substitution (corpus-internal pair: shared early-Christian-tradition or independent-citation of a Christian-version of the LXX-text). Anchors the humility-imperatives of 1 PET 5:5-6: clothe-with-humility because God-gives-grace-to-humble. Thai render matches JAS 4:6 verbatim for cross-corpus key-term consistency.

1PE 5:6.notes: ‘MIGHTY HAND OF GOD’ (κραταιὰν χεῖρα τοῦ θεοῦ) is a deeply-rooted OT-formula for divine-saving-power, esp. in the Exodus-deliverance tradition: EXO 3:19 ‘ἐν χειρὶ κραταιᾷ’; EXO 6:1 LXX ‘ἐν χειρὶ κραταιᾷ ἐξαποστελεῖ αὐτούς’; EXO 13:9 ‘ἐν γὰρ χειρὶ κραταιᾷ ἐξήγαγέν σε κύριος’; EXO 32:11 ‘ἐν τῇ χειρί σου τῇ κραταιᾷ’; DEU 3:24, 9:26 (κραταιᾷ + χείρ). Peter applies the Exodus-mighty-hand to the suffering-Christian-community: humble-yourselves under-the-same-mighty-hand that delivered Israel — implying eschatological-deliverance is coming. Connects to 1 PET 1:18 ‘redemption’ (Exodus-imagery) within the letter.

1PE 5:7.notes: Verbatim verb-and-noun-match with PSA 55:22 LXX [54:23 LXX] ‘ἐπίρριψον ἐπὶ κύριον τὴν μέριμνάν σου, καὶ αὐτός σε διαθρέψει’ (cast on the Lord your-anxiety, and he himself will sustain you). Peter retains the distinctive-rare verb ἐπιρρίπτω + the noun μέριμνα, signaling deliberate-allusion. The psalm is a lament-of-the-betrayed-righteous-one (David) who casts his burden on God; Peter applies this directly to the suffering-Christian-community. The αὐτῷ μέλει περὶ ὑμῶν (‘he cares for you’) extends the Psalm’s confidence-in-divine-care.

1PE 5:8.notes: DEVIL-AS-ROARING-LION simile (λέων ὠρυόμενος ... ζητῶν τινα καταπιεῖν) draws on multiple OT lion-as-predator images: Rahlfs Psalm 21:14 (22:13 in common English numbering) ‘ὡς λέων ὁ ἁρπάζων καὶ ὠρυόμενος’ (the messianic-suffering psalm’s opponents pictured-as-roaring-tearing-lion — the same psalm Christ cited from the cross); EZK 22:25 LXX ‘ὡς λέοντες ὠρυόμενοι ἁρπάζοντες ἁρπάγματα’ (Israel’s false-prophets/princes as-roaring-lion-devouring). The verb ὠρύομαι is rare (HAPAX in NT), strengthening the OT-allusion-claim. Peter casts the devil in the role of OT-lion-predator-of-the-righteous; the suffering-Christians are the prey, like Christ in PSA 22 and Israel’s afflicted in EZK 22. Theological-payload: the cosmic-adversary echoes Christ’s passion-context.

1PE 5:9.notes: ‘RESIST HIM, STANDING-FIRM-IN-FAITH, knowing the same sufferings are being-completed for your brotherhood in the world’ — the resist-the-adversary + worldwide-suffering-of-the-faithful frame echoes JOB 1-2, where the satanic-adversary (LXX ὁ διάβολος, JOB 2:7) afflicts the steadfast-righteous-one. Peter’s ἀντίδικος + διάβολος pair (5:8) → ἀντίστητε στερεοὶ τῇ πίστει (5:9) parallels Job’s steadfastness under-adversary-affliction. JAS 4:7 ἀντίστητε δὲ τῷ διαβόλῳ shares the imperative + same OT-Job-resist-tradition (corpus-internal-link). Not a verbatim citation; thematic-tradition-stream.

2PE 1:17.notes: DIRECT CITATION of the transfiguration-voice from the Synoptic accounts (MAT 17:5 + MAR 9:7 + LUK 9:35). Peter's wording most closely matches MAT 17:5 (Ὁ υἱός μου ὁ ἀγαπητός μου οὗτός ἐστιν, εἰς ὃν ἐγὼ εὐδόκησα), though with Petrine-distinctive word-order. The transfiguration-voice itself echoes the Father's voice at Jesus's baptism (MAT 3:17 + MAR 1:11 + LUK 3:22 — Σὺ εἶ / Οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ υἱός μου ὁ ἀγαπητός), which is itself a fusion of PSA 2:7 LXX (Υἱός μου εἶ σύ — royal-coronation) + ISA 42:1 LXX (the elect-Servant ‘ὁ ἐκλεκτός μου, προσεδέξατο αὐτὸν ἡ ψυχή μου’). Peter applies this transfiguration-eyewitness to anchor his Christological-credibility against false-teachers (vv.16, 19). Same Thai-pattern as MAT 17:5.

REV 3:14.notes: Christological-titles cluster: (1) ‘the Amen’ from ISA 65:16 LXX (‘the-God-of-Amen / God-of-Truth’ אֱלֹהֵי אָמֵן — divine-self-name applied-to-Christ) — Christ-as-the-divine-Amen-confirmation. (2) ‘the originator-of-creation’ resonates with PRO 8:22-31 LXX wisdom-Christology (Wisdom-as-the-pre-existent-master-craftsman of-creation; cf. JHN 1:3 + COL 1:16-17 corpus-internal). The Trinitarian-orthodox reading: ἀρχή = source-of-creation (NOT first-created).

REV 3:21.notes: Greek Psalm 109:1 (English 110:1) invites the addressee to sit at the speaker’s right hand. Matthew 19:28 assigns the Son of Man a throne and the disciples twelve thrones. Luke 22:30 pairs a meal with seats of judgment, without numbering the thrones. Revelation compares the victor sitting with Jesus on his throne to Jesus sitting with his Father on his Father’s throne.

REV 4:5.notes: Greek Exodus 19:16 describes sounds, lightning, a dark cloud and a trumpet blast. Revelation lists flashes, sounds and thunders separately. Zechariah 4:2–6 links a lampstand with seven lamps to an oracle about God’s Spirit. Revelation calls the seven burning torches the seven spirits of God.

REV 12:6.notes: Wilderness-protection + nourishment echoes EXO 16 (Israel-fed-with-manna in-wilderness for-40-years) + 1 KGS 19 LXX (Elijah-fed-by-angels in-wilderness for-40-days). Eschatological-fulfillment of-OT-wilderness-deliverance pattern. 1260-days = 3.5-years (matches 11:3 + 12:14).

REV 13:6.notes: The beast’s speech against God recalls Daniel 7:25. The selected Greek has no conjunction before ‘those who dwell in heaven’. Thai คือ treats them as explaining God’s dwelling. A reading that takes them as a further object of the beast’s blasphemy gives a different division of the sentence.

HEB 5:3.notes: Compare Leviticus 9:7 in the inauguration of the priesthood and Leviticus 16:6, 11 on the Day of Atonement. Leviticus 16:15 turns to the people’s goat. Hebrews compares the priest’s need to offer for himself and the people.

HEB 5:4.notes: OT-allusion EXO 28:1 + NUM 16-17 LXX (Aaron-divine-call to-priesthood + Korah's-rebellion against-divine-appointment). HAPAX καθώσπερ (only NT — just-as). Divine-appointment principle.

HEB 5:5.notes: Here Psalm 2:7 names the Son. The explicit priestly declaration follows in verse 6 from Psalm 110:4 (Greek 109:4). The author brings the two sayings together as God’s testimony about the Son.

HEB 5:6.notes: DIRECT CITATION PSA 110:4 LXX [PSA 109:4] (‘σὺ ἱερεὺς εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα κατὰ τὴν τάξιν Μελχισέδεκ’). Melchizedek-priesthood = HEB 7-key. PSA 110 most-cited NT-OT-text (v.1 already at-1:13; v.4 introduces-here).

HEB 5:7.notes: NT-cross-link MAT 26:36-46 + MAR 14:32-42 + LUK 22:41-44 (Gethsemane). HAPAX ἱκετηρία (only NT — supplication). σῴζειν-ἐκ-θανάτου = resurrected-from-death (not-spared-from-dying).

HEB 5:10.notes: DIRECT CITATION REPEAT PSA 110:4 LXX (from-v.6). Closes 5:1-10 priestly-introduction. HAPAX προσαγορεύω (only NT — formal-designation). Sets-up HEB 7 Melchizedek-discussion.

HEB 4:3.notes: DIRECT CITATION REPEAT PSA 95:11 LXX [PSA 94:11] (from-3:11). Already-not-yet rest. Creation-rest pre-Sinai.

HEB 4:4.notes: Greek Genesis 2:2 supplies the seventh-day rest clause. Hebrews names God explicitly in the quoted rest clause and arranges the words about that day differently. The subject, seventh day and rest from the works remain the same.

HEB 4:5.notes: DIRECT CITATION REPEAT PSA 95:11 LXX. Twin-citation forms-argument: rest-exists + rest-still-available.

HEB 4:7.notes: DIRECT CITATION REPEAT PSA 95:7-8 LXX. PSA-95 attributed-to-David. Centuries-after-Joshua proves rest-not-given through-Joshua.

HEB 4:8.notes: OT-allusion JOS 21:44 + JOS 22:4 LXX (LORD-gave-rest-from-enemies). Ἰησοῦς-here = JOSHUA (NOT Jesus). Translation โยชูวา to-disambiguate. Joshua's-rest incomplete-because-PSA-95-promises-future.

HEB 3:2.notes: Hebrews compares Jesus’ faithfulness with Moses’ in Numbers 12:7. The Greek of Numbers has “in all my house.” Hebrews 3:2 in the selected text has “in his house,” while 3:5 does include “all.”

HEB 3:5.notes: DIRECT CITATION continuation NUM 12:7 LXX. HAPAX θεράπων (only NT — LXX-Mosaic-honor-title). Distinguishes-Moses-honor-servant from-Son. NT-cross-link JHN 5:46 (Moses-witnessed-to-Christ).

HEB 3:7.notes: Hebrews introduces the Psalm as what the Holy Spirit says. The present λέγει brings those words to the hearers now; it does not identify the human writer or the process of composition.

HEB 3:8.notes: Hebrews quotes the Greek Psalm’s terms for rebellion and testing, corresponding respectively to Meribah and Massah in the Hebrew Psalm.

HEB 3:9.notes: The Greek of Hebrews has ἐπείρασαν … ἐν δοκιμασίᾳ, one testing verb followed by a noun. Thai supplies เรา from the divine speech. The Greek Psalm uses a second finite verb, while some Hebrews witnesses also supply a first-person object.

HEB 3:10.notes: The opening “forty years” completes the preceding thought about seeing God’s works. διό then introduces God’s anger at that generation. Greek Psalm 94:10 and Hebrew Psalm 95:10 instead attach the forty years to the anger.

HEB 3:11.notes: DIRECT CITATION completion PSA 95:11 LXX [PSA 94:11]. κατάπαυσις = SABBATH-promised-land-rest. Sets-up HEB 4 chapter-long-rest-discussion. Hebrew-oath εἰ = strong-negative ‘never’.

HEB 3:15.notes: DIRECT CITATION REPEAT PSA 95:7-8 LXX. Pastoral-emphasis-by-repetition: ‘today’ open-window.

HEB 3:17.notes: Numbers 14:29, 32–33 foresees the deaths in the wilderness. Hebrews recalls them in a retrospective question about the bodies that fell there, changing the person and tense.

HEB 2:2.notes: OT-allusion DEU 33:2 LXX (‘ἐκ δεξιῶν αὐτοῦ ἄγγελοι μετ’ αὐτοῦ’) + 2nd-Temple-tradition (angels-mediated-Torah). NT-cross-link ACT 7:53 + GAL 3:19. a-fortiori-argument: lesser-mediation produced-just-punishment.

HEB 2:7.notes: This is Greek Psalm 8:6 (English Psalm 8:5). The selected Greek text of Hebrews proceeds from the crowning to the subjection of all things, omitting the Psalm’s intervening clause about the works of God’s hands.

HEB 2:8.notes: This is Greek Psalm 8:7 (English Psalm 8:6). The quotation ends with the feet. The author then explains the subjection of all things.

HEB 2:12.notes: DIRECT CITATION PSA 22:22 LXX [PSA 21:23] (suffering-Servant-Psalm). Cross-link MAT 27:46 (cross-cry from-same-Psalm). Christ-as-PSA-22-speaker leads-the-redeemed in-praise.

HEB 2:13.notes: DIRECT CITATION ISA 8:17 + ISA 8:18 LXX (Isaiah-trusts + Isaiah-and-children). Christ-fulfills-Isaiah-figure as-faithful-Servant + father-of-spiritual-children. NT-cross-link JHN 17:6 (‘the-ones-You-gave-me’).

HEB 2:16.notes: Isaiah 41:8 names the seed of Abraham and 41:9 uses οὗ ἀντελαβόμην. Hebrews draws those images together using a different verb.

HEB 2:17.notes: OT-allusion LEV 16 LXX (Day-of-Atonement vocabulary: ἱλάσκομαι). ἀρχιερεύς FIRST-introduction (corpus ACT 4:6). Theme central-to HEB 4-10. λαός corpus = ประชากร.

HEB 1:2.notes: OT-allusion PSA 2:8 LXX (Davidic-Messiah inheriting-nations) + PRO 8:22-31 LXX (Wisdom-as-creation-mediator) + WIS 9:1-2 (Word-creates). NT-cross-link JHN 1:3 + COL 1:16 (Christ-as-creator). Anarthrous-υἱός = ‘in-Son-quality’ register.

HEB 1:3.notes: Wisdom 7:26 provides the radiance image. Psalm 110:1 supplies the right-hand image; its imperative is quoted directly at Hebrews 1:13.

HEB 1:5.notes: Hebrews directly joins Psalm 2:7 and 2 Samuel 7:14. Revelation 21:7 adapts the father–son covenant pattern and uses God in the first clause.

HEB 1:6.notes: DIRECT CITATION DEU 32:43 LXX (longer-LXX/4QDeut^q reading: ‘προσκυνησάτωσαν αὐτῷ πάντες υἱοὶ θεοῦ’ — Song-of-Moses) + PSA 97:7 LXX [PSA 96:7] (‘προσκυνήσατε αὐτῷ πάντες οἱ ἄγγελοι αὐτοῦ’). Both-LXX-readings converge. Worship-of-Son = divine-Son (Christological-divinity-anchor). πρωτότοκος corpus COL 1:15.

HEB 1:7.notes: DIRECT CITATION PSA 104:4 LXX [PSA 103:4] (‘ὁ ποιῶν τοὺς ἀγγέλους αὐτοῦ πνεύματα, καὶ τοὺς λειτουργοὺς αὐτοῦ πῦρ φλέγον’). πνεῦμα-ambiguity preserved (‘spirit/wind’). Angels-MUTABLE vs Son-IMMUTABLE (contrast continues v.10-12).

HEB 1:8.notes: DIRECT CITATION PSA 45:6-7 LXX [PSA 44:7-8] (‘ὁ θρόνος σου, ὁ θεός, εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα τοῦ αἰῶνος’ — royal-wedding-Psalm Christologically-applied). HAPAX εὐθύτης (only NT). CRITICAL Christological-divinity-anchor: ὁ-θεός vocative addressed-to-Son.

HEB 1:9.notes: Psalm 45:7 (Greek Psalm 44:8) speaks to the one anointed. God is the subject of the verb of anointing.

HEB 1:10.notes: Hebrews quotes Greek Psalm 101:26, corresponding to Psalm 102:25 in common English numbering. Hebrews places σύ before “in the beginning.”

HEB 1:11.notes: Hebrews quotes Greek Psalm 101:27, corresponding to Psalm 102:26 in common English numbering. Hebrews uses διαμένεις for the addressee remaining; Rahlfs prints διαμενεῖς.

HEB 1:12.notes: Hebrews quotes Greek Psalm 101:27–28, corresponding to Psalm 102:26–27 in common English numbering. Hebrews says ἑλίξεις, “you will roll them up,” and repeats the garment comparison. Rahlfs Psalm 101:27 has ἀλλάξεις, “you will change them.”

HEB 1:13.notes: DIRECT CITATION PSA 110:1 LXX [PSA 109:1] — MOST-CITED OT-text in-NT (~25× across-NT). Cross-link with-HEB 1:3 right-hand-formula. Christ-Davidic-Lord enthroned at-Father's-right-hand.

REV 22:1.notes: DIRECT CITATION cluster: GEN 2:10 LXX (Eden-river) + EZK 47:1-12 LXX (temple-river healing-Dead-Sea) + ZEC 14:8 LXX (living-waters-from-Jerusalem) + PSA 46:4 LXX [PSA 45:5] + JOEL 3:18 LXX [JOEL 4:18]. Christological-binitarian throne (God + Lamb). Eden-temple-Jerusalem fusion.

REV 22:2.notes: Hebrew Ezekiel 47:12 describes monthly fruit and leaves for healing along the river. Greek Ezekiel 47:12 describes fresh production and uses ἀνάβασις for growth that serves health. Revelation explicitly gives fruit each month and leaves for the healing of nations. The tree of life also recalls Genesis 2:9 and 3:22–24.

REV 22:3.notes: DIRECT CITATION ZEC 14:11 LXX (‘οὐκ ἔσται ἀνάθεμα ἔτι’ — no-more-anathema) + reverses-GEN 3:17 LXX curse. HAPAX κατάθεμα (only NT, variant ἀνάθεμα). Singular-pronoun for-dual-throne (binitarian-fusion).

REV 22:4.notes: Greek Psalm 16:15 (English 17:15) uses ὀφθήσομαι, ‘I will appear before your face’. The Hebrew speaks of beholding God’s face. Revelation expressly says they will see his face, which the Thai renders จะได้เห็นพระพักตร์ของพระองค์. Compare Exodus 33:20 and Matthew 5:8. Revelation 7:3 mentions sealing the servants’ foreheads. Revelation 14:1 explicitly names the Lamb and his Father in the inscription on the foreheads. Here the servants bear his name.

REV 22:5.notes: DIRECT CITATION continuation ISA 60:19-20 LXX (LORD-eternal-light). βασιλεύσουσιν final-realization of-promise-thread (1:6 + 5:10 + 20:4-6). Eternal-reign theme-completed.

REV 22:6.notes: OT-allusion NUM 16:22 LXX + NUM 27:16 LXX (LORD-God-of-spirits-of-all-flesh). Inclusio with-1:1-3 prologue (truth-formula + ‘what-must-happen-soon’). Authenticating chain-of-revelation.

REV 22:10.notes: Theodotion’s Daniel 12:4 commands Daniel to close up the words and seal the book. Old Greek tells him to cover the commands and uses σφράγισαι for sealing the book. Daniel gives a terminus at the end. Revelation tells John not to seal the words because the time is near. A long interval in Daniel is an inference. Compare the sealed words in Daniel 12:9.

REV 22:11.notes: SBLGNT prints ῥυπαρευθήτω, from a verb used only here in that edition. NA28 prints ῥυπανθήτω, another verb for defilement. The Thai ให้ยังคงโสมมต่อไป renders this as continuing in a defiled condition. The four imperatives recall the separation of the wicked and wise in Daniel 12:10.

REV 22:12.notes: DIRECT CITATION ISA 40:10 LXX + ISA 62:11 LXX (‘ἰδοὺ ὁ μισθὸς αὐτοῦ μετ’ αὐτοῦ’ — reward-with-him) + PSA 62:12 LXX [PSA 61:13] + PRO 24:12 LXX (give-each-according-to-deeds). Judgment-by-works (REV 2:23, 20:12-13).

REV 22:13.notes: DIRECT CITATION ISA 41:4/44:6/48:12 LXX (LORD-first-and-last). Christ-self-identifies (1:8 was-Father; 21:6 ambiguous; 22:13 Christ-explicit) — Christological-divinity climactic.

REV 22:14.notes: OT-allusion ZEC 3:3-5 LXX (Joshua-priestly-garments cleansed). Cross-link REV 7:14 (washed-in-blood-of-Lamb). 7th-of-7-Revelation-beatitudes (final). Two-fold-privilege: tree + city-entry.

REV 22:15.notes: Greek Deuteronomy 23:19 (English 23:18) refers to something exchanged for a dog and leaves the dog’s identity unexplained. Reading it as a cult prostitute is an interpretation. In Revelation สุนัข retains the image. The list does not identify these dogs as a particular class of prostitute. Compare the hostile dogs of Psalm 22 and the use of dogs in Philippians 3:2. Revelation 21:8 uses φαρμάκοις and 22:15 uses φάρμακοι, dative and nominative plurals of the same personal noun. Thai uses ผู้ใช้เวทมนตร์ at both places. SBLGNT 9:21 prints φαρμάκων, while 18:23 has φαρμακείᾳ for sorcery.

REV 22:16.notes: DIRECT CITATION ISA 11:1, 10 LXX (Davidic-Messianic-Root) + NUM 24:17 LXX (Balaam's-star-from-Jacob). Cross-link REV 5:5 (Root-of-David) + 2:28 (morning-star promise) + 2 PE 1:19. Christological-paradox Root-AND-Offspring.

REV 22:17.notes: DIRECT CITATION continuation ISA 55:1 LXX (water-without-price). NT-cross-link JHN 4:14, 7:37-38. Triple-‘come’ chiasm: Spirit+Bride → hearer → thirsty.

REV 22:18.notes: DIRECT CITATION DEU 4:2 LXX + DEU 12:32 LXX [DEU 13:1] (‘οὐ προσθήσετε πρὸς τὸ ῥῆμα ... καὶ οὐκ ἀφελεῖτε’ — do-not-add-or-subtract-from-Torah-Word). Canonical-protective-formula. Inviolability-of-prophetic-Word.

REV 22:19.notes: SBLGNT and NA28 print ξύλου, “tree,” here. A Latin tradition reads libro, “book,” in place of ligno, “tree.” Erasmus printed the Greek book reading after supplying the missing ending of his Greek copy from Latin. A Latin reading and its Greek rendering are distinct witnesses in this history. The Thai ต้นไม้แห่งชีวิต follows the tree reading, which also appears in 22:2 and 22:14. The warning about taking away recalls Deuteronomy 4:2 and 12:32.

REV 22:20.notes: NT-cross-link 1 COR 16:22 ‘μαραναθα’ Aramaic-equivalent (‘our-Lord-come’). Third-‘I-come-soon’ refrain (v.7, 12, 20). Bride-Christ liturgical-dialogue.

REV 21:1.notes: DIRECT CITATION ISA 65:17 LXX (‘ἔσται γὰρ ὁ οὐρανὸς καινὸς καὶ ἡ γῆ καινή’) + ISA 66:22 LXX. NT-cross-link 2 PE 3:13. Sea-no-more = chaos/rebellion-source removed (GEN 1:2 + REV 13:1 + 17:15).

REV 21:2.notes: DIRECT CITATION ISA 52:1 LXX (holy-city-Jerusalem) + ISA 65:18-19 LXX + ISA 61:10 LXX (bride-adorned). EZK 40-48 LXX visionary-Jerusalem. City-AS-Bride identification (made-explicit v.9-10). NT-cross-link EPH 5:25-27.

REV 21:3.notes: DIRECT CITATION covenant-formula: LEV 26:11-12 LXX + EZK 37:27 LXX + JER 31:33 LXX [JER 38:33] (new-covenant). NT-cross-link JHN 1:14 (Logos-tabernacled). Plural λαοί universalizes covenant-people.

REV 21:4.notes: DIRECT CITATION ISA 25:8 LXX (‘ἀφεῖλεν ὁ θεὸς πᾶν δάκρυον ἀπὸ παντὸς προσώπου’) + ISA 35:10 LXX (‘ἀπέδρα ὀδύνη καὶ λύπη καὶ στεναγμός’). Echo REV 7:17. Triple-negation reverses-Eden-curse (GEN 3:16-19 LXX).

REV 21:5.notes: DIRECT CITATION ISA 43:19 LXX (‘ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ ποιῶ καινά’ — behold-I-do-new-things). Present-tense recreation-in-progress. καινός qualitative-new.

REV 21:6.notes: The speaker continues the speech of the one seated on the throne in 21:5. Greek Isaiah 41:4 speaks of God as first and of the things to come, 44:6 as first and after these things, and 48:12 as first and forever. The Hebrew texts express God’s priority and enduring sovereignty with first-and-last language. Here the titles are Alpha and Omega, beginning and end. Compare 1:8 and 22:13. The gift of water recalls Isaiah 55:1 and the living-water sayings in John 4:14 and 7:37–38.

REV 21:7.notes: DIRECT CITATION 2 SAM 7:14 LXX [2 KGS 7:14] (Davidic-covenant Solomon-as-God's-son) + PSA 89:26-27 LXX [PSA 88:27-28] + ZEC 8:8 LXX. Davidic-Messianic-promise universalized to-overcomers. 7-Letters νικάω-thread fulfilled.

REV 21:10.notes: In Greek Ezekiel 40:1–2 the Lord’s hand brings the prophet in a vision and sets him on a high mountain. He sees a structure like a city. In verse 4 the man explains that the prophet is there to be shown these things. In Revelation the angel carries John in the Spirit and shows him the city descending.

REV 21:11.notes: The Greek names link the vision to 4:3. For ἴασπις the Thai there has หินยัสเปอร์, while 21:11, 18 and 19 have พลอยหยก. For σάρδιον, 4:3 has คาร์เนเลียน and 21:20 has พลอยทับทิม. These Thai alternatives do not identify the same modern minerals. Ancient gemstone names do not always establish a precise modern mineral species. The glory of the city recalls Isaiah 60:1–2 and Ezekiel 43:2–5.

REV 21:12.notes: DIRECT CITATION EZK 48:30-35 LXX (twelve-gates-by-tribes-of-Israel). 12+12=24 = elders (REV 4:4). OT/NT-Israel-Apostles integrated-architecture.

REV 21:15.notes: DIRECT CITATION EZK 40:3-5 LXX (measuring-rod) + ZEC 2:1-5 LXX (measure-Jerusalem). κάλαμος corpus REV 11:1. Eternal-city's-divine-precision.

REV 21:16.notes: DIRECT CITATION 1 KGS 6:20 LXX [3 KGS 6:20 LXX] (Holy-of-Holies cube — 20-cubits each-dimension). HAPAX τετράγωνος (only NT — square/foursquare). City = cosmic-Holy-of-Holies. 12,000 stadia symbolic-perfect-totality.

REV 21:19.notes: Greek Exodus 28:17–20 names twelve stones in a sequence that only partly overlaps with these foundations. Verse 21 adds the tribal names engraved on the stones. Greek Isaiah 54:11 describes foundations of a precious blue stone. A priestly association with the city is possible. Revelation names the apostles on the foundations in 21:14.

REV 21:20.notes: Greek Exodus 28:17–20 names twelve stones in a sequence that only partly overlaps with these foundations. Verse 21 adds the tribal names engraved on the stones. Greek Isaiah 54:11 describes foundations of a precious blue stone. A priestly association with the city is possible. Revelation names the apostles on the foundations in 21:14.

REV 21:22.notes: INVERSE-allusion EZK 40-48 LXX (eschatological-temple). God+Lamb = singular-temple (binitarian). City-as-Holy-of-Holies-cube (v.16) eliminates-need for-distinct-sanctuary.

REV 21:23.notes: DIRECT CITATION ISA 60:19-20 LXX (sun-moon-not-needed, LORD-eternal-light). Lamb-as-lamp Christological-mediation. Light-source theological-not-physical.

REV 21:24.notes: Greek Isaiah 60:5 uses μεταβαλεῖ for the wealth of sea, nations and peoples turning to Zion. Verse 6 brings in the camels. In 60:11 the wealth or might of nations comes in and their kings are led. Revelation 21:24 has the nations walk in the city’s light and the kings themselves bring their glory into it. Compare Isaiah 60:3.

REV 21:25.notes: DIRECT CITATION ISA 60:11 LXX (gates-open-continuously). Security-by-divine-presence, not-by-fortress-walls. No-night = no-fear, no-shutting.

REV 21:26.notes: DIRECT CITATION continuation ISA 60:5-9, 11 LXX (nations-bring-glory-and-tribute). Cultural-treasures of-nations preserved-in-eternal-city.

REV 21:27.notes: DIRECT CITATION ISA 52:1 LXX (no-uncircumcised-or-unclean enter-Jerusalem). Five earlier passages mention the book of life (3:5, 13:8, 17:8, 20:12 and 20:15). This verse brings the total to six in the selected Greek. The Lamb is expressly named in the designation at 13:8 and 21:27. Holy-city-purity preserved by-Lamb's-redemption-list.

REV 20:3.notes: In Old Greek Daniel 6:18 the king’s ring seals the stone over the lions’ den. The corresponding English verse is commonly numbered 6:17. Revelation instead portrays the angel securing the abyss to restrain the deceiver for a limited time.

REV 20:4.notes: DIRECT CITATION of DAN 7:9-10, 22, 26 LXX (‘ἐθεώρουν ἕως ὅτου θρόνοι ἐτέθησαν ... κριτήριον ἐκάθισεν’). HAPAX πελεκίζω (only NT — behead-with-axe). Cross-link REV 6:9 souls-under-altar + MAT 19:28/LUK 22:30 (apostles-judging-on-thrones).

REV 20:8.notes: DIRECT CITATION EZK 38-39 LXX (Gog-of-the-land-of-Magog from-Rosh-Meshech-Tubal — final-eschatological-enemy). TWO HAPAX (Γώγ + Μαγώγ — proper-nouns). REV universalizes-from-northern to-‘four-corners’. Greek Genesis 32:13 (English 32:12) is Jacob recalling the promise that his descendants will be like the sand of the sea. In Genesis 22:17 God promises Abraham offspring like sand by the shore of the sea. Revelation uses the sand comparison for the number of the hostile nations. An inversion of the promise is a possible interpretation.

REV 20:9.notes: DIRECT CITATION cluster: 2 KGS 1:10-12 LXX [4 KGS 1:10-12 LXX] (Elijah-fire-from-heaven against-Ahaziah's-50s) + EZK 38:22 LXX (Gog-fire-and-brimstone-rain) + GEN 19:24 LXX (Sodom-fire-from-heaven). HAPAX κυκλεύω (only NT). Greek Psalm 77:68 (Hebrew and English 78:68) names τὸ ὄρος τὸ Σιων ὃ ἠγάπησεν, Mount Zion which he loved. Revelation names the beloved city, นครอันเป็นที่รัก, without giving its name. Zion or Jerusalem is an interpretation suggested by the Psalm.

REV 20:11.notes: In Greek Isaiah 51:6 the heavens are described with ἐστερεώθη, ‘was made firm’, in a comparison with smoke. The Hebrew-based Thai of Isaiah describes the heavens vanishing like smoke. Theodotion’s Daniel 2:35 says no place was found for the dispersed material of the statue. Revelation applies the no-place expression to earth and sky fleeing the one on the throne.

REV 20:12.notes: DIRECT CITATION DAN 7:10 LXX (‘κριτήριον ἐκάθισεν, καὶ βίβλοι ἠνεῴχθησαν’ — court-sat, books-opened). Two-book-categories: deeds-books + book-of-life. Judgment-by-deeds corpus REV 2:23, 22:12. βίβλος-τῆς-ζωῆς corpus.

REV 20:13.notes: Old Greek Daniel 12:2 describes many sleepers in the broad expanse of the earth rising (ἀναστήσονται). Theodotion speaks of sleepers in the dust of the earth awakening. Neither describes the sea or Hades giving up the dead. Revelation names the sea, Death and Hades to convey the scope of the judgment. Compare Isaiah 26:19 for the dead rising.

REV 20:14.notes: In Greek Isaiah 25:8, death is the subject of κατέπιεν: death swallowed, having prevailed. The Hebrew describes God swallowing death forever. In 1 Corinthians 15:54 death is swallowed up, and 15:26 calls death the last enemy. Revelation pictures Death and Hades being thrown into the lake of fire.

REV 19:1.notes: OT-allusion LXX-Psalter Hallel (PSA 104-106 LXX, PSA 110-118 LXX Hallel-Egyptian, PSA 134-150 LXX Final-Hallel). Heavenly-Hallelujah-chorus opens-celebration after-Babylon-fall. Triadic-attribution corpus-pattern (cf. 7:10, 12:10).

REV 19:2.notes: Greek Deuteronomy 32:43 speaks of God avenging the blood of his sons, using ἐκδικᾶται. Greek 4 Kingdoms 9:7 (2 Kings 9:7) mentions the blood of God’s servants and its avenging at the hand of Jezebel. Revelation speaks of God avenging his servants’ blood at the hand of the great prostitute. The true and just judgments also recall Deuteronomy 32:4 and Revelation 16:7.

REV 19:3.notes: DIRECT CITATION ISA 34:10 LXX (Edom-judgment ‘smoke-shall-ascend-forever’). Same-allusion as-14:11; now-Babylon-system. Eternal-irrevocability of-judgment.

REV 19:4.notes: Revelation has Ἀμήν, Ἁλληλουϊά, reflected in อาเมน and ฮาเลลูยา. Greek Psalm 105:48 ends γένοιτο γένοιτο. Hebrew Psalm 106:48 closes with amen and a call to praise the Lord. Compare the closing doxologies of several collections within the Psalter.

REV 19:5.notes: DIRECT CITATION of PSA 135:1 LXX [PSA 134:1] (‘αἰνεῖτε ... δοῦλοι κύριον’) + PSA 115:13 LXX [PSA 113:21] (‘τοὺς φοβουμένους τὸν κύριον, τοὺς μικροὺς μετὰ τῶν μεγάλων’). Hallel-Psalter combine.

REV 19:6.notes: DIRECT CITATION enthronement-Psalter cluster: PSA 93:1 LXX [PSA 92:1] / PSA 96:10 LXX [PSA 95:10] / PSA 97:1 LXX / PSA 99:1 LXX (‘ΚΥΡΙΟΣ-ΕΒΑΣΙΛΕΥΣΕΝ’ enthronement-cry). Now-actualized at-end-of-Babylon-judgment.

REV 19:7.notes: Hebrew Isaiah 54:5 calls the Maker the woman’s husband. Greek Isaiah 54:5 speaks of her maker and redeemer. The image of a wife and her restoration is present in the wider Greek passage, Isaiah 54:4–6. Revelation depicts the wedding of the Lamb and his bride. Other marriage imagery appears in Isaiah 62:5, Hosea 1–3, Jeremiah 2–3 and Ezekiel 16.

REV 19:9.notes: OT-allusion ISA 25:6-9 LXX (eschatological-feast-on-Mount-Zion ‘ποιήσει κύριος Σαβαωθ πᾶσι τοῖς ἔθνεσιν’) + MAT 22:1-14/LUK 14:15-24 NT-cross-link (wedding-banquet-parables). 4th-of-7-Revelation-beatitudes.

REV 19:11.notes: DIRECT CITATION ISA 11:4-5 LXX (Davidic-Messiah ‘κρινεῖ ταπεινῷ κρίσιν ... ἔσται δικαιοσύνῃ ἐζωσμένος’ — judges-with-righteousness, righteousness-as-belt). Christ-rider self-revelation continues 3:14 (Laodicea ‘Faithful-and-True’ name).

REV 19:12.notes: OT-allusion DAN 10:6 LXX (‘ὀφθαλμοὶ αὐτοῦ ὡσεὶ λαμπάδες πυρός’) + REV 1:14, 2:18 self-revelation echoes. Philippians 2:9 describes an exalted name. The rider’s name being known to him alone is stated in Revelation.

REV 19:13.notes: Hebrew Isaiah 63:3 speaks of treading alone and of blood spattering the warrior’s garments. Greek Isaiah 63:2 compares the red clothing to that of someone coming from a trodden winepress. Verse 3 brings blood down to the earth. Revelation 19:13 describes a robe marked with blood and leaves unstated whose blood it is. The rider bears the name พระวาทะของพระเจ้า.

REV 19:15.notes: Revelation 19:15 depicts the rider treading God’s winepress. Greek Isaiah 63:2 supplies the winepress comparison, while the warrior treading alone is explicit in Hebrew Isaiah 63:3. The mouth and sword recall Isaiah 11:4 and 49:2. The iron rod recalls Greek Psalm 2:9.

REV 19:16.notes: DIRECT CITATION DEU 10:17 LXX (‘ὁ θεὸς θεῶν καὶ κύριος τῶν κυρίων’) + DAN 4:37 LXX (Nebuchadnezzar's-confession). HAPAX μηρός (only NT — thigh). Cross-link REV 17:14 (chiastic-order). NT-cross-link 1 TIM 6:15.

REV 19:17.notes: In Greek Ezekiel 39:17 the prophet summons birds and wild beasts to a great sacrifice. In Revelation an angel calls the flying birds to God’s great supper. The allusion to Ezekiel also contrasts with the wedding supper in verse 9.

REV 19:18.notes: Greek Ezekiel 39:18 names the flesh of mighty men (κρέα γιγάντων) and the blood of rulers. Verse 20 adds horse and rider. Revelation repeats σάρκας for kings, commanders, mighty men, horses and riders, and includes all ranks. An association with the merchants of chapter 18 is interpretive. The list here does not name them.

REV 19:19.notes: OT-allusion PSA 2:1-2 LXX (kings-take-counsel against-LORD-and-Anointed) + ZEC 14:2-3 LXX (gathering-against-Jerusalem). Continuation-of-Armageddon mobilization (16:14-16).

REV 19:20.notes: OT-allusion DAN 7:11 LXX (‘ἐδόθη εἰς καῦσιν πυρός’ — fourth-Beast-burned-with-fire) + GEN 19:24 LXX (Sodom-Gomorrah-fire-and-brimstone) + ISA 30:33 LXX (Topheth-fire-and-brimstone). FIRST-NT λίμνη-τοῦ-πυρός (lake-of-fire) — recurring-corpus.

REV 19:21.notes: DIRECT CITATION EZK 39:17-20 LXX (bird-feast realized) + ISA 11:4 LXX fulfilled (Word-of-mouth strikes). Final-eschatological-battle resolved-without-narrated-combat.

REV 18:1.notes: OT-allusion EZK 43:2 LXX (‘ἡ γῆ ἐξέλαμπεν ὡς φέγγος ἀπὸ τῆς δόξης’ — earth-shone-with-radiance from-glory). Angel-with-derivative-glory introduces-Babylon-fall.

REV 18:2.notes: Revelation repeats ἔπεσεν, an aorist, as in 14:8. Hebrew Isaiah 21:9 also repeats its verb. Greek Isaiah 21:9 has one perfect πέπτωκεν and mentions the images (ἀγάλματα). Greek Jeremiah 28:8 (Hebrew and English 51:8) has one aorist. The repeated announcement alludes to these prophecies. The desolate city’s inhabitants recall Isaiah 13:21–22, 34:11–15 and the descriptions of Babylon in Jeremiah 50–51.

REV 18:3.notes: DIRECT CITATION continuation of-JER 51:7 LXX (Babylon-cup making-nations-drunk-and-mad). HAPAX στρῆνος (only NT — sensual-luxury). Three-fold-clientele setup: nations + kings + merchants.

REV 18:4.notes: Hebrew Jeremiah 51:45 calls God’s people out of Babylon. The corresponding line is absent from Greek Jeremiah 28 after verse 44. Greek Isaiah 52:11 uses a plural command to depart from her midst. Greek Isaiah 48:20 uses a singular command to leave Babylon. Revelation addresses the people as a group and explains why they should leave. The call also alludes to the flight from Babylon in Hebrew Jeremiah 50:8 (Greek 27:8).

REV 18:5.notes: DIRECT CITATION of JER 51:9 LXX [JER 28:9 LXX] (‘ἤγγισεν εἰς οὐρανὸν τὸ κρίμα αὐτῆς’ — judgment-reaches-heaven) + GEN 11:4 LXX (Babel-tower ‘εἰς οὐρανόν’) cluster. Cross-link REV 16:19 (Babylon-remembered-before-God).

REV 18:6.notes: Greek Jeremiah 16:18 has ἀνταποδώσω διπλᾶς τὰς ἀδικίας, the Lord’s promise of double repayment. Revelation gives an imperative of διπλόω with a neuter plural expression and pictures Babylon’s own cup being mixed for her. The shared theme is repayment in kind. Compare Hebrew Jeremiah 50:29 and Isaiah 40:2.

REV 18:7.notes: Greek Isaiah 47:7–8 presents Babylon expecting lasting rulership, refusing to sit as a widow and expecting never to know loss of children. Revelation adapts the boast. Babylon calls herself a queen and says she will never see grief. Death, grief and famine follow in 18:8.

REV 18:8.notes: DIRECT CITATION of ISA 47:9 LXX (one-day-double-plague rebuts-‘I-am-not-a-widow’) + EZK 14:21 LXX (four-fold-judgment cluster) + JER 50:34 LXX [JER 27:34] (mighty-Redeemer).

REV 18:9.notes: DIRECT CITATION EZK 26-27 LXX Tyre-lament — major-OT-archetype. Triple-mourner-section (kings/merchants/mariners) opens. EZK 26:16-18 LXX kings-of-coastlands lament-from-afar at-Tyre's-fall.

REV 18:10.notes: In Greek Ezekiel 26:16 the maritime rulers descend from their thrones and sit on the ground. The kings in Revelation stand at a distance out of fear. Their lament alludes to the mourning for Tyre. The merchants and seafarers also keep their distance in verses 15 and 17.

REV 18:11.notes: DIRECT CITATION EZK 27 LXX (Tyre-merchant-lament — extensive-tribe-goods-list directly-paralleled in-REV 18:12-13). Second-mourner-section.

REV 18:12.notes: DIRECT CITATION EZK 27:12-25 LXX (Tyre-trade-tribes-and-goods detailed-list). FIVE HAPAX in-this-verse: σιρικός (silk), θύϊνος (citron-wood), ἐλεφάντινος (ivory), σίδηρος (iron), μάρμαρος (marble) — all only-NT-occurrences.

REV 18:13.notes: DIRECT CITATION EZK 27:13 LXX (‘ψυχάς ἀνθρώπων’ — Tyre-trades-souls-of-men + bronze-vessels). FOUR HAPAX in-this-verse: κιννάμωμον (cinnamon), ἄμωμον (amomum), σεμίδαλις (fine-flour), ῥεδή (carriage Latin-loan). Climactic ‘souls-of-men’ = human-trafficking indictment.

REV 18:17.notes: DIRECT CITATION EZK 27:27-29 LXX (Tyre-mariners-shipmasters-pilots come-down-from-ships). Third-mourner-section (maritime). Shipping-empire imagery historical-Rome's-grain-lanes.

REV 18:18.notes: Hebrew Ezekiel 27:32 asks who is like Tyre. Rahlfs–Hanhart Greek Ezekiel 27:32 introduces the lament and then proceeds to verse 33 without that question. Revelation makes the seafarers explicitly ask what city is like the great city.

REV 18:19.notes: In Greek Ezekiel 27:30 the mourners put earth on their heads, using ἐπιθήσουσιν, γῆν and the singular κεφαλήν. Revelation uses the verb for throwing, the word for dust, and the plural for heads. The allusion preserves the public gesture of grief.

REV 18:20.notes: Hebrew Jeremiah 51:48 pictures heaven and earth rejoicing over Babylon. Its corresponding line is absent from Rahlfs–Hanhart Greek Jeremiah 28. Greek Deuteronomy 32:43 calls on the heavens to rejoice. Revelation addresses heaven and three human groups, the saints, apostles and prophets.

REV 18:21.notes: In Greek Jeremiah 28:63–64 (Hebrew and common English 51:63–64) Seraiah is to tie a stone to the scroll, ἐπιδήσεις ἐπ᾿ αὐτὸ λίθον, and throw it into the Euphrates. In Revelation an angel casts a stone like a great millstone into the sea. Both acts depict Babylon’s downfall.

REV 18:22.notes: Hebrew Jeremiah 25:10 includes the sound of millstones, lamplight and bridal voices. Greek Jeremiah 25:10 includes ὀσμὴν μύρου, the scent of perfume, with lamplight and the voices of bridegroom and bride. Revelation 18:22 ends with the millstone. Verse 23 continues with the lamp and the wedding voices. The loss of music also recalls Ezekiel 26:13.

REV 18:23.notes: Hebrew Jeremiah 25:10 includes the sound of millstones, lamplight and bridal voices. Greek Jeremiah 25:10 includes ὀσμὴν μύρου, the scent of perfume, with lamplight and the voices of bridegroom and bride. Revelation 18:22 ends with the millstone. Verse 23 continues with the lamp and the wedding voices. The reference to sorcery recalls Nahum 3:4 and Isaiah 47:9–12.

REV 18:24.notes: Greek Jeremiah 28:49 (Hebrew and English 51:49) says that the slain of all the earth will fall in Babylon. Revelation says the blood of prophets, saints and all who were slain on earth was found in the city. The nations-wide scope of the deaths links the two passages.

REV 17:1.notes: The many waters recall Greek Jeremiah 28:13 (Hebrew and English 51:13). Its plural participle κατασκηνοῦντας refers to people dwelling by many waters. Revelation depicts one woman seated on many waters. Revelation 17:15 identifies the waters as peoples, multitudes, nations and languages.

REV 17:2.notes: Hebrew Isaiah 23:17 describes Tyre engaging in prostitution with the kingdoms of the earth. Greek Isaiah uses the prostitute image and then speaks of commerce with the kingdoms. Greek Jeremiah 28:7 (Hebrew and English 51:7) describes Babylon’s cup making the earth drunk. Revelation joins sexual unfaithfulness and intoxication. Compare Nineveh in Nahum 3:4.

REV 17:4.notes: DIRECT CITATION of JER 51:7 LXX (‘ποτήριον χρυσοῦν Βαβυλὼν ἐν χειρὶ κυρίου’ — golden-cup-Babylon-in-LORD's-hand making-earth-drunk-and-mad). Imperial-luxury cluster (purple/scarlet/gold/precious-stones/pearls) matches REV 18 lament + INVERSE-of bride-of-Lamb (19:8) + INVERSE-of New-Jerusalem (21:18-21 same-materials, different-valuation).

REV 17:5.notes: OT-allusion DAN 9:27 LXX + DAN 12:11 LXX βδέλυγμα-τῆς-ἐρημώσεως (‘abomination-of-desolation’) cluster echo. ‘Mother-of-prostitutes’ = system-archetype. Forehead-name INVERSE: 7:3+14:1 saints-with-divine-name vs 13:16-17 Beast-marked vs here-Babylon-named.

REV 17:6.notes: OT-allusion ISA 49:26 LXX (oppressors-drink-own-blood) + lex-talionis cross-link REV 16:6 (blood-of-saints-and-prophets given-to-drink). Vampire-prostitute imagery: drunk-on-martyr-blood (Antipas REV 2:13, two-witnesses REV 11:3-12).

REV 17:8.notes: OT-allusion DAN 7:7+21 LXX fourth-Beast pattern. Beast PARODY-of divine-eternal-formula (REV 1:4, 1:8, 4:8 was/is/coming). Beast-from-ἄβυσσος (corpus REV 9, 11). Verbal-echo of-13:8 book-of-life from-foundation-of-world.

REV 17:12.notes: DIRECT CITATION of DAN 7:24 LXX (‘τὰ δέκα κέρατα δέκα βασιλεῖς ἀναστήσονται’ — ten-horns = ten-kings-will-rise). Ten-horns of-Daniel's-fourth-Beast applied-to final-imperial-system. ‘One-hour’ = brief-period idiom (REV 18:10/17/19).

REV 17:14.notes: Old Greek Daniel 4:37 calls God king of kings, God of gods and lord of lords. Theodotion 4:37 calls him king of heaven, and 4:34 praises his enduring rule. Deuteronomy 10:17 includes lord of lords. Revelation 17:14 calls the Lamb lord of lords and then king of kings. The two titles appear in reverse order in 19:16. Compare 1 Timothy 6:15.

REV 17:16.notes: The former lovers and the stripping recall Ezekiel 16:37–41 and 23:25–29. In Greek Ezekiel 23:25 fire consumes the survivors. Greek Psalm 26:2 (English 27:2) describes enemies approaching to eat the speaker’s flesh. In Revelation the horns and the beast eat the woman’s flesh and burn her with fire.

REV 17:17.notes: The passage alludes to prophetic descriptions of God’s use of rulers. In Hebrew Jeremiah 25:9 God calls Nebuchadnezzar “my servant.” Greek Jeremiah 25:9 lacks that designation. The shared point is that God can use rulers for his purpose. Revelation itself says God puts it into their hearts to give their kingdom to the beast. Compare Acts 4:27–28. In Revelation 17:17 τελεσθήσονται is future passive, “will be fulfilled.” Revelation 10:7 and 15:1 have ἐτελέσθη, a form of the same verb. Revelation 16:17 expresses completion with Γέγονεν, from γίνομαι.

REV 16:2.notes: DIRECT CITATION of EXO 9:9-11 LXX sixth-Egyptian-plague (soot-becomes-boils ἕλκη on-Egyptians-and-magicians). First-bowl recapitulates-EXO-plague-of-boils. Distinguishing-judgment: only-Beast-worshipers afflicted (INVERSE EZK 9:4-6 marked-spared).

REV 16:3.notes: DIRECT CITATION of EXO 7:17-21 LXX first-Egyptian-plague (Nile-to-blood + fish-died). Bowls-intensify-trumpets pattern: REV 8:8-9 was-third-of-sea-blood, here all-sea-blood + every-living-thing-died.

REV 16:4.notes: DIRECT CITATION continuation of-EXO 7:19 LXX (‘all-river-waters, canals, marshes, all-standing-water’ become-blood). Third-bowl extends-Egyptian-plague to-all-freshwater-sources.

REV 16:5.notes: OT-allusion DEU 32:4 LXX continuation (‘δίκαιος-καὶ-ὅσιος-κύριος’) — angel-of-waters doxology echoes 15:3-4 Song-of-Moses-and-the-Lamb. Eternal-formula truncated (no-‘coming’) because-judgment-has-arrived.

REV 16:6.notes: Wisdom 11:6–8 recalls the bloodied river, the decree to kill infants and the abundant water given to the people in the wilderness. Isaiah 49:26 describes oppressors drinking their own blood. Revelation 16:6 explicitly says God gives the persecutors blood to drink because they shed the blood of saints and prophets. The allusion draws on retribution and water turned to blood.

REV 16:7.notes: OT-allusion DEU 32:4 LXX continuation (true-and-just-judgments) + PSA 19:9 LXX [PSA 18:10 LXX] (κρίματα-κυρίου-ἀληθινά). Altar-personified continues-from-REV 6:9 + 8:3-5. Chiastic-doxology with-15:3 (δίκαιαι-καὶ-ἀληθιναί ↔ ἀληθιναὶ-καὶ-δίκαιαι).

REV 16:8.notes: INVERSE-allusion ISA 49:10 LXX + REV 7:16 (‘sun-shall-not-strike-them, no-scorching-καῦμα’ — applied-to-redeemed). Bowl-victims experience the-OPPOSITE: sun-becomes-instrument-of-wrath.

REV 16:10.notes: DIRECT CITATION of EXO 10:21-23 LXX ninth-Egyptian-plague (‘ψηλαφητὸν σκότος’ — palpable-darkness three-days, no-one-rose-from-place) + Day-of-the-LORD darkness-cluster: ISA 8:21-22, JOEL 2:2, ZEP 1:15 LXX. Beast's-throne directly-targeted (symbolic-imperial-dethronement). HAPAX μασάομαι in-this-verse (only NT).

REV 16:11.notes: OT-allusion: θεός-τοῦ-οὐρανοῦ = LXX-Aramaic-Persian-period title (DAN 2:18-19, EZRA 1:2 LXX, EZRA 5:11 LXX). Even-foreign-title-acknowledgment doesn't-prevent-blasphemy.

REV 16:12.notes: Hebrew Jeremiah 50:38 speaks of Babylon’s waters drying up. That verse is absent from Greek Jeremiah 27. Greek Jeremiah 28:36 (Hebrew and English 51:36) speaks of drying up Babylon’s spring. Revelation names the Euphrates as the river that dries up so that rulers arriving from the east can cross. Compare the passages about crossings in Isaiah 11:15–16 and Zechariah 10:11. In Greek Isaiah 11:15 the Lord strikes the river into seven valleys so that people can cross. Greek Zechariah 10:11 describes the drying of the depths of rivers. The identification with the Euphrates is an inference in these comparisons. Revelation names the Euphrates explicitly.

REV 16:13.notes: The frogs in Greek Exodus 7:26–8:11 (English 8:1–15) come up from the waters after Aaron extends his hand, and the magicians also bring up frogs. Revelation describes three unclean spirits that look like frogs, emerging from the mouths of the dragon, the beast and the false prophet. The plague is a thematic allusion.

REV 16:14.notes: DIRECT CITATION of ‘great-Day-of-the-LORD’ formula = JOEL 2:11 LXX + JOEL 2:31 LXX [JOEL 3:4 LXX] + JOEL 3:14 LXX [JOEL 4:14 LXX] + ZEP 1:14 LXX (‘ἡμέρα κυρίου ἡ μεγάλη’) + ZEC 14:2-3 LXX (LORD-gathers-nations against-Jerusalem). Final-eschatological-battle-mobilization.

REV 16:15.notes: OT-allusion GEN 3:7 LXX nakedness-shame post-fall (extended ISA 47:3, EZK 16:37). 3rd-of-7-Revelation-beatitudes. Synoptic-parallel cluster (thief-coming): MAT 24:43, LUK 12:39, 1 THE 5:2-4, 2 PE 3:10, REV 3:3.

REV 16:16.notes: OT-allusion: Ἁρμαγεδών HAPAX (only NT) = Hebrew הר מגדו (har-Megiddo, ‘Mountain-of-Megiddo’). Megiddo-as-OT-battlefield: JDG 5:19 LXX (Deborah-Sisera), 2 KGS 23:29 LXX [4 KGS 23:29 LXX] (Josiah-Pharaoh-Necho), 2 CHR 35:22, ZEC 12:11 LXX (mourning-of-Hadad-Rimmon). Symbolic-final-battlefield.

REV 16:18.notes: Theodotion’s Daniel 12:1 speaks of an unprecedented time of distress and uses οἵα οὐ γέγονεν. Old Greek speaks of a day of distress and gives its point of comparison differently. Revelation applies comparable language to an earthquake without precedent since humanity came to be on the earth. The storm imagery recalls Sinai in Exodus 19:16. The description of unprecedented hail in Exodus 9:18, 24 offers another parallel.

REV 16:19.notes: In Ezekiel 5:1–2 the prophet divides his hair in a sign about Jerusalem. The Hebrew uses thirds and the Greek describes fourths. In Revelation the great city itself splits into three parts. Zechariah 14:4 describes a mountain splitting. Babylon receives the cup of the wine of God’s fierce wrath. The Thai พระพิโรธอันเกรี้ยวกราด conveys the linked anger terms. The cup recalls Greek Jeremiah 32:15–16 (Hebrew and English 25:15–16) and Isaiah 51:17, 22–23.

REV 16:20.notes: DIRECT CITATION cluster: ISA 40:4 LXX (mountains-leveled), ISA 54:10 LXX (mountains-may-depart), JER 4:23-26 LXX (earth-formless), NAH 1:5 LXX (mountains-quake at-LORD's-presence). Cross-link REV 6:14 (sixth-seal mountains-and-islands-moved). Bowls-intensify-seals/trumpets pattern.

REV 16:21.notes: DIRECT CITATION of EXO 9:23-24 LXX seventh-Egyptian-plague (hail-mixed-with-fire, unique-since-Egypt-began) + JOS 10:11 LXX (LORD-cast-great-stones-from-heaven against-Amorites Beth-Horon) + EZK 38:22 LXX (Gog-judgment hail+fire+brimstone) + ISA 30:30 LXX. HAPAX ταλαντιαῖος (only NT — approximately one talent). Third-of-triple-blasphemy completes-bowl-cycle.

REV 15:2.notes: The seer describes the victors standing ἐπὶ τὴν θάλασσαν. Thai has them on the glass sea, while the BSB places them beside it. The stationary pose permits different renderings of ἐπί. In Exodus 14 the sea and the pillar of fire and cloud are distinct. The sea mixed with fire belongs to Revelation’s vision.

REV 15:3.notes: In Greek Deuteronomy 32:4 the works are true, and the ways are judgments. The song calls the Lord just and holy. Revelation addresses God directly, calling his ways just and true in 15:3 and calling him holy in 15:4. It adapts the wording of Moses’ song. Greek Psalm 110:2 (English 111:2) calls the Lord’s works great. Greek Psalm 138:14 (English 139:14) has θαυμάσια where Revelation uses θαυμαστά. At 15:3 the SBLGNT reads τῶν αἰώνων, ‘of the ages’, rendered แห่งกาลทั้งปวง. NA28, Tregelles and Robinson–Pierpont read τῶν ἐθνῶν, ‘of the nations’, as in the BSB. The alternatives replace one noun with another. Hebrew Jeremiah 10:7 asks who would not fear the king of the nations. Rahlfs–Hanhart Greek Jeremiah 10 passes directly from verse 5 to verse 9 and does not contain that question. The Hebrew comparison helps explain Revelation 15:4, and the ‘nations’ alternative at 15:3.

REV 15:4.notes: Hebrew Jeremiah 10:7 asks who would not fear the king of the nations. Rahlfs–Hanhart Greek Jeremiah 10 passes directly from verse 5 to verse 9 and does not contain that question. The Hebrew comparison helps explain Revelation 15:4, and the ‘nations’ alternative at 15:3. Greek Psalm 97:2 (English 98:2) uses ἐγνώρισεν of making salvation known and ἀπεκάλυψεν of revealing righteousness. Revelation uses ἐφανερώθησαν for the righteous acts being manifested. Greek Psalm 85:9 (English 86:9) supplies the nations coming and worshipping motif. Compare the description of God’s holiness in Deuteronomy 32:4.

REV 15:5.notes: Greek Numbers 9:15 gives τὴν σκηνήν, τὸν οἶκον τοῦ μαρτυρίου, identifying the tent as the house of testimony. Numbers 17:7 uses τὴν σκηνὴν τοῦ μαρτυρίου, the tent of testimony. Revelation draws on this tabernacle terminology for the heavenly temple.

REV 15:6.notes: The six men in Greek Ezekiel 9:2 are accompanied by one man wearing a long robe and a sapphire belt. The Hebrew description mentions linen and a writing kit. In Old Greek Daniel 10:5 the man wears linen and is girded around the waist with linen amid a description of light. Revelation puts golden bands across the angels’ chests.

REV 15:7.notes: In both Old Greek and Theodotion the living-God declaration is Daniel 6:27 (commonly 6:26 in English). The Greek Daniel versions express the duration differently. Revelation 15:7 uses its recurring ‘ages of the ages’ expression for the life of God.

REV 15:8.notes: DIRECT CITATION cluster: EXO 40:34-35 LXX (cloud-filled-tabernacle-of-testimony, glory-of-LORD, Moses-cannot-enter) + 1 KGS 8:10-11 LXX [3 KGS 8:10-11 LXX] (cloud-filled-Solomon's-temple, priests-cannot-stand-to-minister) + ISA 6:1-4 LXX (smoke-filled-temple at-prophet's-call). Theophanic-cloud-as-judgment-seal: throne-room sealed-off during-bowl-judgments.

REV 14:1.notes: In Hebrew Psalm 2:6 God speaks of installing his king on Zion. In Greek Psalm 2:6 the king speaks in the first person of being installed by God on Zion. The Lamb standing on Mount Zion recalls the setting of the psalm. The names on the foreheads contrast with the beast’s mark in 13:16–17.

REV 14:5.notes: ‘No lie in their mouths’ echoes ZEP 3:13 LXX (‘οὐ μὴ εὑρεθῇ ἐν τῷ στόματι αὐτῶν γλῶσσα δολία’ — ‘no-deceitful-tongue-in-their-mouths’ — eschatological-remnant) + ISA 53:9 LXX (the-Servant: ‘οὐδὲ εὑρέθη δόλος ἐν τῷ στόματι αὐτοῦ’ — ‘no-deceit-in-his-mouth’). The 144,000 share-the-Servant's-character.

REV 14:7.notes: The call to worship the Creator alludes to Exodus 20:11 and Psalm 146:6 (Greek Psalm 145:6). Heaven, earth and sea recur in Revelation 10:6. Here the angel also names springs of water, น้ำพุทั้งหลาย. The call to fear God recalls Ecclesiastes 12:13.

REV 14:8.notes: Hebrew Isaiah 21:9 repeats the verb for Babylon’s fall. Greek Isaiah 21:9 has a single perfect πέπτωκεν, followed by the fallen or broken images. Greek Jeremiah 28:8 (Hebrew and English 51:8) has a single aorist and speaks of Babylon being shattered. Greek Jeremiah 28:7 gives the preceding wine imagery. Revelation repeats its aorist ἔπεσεν. Compare the announcement again at Revelation 18:2.

REV 14:10.notes: Greek Psalm 74:9 (English 75:8) describes the cup in the Lord’s hand using οἴνου ἀκράτου. Greek Jeremiah 32:15 (Hebrew and English 25:15) likewise describes unmixed wine in the cup given to the nations. Revelation’s cup of wrath also uses ἄκρατος for wine that is undiluted.

REV 14:11.notes: In Greek Isaiah 34:10 perpetual duration accompanies the statement that the fire will not be quenched. The following clause says smoke will rise. Revelation expressly assigns the ages of the ages to the ascending smoke. Greek Genesis 19:28 separately presents flame rising from the plain like furnace vapor.

REV 14:14.notes: ‘Like-Son-of-Man on-cloud’ direct-allusion to DAN 7:13 LXX (Son-of-Man-coming-with-clouds). Christological-eschatological-reaper-figure with-golden-crown + sharp-sickle.

REV 14:15.notes: In Greek Joel 4:13 (English 3:13) the command to send sickles is plural, the harvest is present and the winepress is full. Revelation 14:15 addresses one reaper and says the grain harvest is dry. Verse 18 separately addresses one reaper and calls the grapes ripe.

REV 14:18.notes: Continuation of-JOEL 3:13 LXX direct-citation (vintage-of-the-grapes — second-half of-the-OT-text). The grape-harvest = wrath; matches v.15 grain-harvest = first-half of-Joel-text.

REV 14:19.notes: Revelation alludes to the winepress and divine judgment in Isaiah 63:1–6. Hebrew Isaiah 63:3 describes spattering blood or lifeblood on the warrior’s garments. Greek Isaiah 63:3 speaks of bringing their blood down to earth. Revelation 14:19 places the grapes in the winepress and verse 20 describes blood flowing out.

REV 13:1.notes: Beast-from-Sea direct-allusion to DAN 7:2-7 LXX (four-beasts-from-the-sea). Revelation's-Beast = composite-Antichrist of-Daniel's-four-beasts (lion + bear + leopard + fourth-terrifying-beast).

REV 13:2.notes: DIRECT CITATION of DAN 7:4-6 LXX (first-three-beasts: lion + bear + leopard). Revelation-Beast composite-of-three Daniel-beasts. The Antichrist combines-all-evil-imperial-tyrannies.

REV 13:5.notes: DIRECT ALLUSION to DAN 7:8, 11, 20 LXX (the-little-horn ‘mouth-speaking-great-things’ + boasting-blasphemy) + DAN 7:25 (‘speaks-words-against-the-Most-High and-shall-wear-out-the-saints-of-the-Most-High’ + ‘time-times-half-time’ = 42-months). The little-horn-of-Daniel-7 fulfilled-as-Antichrist-Beast.

REV 13:7.notes: Revelation alludes to the horn’s attack in Daniel 7:21. Theodotion has ἐποίει πόλεμον μετὰ τῶν ἁγίων and ἴσχυσεν for its success. Old Greek describes the conflict with πρὸς and τροπούμενον. Revelation retains the war with the saints and uses νικῆσαι for the beast overcoming them. The list of peoples recalls 5:9 and 7:9.

REV 13:13.notes: False-prophet-fire-from-heaven INVERTS Elijah-fire-from-heaven: 1 KGS 18:38 LXX (Mt-Carmel-victory) + 2 KGS 1:10-12 LXX (Ahaziah's-captains). Anti-Elijah-deception. Cross-reference to REV 11:5 (true-witnesses fire-from-mouth).

REV 13:14.notes: Image-of-Beast worship-or-die echoes DAN 3:1-7 LXX (Nebuchadnezzar's-golden-image: worship-or-be-burned-in-furnace). Imperial-cult mandatory-worship pattern.

REV 13:10.notes: Greek Jeremiah 15:2 repeats εἰς αἰχμαλωσίαν in its announcement of captivity. Greek Jeremiah 50:11 (Hebrew and English 43:11) repeats the pattern using ἀποικισμόν for deportation and ῥομφαίαν for sword. Revelation uses αἰχμαλωσίαν and μάχαιρα. Matthew 26:52 speaks of taking up a sword. Revelation’s selected text speaks of one destined to be killed by the sword.

REV 12:1.notes: Sun + moon + 12-stars echo GEN 37:9-10 LXX (Joseph's-second-dream: sun + moon + 11-stars + Joseph = 12-tribes-of-Israel).

REV 12:2.notes: Mother-in-birth-pangs cluster: ISA 66:7-8 LXX (Zion-as-mother-giving-birth-to-nation-in-a-day) + MIC 4:10 LXX (‘ὠδίνε καὶ ἀνδρίζου ... ὡς τίκτουσα’ — daughter-of-Zion-in-birth-pangs).

REV 12:3.notes: The dragon has seven heads, ten horns and seven diadems. Daniel 7:7 supplies the ten-horn comparison, and 7:24 interprets the horns as kings. The seven heads and their diadems are features of this vision. The combination of heads and horns recurs in Revelation 13:1 and 17:3, 7.

REV 12:4.notes: In Daniel 8:10 Old Greek has ἐρράχθη and Theodotion has ἔπεσεν. Revelation uses ἔβαλεν for the dragon throwing a third of the stars to earth. Identifying these stars as angels is an interpretation of the vision. The Daniel parallel itself does not identify them.

REV 12:5.notes: Revelation 12:5 is the second of three iron-rod passages in book order, after 2:27 and before 19:15. Greek Psalm 2:9 addresses the ruler directly with ποιμανεῖς. Revelation describes the child in the third person and names all the nations.

REV 12:7.notes: Michael + dragon-warfare echoes DAN 10:13, 21; 12:1 LXX (Michael-as-Israel's-prince + cosmic-warfare against-Persia/Greece) + JUD 9 (Michael-disputing-with-Satan-over-Moses-body — corpus-internal-link). The archangel-Michael as dragon-defeater.

REV 12:9.notes: Four-fold-Satan-identification (dragon + ancient-serpent + devil + Satan) — the ‘ancient-serpent’ direct-link to GEN 3:1, 14-15 LXX (Eden-serpent-in-Garden) — protoevangelium-completed identification. The Christian-tradition's-definitive-integration of-Satan-vocabulary.

REV 12:10.notes: ‘Accuser of our brothers, accusing them day-and-night’ echoes JOB 1:6-12 + 2:1-7 LXX (Satan-as-accuser-in-divine-court accusing-Job) + ZEC 3:1 LXX (‘the satan-standing-at-his-right-hand to-accuse-him’ — Joshua-the-high-priest-vision). The Hebrew-שָׂטָן etymologically = ‘accuser’ — definitive-defeat of-his-court-role.

REV 12:12.notes: ‘Rejoice, heavens’ direct-allusion to ISA 49:13 LXX (‘εὐφραίνεσθε, οὐρανοί, καὶ ἀγαλλιάσθω ἡ γῆ’ — ‘rejoice, heavens, and let-the-earth-be-glad’). Servant-deliverance-rejoicing applied-to-cosmic-victory-over-Satan.

REV 12:14.notes: The eagle’s wings allude to Exodus 19:4 and Deuteronomy 32:11. Revelation 12:6 gives 1,260 days, while 12:14 says a time, times and half a time, close to Old Greek Daniel 12:7. Old Greek Daniel 7:25 uses repeated prepositions and genitive forms. Reading the plural as two times and the whole as three and a half years of 360 days is a schematic comparison.

REV 12:16.notes: Greek Numbers 16:30 speaks of the earth opening its mouth. Verse 32 describes the earth opening and swallowing the rebels. Greek Exodus 15:12 also says the earth swallowed the enemy. In Revelation the earth helps the woman by swallowing the river.

REV 12:17.notes: DIRECT ALLUSION to GEN 3:15 LXX (protoevangelium: ‘ἔχθραν θήσω ἀνὰ μέσον σου καὶ ἀνὰ μέσον τῆς γυναικὸς, καὶ ἀνὰ μέσον τοῦ σπέρματός σου καὶ ἀνὰ μέσον τοῦ σπέρματος αὐτῆς’ — ‘enmity-between you-and-the-woman, your-seed-and-her-seed’). The Eden-curse-of-the-serpent fulfilled-in-eschatological-warfare against-the-woman's-remaining-seed.

REV 11:1.notes: In Zechariah 2:5–6 in Greek, Hebrew and Eremos (2:1–2 in common English numbering), a man carries a line to measure Jerusalem’s width and length. Here the seer is given a reed and told to measure the temple, the altar and the worshipers. Compare Ezekiel 40–42 for the temple-measuring vision.

REV 11:2.notes: ‘Forty-two-months trampled’ echoes DAN 7:25 LXX + DAN 12:7 LXX (the ‘time + times + half-time’ = 3.5 years) + LUK 21:24 (‘Jerusalem-trodden-by-Gentiles until-the-times-of-the-Gentiles-are-fulfilled’ corpus-internal-link). 42-months = 3.5-years = 1260-days — Revelation's eschatological-half-week.

REV 11:3.notes: The number of witnesses recalls Deuteronomy 19:15. The witnesses wear sackcloth. Zechariah 13:4 mentions a hairy prophetic mantle. Second Kings 1:8 describes Elijah as hairy and mentions a leather belt. Neither comparison expressly says Elijah wore sackcloth.

REV 11:4.notes: Zechariah 4:2–3, 11 depicts a single lampstand flanked by two olive trees. In 4:14 two figures associated with oil stand beside the Lord of the whole earth. Revelation identifies its two witnesses with both two trees and two lampstands. Joshua and Zerubbabel are proposed identifications in Zechariah’s setting. Zechariah 4:14 and Revelation 11:4 do not name either figure.

REV 11:5.notes: Elijah calls down fire from heaven in 2 Kings 1:10, 12. In Jeremiah 5:14 God makes the prophet’s words fire in his mouth. Revelation’s fire comes from the witnesses’ mouths.

REV 11:6.notes: Elijah announces drought in 1 Kings 17:1, without giving its duration there. Luke 4:25 and James 5:17 specify three years and six months. In Exodus 7 God gives instructions through Moses and Aaron strikes the Nile. Revelation gives the witnesses power over the waters and the plagues.

REV 11:7.notes: First-mention of-the-Beast-from-the-Abyss. Echoes DAN 7:3, 7 LXX (four-beasts-from-the-sea — especially-the-fourth-terrifying-and-dreadful beast). Anticipates-REV-13:1-10 + 17:8 detailed-Beast-revelation.

REV 11:8.notes: Symbolic-naming Sodom + Egypt: (1) ISA 1:9-10 LXX calls-Jerusalem ‘Sodom’-and-‘Gomorrah’ (prophet's-rebuke of-spiritual-corruption) + EZK 16:46-49 LXX (Sodom-as-Jerusalem's-sister-symbol). (2) Egypt = bondage-symbol (EXO-tradition). The crucifixion-locale-identifier confirms-the-city-is-Jerusalem (where-Christ-was-crucified).

REV 11:11.notes: In Greek Ezekiel 37:5 God uses φέρω for bringing the breath of life to the bones. In 37:10 the breath enters εἰς αὐτούς, and the people stand ἐπὶ τῶν ποδῶν. Revelation 11:11 adds ἐκ τοῦ θεοῦ, uses ἐν αὐτοῖς for the breath entering the two witnesses and uses the accusative in ἐπὶ τοὺς πόδας. Their standing recalls Ezekiel’s scene with adapted wording.

REV 11:12.notes: Cloud-ascension echoes ACT 1:9 (Christ's-ascension-in-cloud — corpus-internal-link) + 2 KGS 2:11 LXX (Elijah-taken-up-in-whirlwind). Two-witnesses share-the-prophetic-ascension-pattern of-Christ-and-Elijah.

REV 11:13.notes: ‘Seven-thousand-killed’ INVERTS 1 KGS 19:18 LXX (Elijah's-7000-faithful-remnant: ‘κατέλιπα ἐν Ισραηλ ἑπτὰ χιλιάδας ἀνδρῶν, πάντα γόνατα ἃ οὐκ ὤκλασαν γόνυ τῷ Βααλ’). Here 7000-killed instead-of-7000-saved — eschatological-judgment-inversion.

REV 11:15.notes: Seventh-trumpet-victory cluster: (1) PSA 2:2 LXX (‘the-kings-of-the-earth ... against the LORD and against His Anointed/Christ’) — Messianic-Psalm-2-rebellion-resolved. (2) DAN 7:14, 27 LXX (Son-of-Man-eternal-kingdom + saints-receiving-everlasting-dominion). The cosmic-transition-of-rulership.

REV 11:18.notes: Greek Psalm 2:1 asks why the nations raged, using ἐφρύαξαν. Revelation 11:18 states that the nations were angry (ὠργίσθησαν) and turns to God’s wrath (ὀργή). The Thai distinguishes human anger from divine wrath.

REV 11:19.notes: Heavenly-temple-opened + ark-of-covenant-appears: echoes EXO 25:10-22 LXX (Tabernacle-ark-of-covenant Most-Holy-Place) + 2 MACC 2:4-8 (legendary-Jeremiah-hiding-the-ark + future-revealing). The earthly-symbolism fulfilled-in-heavenly-reality. Closes-the-trumpet-cycle (chs.4-11) with Sinai-theophany pattern (escalated-with-earthquake + great-hail).

REV 10:1.notes: Ezekiel 1:28 compares the surrounding radiance to a bow in rain clouds. Revelation 4:3 locates a rainbow around the throne. Revelation 10:1 places it on the angel’s head. Compare the pillar of fire in Exodus 13:21–22 and the radiant face in Matthew 17:2 and Revelation 1:16. In verse 6 the angel swears by the Creator.

REV 10:4.notes: ‘Seal what the seven thunders have spoken’ INVERTS DAN 12:4, 9 LXX (‘seal-up-the-words until-the-time-of-the-end’). Daniel-told-to-seal vs Revelation-told-to-NOT-write — the seven-thunders content remains divinely-hidden. Possibly-an apocalyptic-tradition-element that-John-was-restrained-from-publishing.

REV 10:5.notes: The angel raises the right hand. In Daniel 12:7 both Old Greek and Theodotion name both hands. Old Greek follows the oath verb with an accusative. Theodotion uses ἐν with the dative and the singular duration εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα. Revelation 10:6 has a bare dative in SBLGNT, while NA28 includes ἐν, and declares that God lives for the ages of the ages.

REV 10:6.notes: The angel raises the right hand. In Daniel 12:7 both Old Greek and Theodotion name both hands. Old Greek follows the oath verb with an accusative. Theodotion uses ἐν with the dative and the singular duration εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα. Revelation 10:6 has a bare dative in SBLGNT, while NA28 includes ἐν, and declares that God lives for the ages of the ages. The oath also identifies God as creator, recalling Exodus 20:11 and Psalm 146:6.

REV 10:7.notes: The allusion to Greek Amos 3:7 draws on its description of the Lord revealing his instruction to his servants the prophets. Revelation speaks of announcing good news to his servants the prophets. The designation of the recipients is shared. The verb and the message differ.

REV 10:9.notes: Greek Ezekiel 3:3 reports eating the scroll and then says it became like sweet honey in the prophet’s mouth. In Revelation the angel predicts a bitter stomach and a sweet mouth. John then experiences sweetness first and bitterness afterward. Ezekiel supplies the sweetness comparison, and Revelation supplies the bitterness.

REV 10:11.notes: John must prophesy concerning many peoples, nations, languages and kings. In 7:9 the list names every nation, tribes, peoples and languages. In 17:15 the waters signify peoples, multitudes, nations and languages. Each list serves its own scene. The prophetic commission also alludes to Jeremiah 1:10 and the prophetic sending in Ezekiel 2:3–7.

REV 9:2.notes: Greek Exodus 19:18 compares Sinai’s smoke with the smoke of a furnace. In Greek Genesis 19:28 Abraham sees flame rising from the land like furnace vapor. Revelation depicts smoke coming from the shaft and darkening both the sun and the air.

REV 9:3.notes: Demonic-locusts echo EXO 10:12-15 LXX (eighth-Egyptian-plague locust-army) + JOEL 1:4-2:25 LXX (locust-army-of-Day-of-the-Lord, with-fourfold-locust-naming). Egyptian-plague + Joel-army patterns combined.

REV 9:6.notes: In Greek Job 3:21, ὁμείρονται and οὐ τυγχάνουσιν describe people longing for death and failing to obtain it. Revelation 9:6 develops the image by portraying death itself fleeing from the people who seek it.

REV 9:7.notes: Greek Joel 2:4 reads ὡς ὅρασις ἵππων ἡ ὄψις αὐτῶν. Revelation 9:7 develops the likeness to horses ready for battle. The noise of chariots in Joel 2:5 also recalls the sound of the wings in Revelation 9:9.

REV 9:8.notes: ‘Teeth like those of lions’ direct-allusion to JOEL 1:6 LXX (‘οἱ ὀδόντες αὐτοῦ ὀδόντες λέοντος’ — ‘its-teeth teeth-of-lion’). Joel's-locust-army-imagery.

REV 9:9.notes: ‘Sound-of-wings-like-sound-of-chariots’ direct-allusion to JOEL 2:5 LXX (‘ὡς φωνὴ ἁρμάτων ἐπὶ τὰς κορυφὰς τῶν ὀρέων ἐξαλοῦνται’). Joel's-locust-army audio-imagery.

REV 9:14.notes: Euphrates-as-judgment-locus echoes GEN 15:18 LXX (Promised-Land-eastern-boundary at-the-Euphrates) + ISA 8:7 LXX (the king-of-Assyria coming-as-Euphrates-flood-judgment-against-Judah). Euphrates = OT-eschatological-judgment-river. Recurs at REV 16:12 (sixth-bowl).

REV 9:20.notes: Greek Psalms 113:12–15 and 134:15–17 (commonly 115:4–7 and 135:15–17 in English) describe human handiwork in silver and gold and idols unable to use their senses. Revelation specifies gold, silver, bronze, stone and wood, and selects seeing, hearing and walking. Daniel 5:23 likewise contrasts lifeless gods with the living God.

REV 8:1.notes: Greek Zechariah 2:17 (English 2:13) calls on all flesh to show reverence before the Lord. Compare Habakkuk 2:20 and Zephaniah 1:7. Revelation describes actual silence in heaven lasting about half an hour. The allusion is thematic.

REV 8:3.notes: Heavenly-altar-of-incense draws on EXO 30:1-10 LXX (Tabernacle-golden-altar-of-incense before-the-veil) + PSA 141:2 LXX (corpus-link-to-REV-5:8 prayer-as-incense). The heavenly-Tabernacle-counterpart of-the-earthly-altar.

REV 8:5.notes: Censer-cast-down-to-earth echoes EZK 10:2 LXX (the man-clothed-in-linen taking-coals-from-between-the-cherubim and-scattering-them-on-the-city). Judgment-fire-cast-down.

REV 8:7.notes: Greek Exodus 9:24 describes τὸ πῦρ φλογίζον ἐν τῇ χαλάζῃ, with a participle for fire flaming amid the hail. Revelation 8:7 adds blood to its hail and fire. In 16:21 hail falls again, without the mixture of fire and blood.

REV 8:8.notes: Greek Jeremiah 28:25 (Hebrew and English 51:25) portrays Babylon as a mountain rolled down from the rocks and made like a burned mountain. Later, in 28:63–64 (Hebrew and English 51:63–64), a scroll with a stone is thrown into the Euphrates. It is Revelation that has a burning mountain-like object cast into the sea. The change of water to blood also recalls the Nile plague in Exodus 7:20–21.

REV 8:11.notes: The Hebrew of Jeremiah 9:14 (often 9:15 in English) and 23:15 uses לַעֲנָה for wormwood. Greek Jeremiah 9:14 has ἀνάγκας and ὕδωρ χολῆς, hardships and water of gall. Greek 23:15 has ὀδύνην and ὕδωρ πικρόν, pain and bitter water. Neither verse contains Revelation’s Greek plant name Ἄψινθος. A shared plant image does not establish an etymological relationship.

REV 8:12.notes: Cosmic-darkness echoes EXO 10:21-23 LXX (ninth-Egyptian-plague: thick-darkness-over-Egypt) + JOEL 2:10, 31; 3:15 LXX (Day-of-the-Lord cosmic-disturbance — sun/moon/stars-darkened). Egyptian-plague-pattern + Day-of-the-Lord pattern combined.

REV 7:1.notes: Four-winds-of-the-earth + four-angels echo DAN 7:2 LXX (‘the-four-winds-of-heaven striking-the-great-sea’) + ZEC 6:5 LXX (the four-spirits/winds going-out from-before-the-Lord-of-all-the-earth). Cosmological-totality-of-the-four-corners — restraining-judgment for-the-sealing.

REV 7:3.notes: In Greek Ezekiel 9:4 a sign is to be placed on the foreheads of people lamenting the abominations in Jerusalem. Revelation instead speaks of sealing God’s servants on their foreheads before harm comes to the earth, sea and trees. The protective forehead marking connects the scenes.

REV 7:9.notes: ‘Multitude-no-one-could-count from-every-nation’ direct-thematic-allusion to GEN 15:5 LXX (Abraham-promise: stars-uncountable) + GEN 22:17 LXX (sand-of-the-seashore-uncountable). Abrahamic-promise eschatologically-fulfilled with universal-scope. Palm-branches echo LEV 23:40 LXX (Sukkoth-Feast-of-Tabernacles palm-branches) — eschatological-fulfillment of-the-Feast.

REV 7:14.notes: Old Greek Daniel 12:1 describes an unprecedented day of distress. Matthew 24:21 has θλῖψις μεγάλη, rendered ความทุกข์ลำบากใหญ่หลวง. Revelation has the article with both noun and adjective and renders the phrase ความทุกข์ใหญ่. The texts share distress language without specifying identical time spans.

REV 7:15.notes: Hebrew Leviticus 26:11 speaks of God placing his dwelling among his people. The Rahlfs–Hanhart Greek reads ‘my covenant’ there and speaks of God walking among them in 26:12. Greek Ezekiel 37:27 likewise places God’s dwelling among them. Revelation 7:15 describes God spreading his tent over them, while 21:3 speaks of dwelling with them.

REV 7:16.notes: Isaiah 49:10 in Greek lists heat and then the sun, and the one who shows mercy guides the people by springs. Revelation adapts the promise. It names the sun before any heat, and in verse 17 the Lamb shepherds the people and guides them to springs. The Thai groups both sources of harm under the same negative.
