LUK 3:17.notes: Unquenchable-fire (πυρὶ ἀσβέστῳ) = ISA 66:24 eschatological-judgment language (also cited at MRK 9:43-48). Threshing-floor judgment image from MIC 4:12. Day-burning-as-furnace MAL 4:1. Synoptic parallel MAT 3:12.

LUK 3:19.notes: Herodias-marriage violates Lev 18:16 + 20:21 (brother's-wife prohibition, applicable since brother was still living — no levirate exception per Deut 25:5-10).

LUK 3:2.notes: The prophetic allusion lies in the word of God coming to John. Greek Jeremiah 1:1 uses ῥῆμα with ἐπί, while verse 2 has λόγος and πρός. Luke gives John’s location and dates his call without measuring an interval of prophetic silence.

LUK 3:21.notes: Heavens-opened theophany: ISA 64:1 (Oh, that you would tear open the heavens and come down) + EZK 1:1 (the heavens were opened, I saw visions of God). Luke uses plainer ἀνοίγω vs. Mark's more-dramatic σχίζω.

LUK 3:22.notes: Father's voice composite: (a) "you are my Son" = PSA 2:7 royal-Messianic; (b) "the beloved" = GEN 22:2 Isaac-allusion (only/beloved son offered); (c) "in you I am well pleased" = ISA 42:1 servant-song. Triadic christological-theological claim: King + Sacrificial-Son + Suffering-Servant. Identical composite to MAT 3:17 + MRK 1:11.

LUK 3:23.notes: Age-30 biblical-significance: priestly-service age (Num 4:3), David reign-start age (2 Sam 5:4), Joseph-in-Egypt age (Gen 41:46). Jesus begins ministry at the age-threshold of priestly/royal/patriarchal service.

LUK 3:27.notes: Zerubbabel and Shealtiel are named post-exilic leaders (Ezra 3:2 Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel led temple-rebuilding; Neh 12:1 exile-return list).

LUK 3:31.notes: Luke names Nathan in David’s family. The allusion is a genealogical correspondence with 2 Samuel 5:14 and 1 Chronicles 3:5. The Thai of 1 Chronicles has นาธัน, as here, and 2 Samuel has นาธาน. The context identifies the son of David.

LUK 3:32.notes: Luke’s names recall the genealogy in Ruth 4:18–22 and 1 Chronicles 2. Brenton’s Greek Ruth spells Salmon, Boaz and Obed Σαλμών, Βοόζ and Ὠβήδ, compared with Luke’s Σαλά, Βόος and Ἰωβήλ. Luke 3:33 has Admin and Arni where Matthew 1:3–4 and Greek Ruth 4:19 have Aram.

LUK 3:33.notes: Luke’s names recall the genealogy in Ruth 4:18–22 and 1 Chronicles 2. Brenton’s Greek Ruth spells Salmon, Boaz and Obed Σαλμών, Βοόζ and Ὠβήδ, compared with Luke’s Σαλά, Βόος and Ἰωβήλ. Luke 3:33 has Admin and Arni where Matthew 1:3–4 and Greek Ruth 4:19 have Aram.

LUK 3:34.notes: Abraham-Terah-Nahor lineage per Gen 11:24-26. Luke continues past Abraham (where Matthew begins) to universalize Jesus's genealogy.

LUK 3:35.notes: Brenton’s Genesis 10:24 and 11:12–14 place Cainan between Arphaxad and Shelah. Genesis 10:22 also lists a Cainan among Shem’s sons. Brenton’s 1 Chronicles 1:24 omits the intervening name. Jubilees 8:1–5 preserves the longer line. At Luke 3:36 Vaticanus includes Cainan and Bezae omits him. These witnesses do not determine the direction of borrowing.

LUK 3:36.notes: Brenton’s Genesis 10:24 and 11:12–14 place Cainan between Arphaxad and Shelah. Genesis 10:22 also lists a Cainan among Shem’s sons. Brenton’s 1 Chronicles 1:24 omits the intervening name. Jubilees 8:1–5 preserves the longer line. At Luke 3:36 Vaticanus includes Cainan and Bezae omits him. These witnesses do not determine the direction of borrowing.

LUK 3:37.notes: Luke’s pre-flood Cainan in verse 37 belongs to the generation after Enosh. The genealogy in Genesis 5 supplies the parallel. The Cainan between Arphaxad and Shelah in verses 35–36 belongs to another generation.

LUK 3:38.notes: Genesis 1:26–27 describes humanity in God’s image and 2:7 describes God forming the human and giving him breath. Luke ends his genealogy with the genitive “of God,” understood in Thai as Adam’s sonship. Romans 5 and 1 Corinthians 15 compare Adam and Christ. These offer theological parallels without establishing literary dependence.

LUK 3:4.notes: ISA 40:3 LXX verbatim except αὐτοῦ for LXX τοῦ θεοῦ ἡμῶν — same modification Mark and Matthew make. Synoptic-parallel verbatim with MRK 1:3 + MAT 3:3. Luke is unique in extending the Isaiah quote through 40:5 (vv.5-6).

LUK 3:5.notes: ISA 40:4 LXX with minor Lukan paraphrase (drops πάντα, shifts τραχεῖα-sing to plural, writes ὁδοὺς λείας for LXX πεδία). Matthew and Mark do not include this verse — Lukan universalism extends the quote.

LUK 3:6.notes: ISA 40:5 LXX final-clause citation (drops first clause about YHWH glory appearing). UNIQUE TO LUKE. Universal-salvation scope (πᾶσα σάρξ = all humanity/all flesh) is Lukan theological signature (cf. 2:32; Acts 1:8). Closes inclusio with Simeon σωτήριον at 2:30.

LUK 3:7.notes: The coming-wrath (μέλλουσα ὀργή) language echoes OT day-of-YHWH prophetic tradition. Synoptic parallel MAT 3:7.

LUK 3:8.notes: Abrahamic-covenant background (Gen 17:4-7 father of many nations) which crowds presume on. ISA 51:1-2 rock-from-which-you-were-hewn invokes the same stone/sons (banim/abanim) Hebrew wordplay that stands behind the saying.

LUK 4:10.notes: Devil quotes LXX Ps 90:11 (MT Ps 91:11): τοῖς ἀγγέλοις αὐτοῦ ἐντελεῖται περὶ σοῦ τοῦ διαφυλάξαι σε. DELIBERATELY SELECTIVE: omits «ἐν πάσαις ταῖς ὁδοῖς σου» (in all your ways) which qualifies divine protection as covering the faithful believer's ordinary paths, not demand-test scenarios. HAPAX: διαφυλάσσω.

LUK 4:11.notes: Continuation of devil's Ps 91 quote: ἐπὶ χειρῶν ἀροῦσίν σε μήποτε προσκόψῃς πρὸς λίθον τὸν πόδα σου verbatim from LXX Ps 90:12. Even truncated, the citation is rhetorically skilled — Ps 91 is genuinely a messianic-protection psalm.

LUK 4:12.notes: οὐκ ἐκπειράσεις κύριον τὸν θεόν σου verbatim from LXX Deut 6:16. Original Deut context references Massah (Ex 17:1-7) where Israel demanded water-proof from Yahweh. Jesus refuses the parallel demand for self-protection-proof. All three temptation-responses (vv.4, 8, 12) come from Deut 6-8 (Shema-cluster) — Jesus as true Israel rehearses the Torah Israel failed to keep.

LUK 4:18.notes: Luke’s composite citation draws on Isaiah 61:1–2 and 58:6. The imperative of Isaiah 58:6 becomes the infinitive ἀποστεῖλαι within the series of purposes. At 4:19 Luke uses κηρύξαι with the year of the Lord’s favor. Greek Isaiah 61:2 uses καλέσαι with the same noun phrase.

LUK 4:19.notes: Luke’s composite citation draws on Isaiah 61:1–2 and 58:6. The imperative of Isaiah 58:6 becomes the infinitive ἀποστεῖλαι within the series of purposes. At 4:19 Luke uses κηρύξαι with the year of the Lord’s favor. Greek Isaiah 61:2 uses καλέσαι with the same noun phrase.

LUK 4:2.notes: 40-day fast paradigm (Moses on Sinai; Elijah to Horeb) + Israel's 40-year wilderness testing typology — Jesus as true Israel succeeds where the nation failed at hunger-testing.

LUK 4:25.notes: Luke gives the duration as three years and six months, as does James 5:17. First Kings 17:1 reports the drought and 18:1 locates the word to Elijah in the third year. Sirach 48:3 speaks of shutting the sky without giving the duration. Only Luke and James give the precise interval among these comparisons.

LUK 4:26.notes: Reference to Elijah and the widow of Zarephath in Sidon (1 Kgs 17:8-24). HAPAX: Σάρεπτα. Theological scandal — God bypasses Israelite need to provide for a Gentile widow. Foreshadows Lukan Gentile-mission theme (cf. 2:32; Acts).

LUK 4:27.notes: Reference to Naaman the Syrian's cleansing through Elisha (2 Kgs 5:1-14). THREE HAPAX (proper-noun): Ἐλισαῖος, Ναιμάν, Σύρος. Escalation from v.26 — not just foreign widow (passive recipient) but foreign army-commander (active enemy). Both Elijah and Elisha episodes ground the Gentile-grace theme that enrages the Nazareth audience in v.28.

LUK 4:3.notes: Wilderness hunger-testing framework: as Yahweh tested Israel with hunger to know what was in their heart, so devil tests the Son with hunger to see if he will trust.

LUK 4:4.notes: Luke quotes the opening of Deuteronomy 8:3 about living on bread alone. SBLGNT ends there. Tregelles and Robinson–Pierpont continue with “but on every word of God.” Matthew 4:4 and Greek Deuteronomy include what proceeds from God’s mouth. Mark 1:12–13 gives no bread dialogue.

LUK 4:8.notes: κύριον τὸν θεόν σου προσκυνήσεις καὶ αὐτῷ μόνῳ λατρεύσεις. LXX Deut 6:13 has φοβηθήσῃ for MT תירא 'fear'; Jesus/Lukan tradition uses προσκυνήσεις 'worship' (perhaps via Targumic-influenced reading). αὐτῷ μόνῳ 'him only' is also a Jesus-emphasis addition not strictly in MT/LXX. Part of the Shema-cluster (Deut 6:4-15). Synoptic parallel Matt 4:10.

LUK 5:12.notes: Leviticus 13 gives background for diagnosing and isolating a person with a serious skin condition, including 13:45–46. Luke 5:12 does not say that addressing Jesus violated a particular requirement. Luke 5:14 separately directs the man to the priest with the offering Moses commanded; its registry entry refers directly to Leviticus 14:1–32.

LUK 5:13.notes: Jesus's touch inverts the Levitical rule that contact with uncleanness transfers pollution. Here cleansing flows outward from Jesus to the leper, not pollution inward.

LUK 5:14.notes: Jesus instructs the healed leper to present the offering Moses prescribed for cleansing — direct reference to the Levitical ritual of restoration (lamb or doves per economic status).

LUK 5:20.notes: Jesus's pronouncement of forgiveness invokes YHWH's self-declaration in Isaiah that He alone blots out transgressions. The scribes rightly recognize this as a divine prerogative (v.21).

LUK 5:21.notes: Scribes' objection 'who can forgive sins but God alone' echoes ISA 43:25's exclusivity — YHWH alone forgives sin. Their theology is correct; their recognition is incomplete.

LUK 5:24.notes: First 'Son of Man' saying in Luke. Title derives from Daniel 7:13-14 where one 'like a son of man' receives eternal dominion from the Ancient of Days. Jesus claims divine authority to forgive sins on earth via this Danielic title.

LUK 5:30.notes: Pharisees' grumbling (ἐγόγγυζον) echoes the LXX vocabulary of Israel's wilderness grumbling against Moses and YHWH. The verb γογγύζω in LXX almost exclusively appears in the wilderness-rebellion narratives (Exo 16; Num 11, 14, 16, 17). Luke subtly positions the Pharisees as successors to Israel's rebellious tendency.

LUK 5:34.notes: Jesus's self-identification as the bridegroom invokes the OT marriage metaphor for YHWH and Israel. By taking this title, Jesus implicitly claims the divine role in the covenant-marriage. Cf. JHN 3:29 where John the Baptist calls Jesus the bridegroom.

LUK 5:8.notes: Peter's self-identification as a sinful man in response to theophany parallels Isaiah's 'I am a man of unclean lips' response to the temple vision. Same pattern: sinful human encounters divine holiness and recognizes own unworthiness.

LUK 6:13.notes: The choice of twelve apostles echoes the twelve-tribe structure of Israel — Jesus explicitly frames his movement as new-Israel-foundation. Cf. LUK 22:30 ('you will sit on thrones judging the twelve tribes'), REV 21:12-14 (twelve gates + twelve foundations of new Jerusalem). The number is not incidental but theologically-loaded.

LUK 6:17.notes: The crowd from 'Tyre and Sidon' (Gentile Phoenician cities) alongside the Judean Jews is a subtle Lukan-universality marker. Luke's gospel has the Isaiah 49:6 'light-to-the-Gentiles' theme running from Simeon's song (LUK 2:32) through Acts (ACT 13:47). Gentile-inclusion is Luke's distinctive theological emphasis.

LUK 6:20.notes: 'Blessed are the poor' echoes Isaiah 61:1's 'good news to the afflicted/poor' (LXX: εὐαγγελίσασθαι πτωχοῖς) — the very text Jesus read at his Nazareth-synagogue inauguration (LUK 4:18-19). Luke's literal 'poor' (πτωχοί) preserves the social-justice edge that Isaiah 61 originally carried. The kingdom-reversal: the materially-poor, the people Isaiah's servant was sent to, now receive the kingdom.

LUK 6:21.notes: Isaiah 61:3 promises 'comfort to those who mourn...garments of praise for the spirit of heaviness' — Jesus's hungry-now-filled and weeping-now-laughing extend this promise. Psalm 126:5-6 'those who sow in tears shall reap in joy' provides the eschatological-reversal pattern. Both texts ground the beatitudes in OT kingdom-hope.

LUK 6:23.notes: 'Their fathers treated the prophets in the same way' explicitly invokes the persecuted-prophets tradition of the OT. 2 Chronicles 36:16 summarizes the pattern: 'they mocked God's messengers...until there was no remedy.' Stephen's speech (ACT 7:52) makes this explicit: 'which of the prophets did your fathers not persecute?' The persecution-of-prophets is a theological-diagnostic of covenant-unfaithfulness.

LUK 6:24.notes: The οὐαί-formula follows OT-prophetic-pattern (Isaiah 5:8-23 has six woes; Amos 5:18-20, 6:1; Habakkuk 2:6-19). Amos 6:1 'woe to those at ease in Zion' is a close parallel — pronouncing judgment on the wealthy-complacent. Isaiah 5:8 pronounces woe on those who 'join house to house' (accumulation-without-end). Jesus extends this prophetic-woe-form to his own audience.

LUK 6:26.notes: Micah 2:11 satirizes the popular false-prophet: 'If a man...should preach to you of wine and strong drink, he would be this people's preacher.' Jeremiah 23:16-17 denounces prophets who 'keep saying to those who despise me, the LORD has said, It shall be well with you.' These texts provide the OT-pattern for Jesus's warning that universal-praise is the mark of false-prophecy, not true-prophecy.

LUK 6:27.notes: Jesus radicalizes Leviticus 19:18's 'love your neighbor' by extending 'neighbor' to include 'enemy.' Proverbs 25:21-22 provides the practical-behavior model: 'If your enemy is hungry, give him bread to eat; if he is thirsty, give him water to drink.' Paul quotes PRO 25:21-22 in Rom 12:20. Jesus's love-enemies teaching is the fulfillment-extension of Torah's neighbor-love.

LUK 6:3.notes: Jesus's appeal to the David-and-showbread narrative (1 Sam 21:1-6) to justify his disciples' Sabbath-plucking. David, fleeing Saul, received consecrated showbread from priest Ahimelech at Nob. Jesus uses this as a greater-to-lesser argument: if the anointed-king-in-need could eat priest-only bread, the greater-than-David Son-of-Man can grant Sabbath-flexibility. The 'have you not read' formula is Jesus's signature Scripture-appeal-against-religious-leaders (cf. MAT 12:3, 19:4, 21:16, 21:42, 22:31).

LUK 6:30.notes: Deuteronomy 15:7-11 commands Israel to 'open wide your hand' to the poor and 'lend him sufficient for his need.' Jesus extends this to radical-generosity: give to everyone who asks, don't demand back what's taken. Torah's generous-lending ethic becomes Jesus's non-reciprocal-giving ethic.

LUK 6:35.notes: Psalm 145:9 'The LORD is good to all, and his mercy is over all that he has made.' God's universal-kindness toward-all-creation (including the ungrateful and wicked) grounds the disciple's enemy-love ethic. Jesus's logic: imitate God's universal-kindness-to-all by extending kindness-to-enemies.

LUK 6:36.greek_matches: imitating God and shared mercy adjective
LUK 6:36.notes: Leviticus 19:2 calls Israel to be holy because God is holy (Hebrew קדוש; Greek ἅγιος). Deuteronomy 18:13 uses תמים for being blameless. Luke calls the hearers to be merciful like their Father. Greek Exodus 34:6 also calls God οἰκτίρμων, merciful. The pattern and adjective have distinct sources.

LUK 6:37.notes: Leviticus 19:15-18 commands righteous-judgment-without-partiality plus neighbor-love. Jesus extends to 'do-not-judge-at-all' (in the sense of condemnatory-judgment). The mishnaic measure-for-measure principle (Sotah 1:7) captures the same reciprocity-logic Jesus uses here. Rabbi Hillel's near-contemporary teaching paralleled this.

LUK 6:4.notes: Luke 6:4 continues the David-showbread narrative (1 Sam 21:6 the specific act of eating) and cross-references the Levitical law (Lev 24:5-9) which restricted the bread-of-the-presence to the Aaronic priests as a perpetual-due. Jesus's argument: David's act was technically a ceremonial-transgression, but Ahimelech granted it and David received it without divine-censure, showing that ritual-law yields to the greater-claim of God's-anointed-servant in need.

LUK 6:41.notes: Psalm 19:12-13 'Who can discern his errors? Cleanse me from hidden faults. Keep back your servant also from presumptuous sins.' The Psalmist's self-examination-prayer models the inward-first-discernment Jesus commends. The rabbinic parallel (b. Arachin 16b, Rabbi Tarphon) also captures the cultural critique of self-righteous-reproof.

LUK 6:45.notes: Proverbs 4:23 'Guard your heart with all diligence, for from it flow the springs of life.' Proverbs 16:23 'The heart of the wise makes his speech judicious.' Both texts establish the heart-speech connection Jesus uses: what is inside the heart inevitably comes out in speech and action. The heart as the inner-source of outward-behavior is a core wisdom-theology theme.

LUK 6:46.notes: Malachi 1:6 'A son honors his father, and a servant his master. If then I am a father, where is my honor? If I am a master, where is my fear?' God's critique of empty-ritual-honor without substantive-obedience matches Jesus's rebuke of 'Lord, Lord' without obedience. Both texts critique the gap between verbal-confession and actual-loyalty.

LUK 6:48.notes: Isaiah 28:16 'Behold, I am the one who has laid as a foundation in Zion, a stone, a tested stone, a precious cornerstone, a sure foundation' establishes the firm-foundation motif Jesus uses. Isaiah 28:17-19 contrasts this with the 'overflowing scourge' that sweeps away the refuge-of-lies. Proverbs 10:25 'When the whirlwind passes, the wicked is no more, but the righteous has an everlasting foundation' provides the whirlwind-reveals-foundation image.

LUK 6:49.notes: The collapse-of-the-foundationless-house pairs with v.48 on the same Isaiah-28 / Proverbs-10 foundation-theology. The 'great ruin' (ῥῆγμα μέγα) is the decisive-judgment image — those who hear but do not obey face catastrophic-collapse when the flood comes. Proverbs 10:25 specifically contrasts the wicked (swept-away) with the righteous (everlasting-foundation).

LUK 7:11.notes: At Nain Jesus restores a widow’s only son. The account recalls Elijah and a widow in 1 Kings 17:17–24; that account calls the boy her son without specifying he was her only child. Luke 7:15 shares the wording about giving him to his mother. Elisha’s restoration of the Shunammite woman’s son in 2 Kings 4:18–37 is a second comparison. Her husband is alive and speaks with her in 4:22–23.

LUK 7:13.notes: ἐσπλαγχνίσθη is the Greek-lexicalization of Hebrew rachamim (רַחֲמִים = womb-compassion). In OT this is YHWH's own compassion (Ps 103:13 'as a father has compassion on his children, so the LORD has compassion on those who fear him'; Isa 49:15 mother-not-forgetting-nursing-child). Luke's first narratorial ὁ κύριος + σπλαγχνίζομαι marks Jesus as the compassion-of-YHWH embodied.

LUK 7:15.notes: καὶ ἔδωκεν αὐτὸν τῇ μητρὶ αὐτοῦ = VERBATIM LXX 1 Kgs 17:23 (Elijah returns widow's son to his mother at Zarephath). Luke's lexical-signature: explicit intertextual echo of Elijah's greatest miracle, now surpassed (Jesus commands vs Elijah prays + stretches three times). Completes the new-Elijah frame begun at v.11.

LUK 7:16.notes: ἐπεσκέψατο ὁ θεὸς τὸν λαὸν αὐτοῦ matches LXX-formula for YHWH's saving-visitation: Gen 21:1 (visiting Sarah to give Isaac), Exo 3:16 (visiting Israel in Egypt), Ruth 1:6 (visiting Naomi's people with bread). Lukan inclusio with 1:68 εὐλογητὸς κύριος ... ἐπεσκέψατο (Benedictus) and 1:78 ἐπισκέψεται. Crowd's language is theologically precise even if their Christology stops at 'great-prophet.'

LUK 7:22.notes: SHARED WITH MAT 11:5. Six-item Messianic-signs-list: blind-see / lame-walk / lepers-cleansed / deaf-hear / dead-raised / poor-evangelized. Items 1,2,4 match ISA 35:5-6 LXX near-verbatim (τυφλοί + χωλοί + κωφοί); item 6 (πτωχοὶ εὐαγγελίζονται) matches ISA 61:1 LXX verbatim (εὐαγγελίσασθαι πτωχοῖς). Items 3 (lepers) and 5 (dead-raised) EXCEED Isaiah's prophecy — Jesus's ministry-signs surpass even what was promised. Jesus's answer to John IS the self-evident Messianic-claim: what Isaiah foretold is happening + more.

LUK 7:27.notes: Jesus introduces a composite quotation concerning John. Greek Exodus 23:20 begins with καί, ἰδού and explicit ἐγώ, and sends the messenger “before you.” Luke’s SBLGNT starts with Ἰδού and omits the independent ἐγώ, which occurs in Robinson–Pierpont. Greek Malachi 3:1 uses ἐξαποστέλλω and “before me.” The shared Greek and the change of pronoun do not establish when the passages were first combined.

LUK 7:28.notes: γεννητοὶ γυναικῶν = Hebraism 'those born of women' for humans-generally (cf. Job 14:1 'Man who is born of a woman'; Job 15:14; Job 25:4). Jesus uses the OT-idiom to frame a superlative: of all humans up to this point, no one is greater than John. Sets up the epochal-distinction of kingdom-of-God surpassing all pre-kingdom distinctions.

LUK 7:34.notes: Pharisees' accusation ἄνθρωπος φάγος καὶ οἰνοπότης echoes DEU 21:20 LXX rebellious-son formula συμβολοκοπῶν οἰνοφλυγεῖ ('glutton, drunkard'), which in Torah warrants stoning. The Pharisees deploy a serious Torah-category against Jesus, not casual insult. Jesus's retort in v.35 subverts: wisdom is vindicated by its children, not its Torah-wielding accusers.

LUK 7:35.notes: Lady-Wisdom personification-tradition: 'Children' of Wisdom = those who embrace her (Prov 8:32 'Blessed are those who keep my ways'). The vindication-of-Wisdom-by-children formula echoes Sir 4:11 (Wisdom's-children) as well. Jesus applies the wisdom-tradition to the John-Jesus reception: those responding-in-faith prove God's two-fold emissary-strategy right.

LUK 7:50.notes: πορεύου εἰς εἰρήνην = LXX-formula for farewell-blessing (לֵךְ לְשָׁלוֹם). Eli blesses Hannah (1 Sam 1:17), Jonathan blesses David (1 Sam 20:42), priest blesses Danites (Judg 18:6). Jesus's closing-pronouncement draws on the OT-farewell-blessing tradition. This is the FIRST LUK use (will repeat at 8:48 to hemorrhaging woman).

LUK 8:10.notes: Luke's abbreviated form of Isaiah 6:9 LXX. LXX reads: Ἀκοῇ ἀκούσετε καὶ οὐ μὴ συνῆτε, καὶ βλέποντες βλέψετε καὶ οὐ μὴ ἴδητε. Luke compresses to ἵνα βλέποντες μὴ βλέπωσιν καὶ ἀκούοντες μὴ συνιῶσιν (same-root repetition preserved — seeing-see, hearing-understand). Luke's version is markedly shorter than Matt 13:14-15 (full LXX quote) and Mark 4:12 (Targum-influenced). Luke's ἵνα clause-structure shifts from Isaiah's indicative-prophetic-command to explicit-purpose: Jesus speaks in parables SO THAT the non-disciples will encounter the same hardening-judgment Isaiah announced. Applied to Jesus's parabolic teaching as prophetic-fulfillment pattern. Parallels: Mark 4:12, Matt 13:13-15, John 12:40, Acts 28:26-27.

LUK 9:14.notes: The meal in Luke is arranged in groups of about fifty. Exodus 16 narrates the manna. Exodus 18:21 and 25 and Deuteronomy 1:15 describe leaders over thousands, hundreds, fifties and tens. The numerical allusion is a comparison with the organization of Israel. Those passages assign responsibilities and do not describe seating at a meal.

LUK 9:17.notes: Feeding-miracle with leftovers echoes Elisha multiplying bread for 100 men in 2 Kings 4:42-44 (τὸ περισσεῦσαν αὐτοῖς κλασμάτων). Also the wilderness-manna (Exo 16).

LUK 9:22.notes: The "third day" resurrection-formula (τῇ τρίτῃ ἡμέρᾳ ἐγερθῆναι) alludes to Hosea 6:2 LXX (ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῇ τρίτῃ ἀναστησόμεθα). Jonah 1:17 (three days-three nights) is an alternate source.

LUK 9:26.notes: Daniel 7:13–14 describes one like a human coming with the clouds to the Ancient of Days and receiving dominion. Attendants serve in 7:10. Luke’s Son of Man saying explicitly names his glory, the Father’s glory and that of the holy angels. The allusion concerns the figure and dominion.

LUK 9:29.notes: HAPAX ἐξαστράπτω (flashing like lightning) for Jesus's garments echoes LXX Dan 10:6 (angel-of-the-Lord: ὡς ὅρασις ἀστραπῆς) and Ezek 1:4,14 (ὡς εἶδος λαμπάδων ... ὡς εἶδος τοῦ βεζέκ). Theophanic-radiance vocabulary.

LUK 9:31.notes: ἔξοδος means departure and is the Greek title of the book of Exodus. Exodus 1:1 itself begins with the names of the sons of Israel. The presence of Moses makes an exodus comparison possible. Luke does not quote the opening verse.

LUK 9:33.notes: Peter's proposal to make three σκηναί (tents/booths) for Jesus, Moses, and Elijah evokes the Feast of Tabernacles/Sukkot (Lev 23:42-43) when Israel dwelt in booths commemorating wilderness-wandering.

LUK 9:34.notes: The overshadowing-cloud (νεφέλη ... ἐπεσκίαζεν) echoes the shekinah-cloud filling the tabernacle (Exo 40:34-38), pillar-of-cloud (Exo 13:21), and Sinai-cloud (Exo 24:15-18). Theophanic-cloud imagery.

LUK 9:35.notes: SBLGNT reads “my Chosen One,” supported by Sinaiticus, Vaticanus and L. Alexandrinus and W have the short “beloved,” as do Robinson–Pierpont and the standard Textus Receptus. Bezae has a longer reading with the expression of approval. Compare the longer voice in Matthew 17:5 and the short “beloved” in Mark 9:7. The voice also recalls Psalm 2:7, Isaiah 42:1 and Deuteronomy 18:15.

LUK 9:41.notes: Deuteronomy 32:5 has “a crooked and perverted generation.” Luke shares γενεά and διεστραμμένη but uses ἄπιστος, “unbelieving,” in place of σκολιά. Deuteronomy 32:20 describes a generation differently and says its children lack faith. These are close verbal and thematic echoes.

LUK 9:51.notes: Double-allusion: (1) τὸ πρόσωπον ἐστήρισεν echoes Ezek 21:2 LXX στήρισον τὸ πρόσωπόν σου (prophetic-determination-formula for facing judgment); (2) ἀνάλημψις (HAPAX) echoes Elijah's being-taken-up in 2 Kings 2:9-11 LXX (ἀναλαμβάνω). Frames Jesus's Passion-Resurrection-Ascension as his "taking-up," with prophetic-face-set resolve.

LUK 9:54.notes: James and John's request πῦρ καταβῆναι ἀπὸ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καὶ ἀναλῶσαι αὐτούς directly alludes to Elijah calling fire from heaven on Ahaziah's messengers (2 Kings 1:10-12). TEXTUAL VARIANT: Byz/TR explicitly adds ὡς καὶ Ἠλίας ἐποίησεν ("as Elijah also did"); SBLGNT/NA28 omits as secondary-harmonization.

LUK 9:60.notes: Jesus's radical-prioritization of kingdom-proclamation over burying one's father echoes Deut 33:9 (Levi, who disregarded father/mother to keep God's covenant). The Levitical-model of undivided-service becomes the disciple's model.

LUK 9:61.notes: The would-be-disciple's request to first-bid-farewell-to-family directly echoes Elisha asking Elijah for the same permission in 1 Kings 19:19-21. Elijah granted Elisha's request; Jesus does NOT grant this request — a deliberate more-stringent-than-Elijah move.

LUK 9:62.notes: HAPAX ἄροτρον (plow). The plow-image directly echoes Elisha plowing with twelve-yoke-of-oxen when Elijah called him (1 Kings 19:19-21). Jesus's saying inverts the OT-precedent: where Elijah permitted farewell, Jesus insists on undivided-forward-focus.

MAT 10:13.notes: The returning-peace concept (if the house is not worthy, your peace returns to you) reflects Isa 55:11 LXX-tradition: 'my word shall not return to me empty' — pronounced blessings/words are efficacious, binding-to-recipient or reverting-to-sender, never void. Jewish cultural-liturgical background treats pronounced blessings as performatively-effective (Gen 27 Isaac's blessing as irrevocable).

MAT 10:15.notes: Sodom and Gomorrah invoked as the OT archetype of divine-judgment on wicked cities. Wider biblical trajectory of the Sodom-judgment-formula: Deut 29:23; Isa 1:9-10; Jer 23:14; Amos 4:11. Jesus appropriates the judgment-archetype for rhetorical intensification: towns that reject the kingdom-message face judgment worse than Sodom's — because greater revelation creates greater accountability. Thematic-parallel with Matt 11:20-24 (woes on Galilean cities).

MAT 10:21.notes: Foreshadows the explicit MIC 7:6 citation at Matt 10:35-36. The family-betrayal prophecy ('brother will betray brother to death') anticipates the explicit Micah-quotation three verses later. Mic 7:6 was cited in Jewish apocalyptic tradition (m. Sotah 9:15; b. Sanhedrin 97a; 4 Ezra 5:9; 2 Baruch 70:3-7) as a sign of the Messianic age's birth-pangs — Jesus inscribes his mission within this prophetic-apocalyptic frame.

MAT 10:22.notes: The 'for my name's sake' (διὰ τὸ ὄνομά μου) formula echoes the OT prayer-language of Dan 9:19 LXX (ἕνεκεν τοῦ ὀνόματός σου 'for your name's sake') — intercessory-prayer pleading God's own-name-honor as ground for divine-action. Jesus inverts: now his own name is the ground for which disciples suffer, claiming divine-name-authority. The formula is picked up by early apostolic consciousness: Acts 5:41 (apostles rejoicing to suffer 'for the name'); 3 John 7 ('for the sake of the name they went out'). Thematic-allusion only; no direct verbal-citation.

MAT 10:35.notes: Explicit Micah 7:6 citation, paraphrased not quoted-verbatim. LXX Mic 7:6: υἱὸς ἀτιμάζει πατέρα, θυγάτηρ ἐπαναστήσεται ἐπὶ τὴν μητέρα αὐτῆς, νύμφη ἐπὶ τὴν πενθερὰν αὐτῆς, ἐχθροὶ ἀνδρὸς οἱ ἐν τῷ οἴκῳ αὐτοῦ ('a son dishonors father, a daughter rises against her mother, a bride against her mother-in-law; a man's enemies are those in his house'). Matthew's verbal-form uses διχάσαι (HAPAX in NT) instead of LXX ἐπαναστήσεται — paraphrastic rendering. Mic 7:6 was cited in Jewish apocalyptic tradition as Messianic-age sign; Jesus claims fulfillment by applying it to the gospel's divisive-effect.

MAT 10:36.notes: Continuation/completion of MIC 7:6 citation begun at Matt 10:35. The clause καὶ ἐχθροὶ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου οἱ οἰκιακοὶ αὐτοῦ is a close-verbatim rendering of LXX Mic 7:6c ἐχθροὶ ἀνδρὸς οἱ ἐν τῷ οἴκῳ αὐτοῦ. Matthew substitutes οἰκιακοί 'household-members' for LXX's οἱ ἐν τῷ οἴκῳ 'those in his house' — lexical tightening without semantic change. Together vv.35-36 form the Matthean appropriation of Mic 7:6 as Christological-fulfillment of the Messianic-age family-upheaval prophecy.

MAT 10:6.notes: πρόβατα ἀπολωλότα οἴκου Ἰσραήλ echoes LXX Jer 50:6 πρόβατα ἀπολωλότα ἐγένετο ὁ λαός μου ('my people have become lost sheep') and Ezek 34:4-6, 34:16 (shepherdless-scattered-sheep imagery — the prophetic critique of Israel's leadership). Matthew repurposes the prophetic complaint-imagery to frame Jesus's mission: Israel is the lost-sheep nation, and the Twelve are sent as gatherers. Phrase reappears at Matt 15:24 applied to Jesus's own self-described mission.

MAT 11:10.notes: MAJOR COMPOSITE CITATION. Opening phrase idou ego apostello ton aggelon mou pro prosopou sou = VERBATIM EXO 23:20 LXX (YHWH sends angel ahead of Israel into Canaan). Continuation hos kataskeuasei ten hodon sou emprosthen sou adapts MAL 3:1 LXX (idou ego exapostello ton aggelon mou, kai epiblepsetai hodon pro prosopou mou). CHRISTOLOGICAL HIGH-WATERMARK: Matthew/Jesus changes Malachi's 'ahead-of-me' (pro prosopou mou) to 'ahead-of-you' (pro prosopou sou) — reassigning YHWH's forerunner to now-go-before Messiah. This makes Jesus the kyrios of Mal 3:1 whose-coming-John-prepares. SHARED-TRADITION with MRK 1:2 and LUK 7:27 (all three synoptics cite the same composite-fusion). Mark attributes it to Isaiah (bundles Mal 3:1 + Isa 40:3), suggesting shared pre-Synoptic Jesus-tradition.

MAT 11:11.notes: gennetos gynaikos 'born-of-woman' = Hebraic idiom for ordinary-human. Exact phrase JOB 14:1 LXX (brotos gennetos gynaikos), also JOB 15:14, 25:4. SIR 10:18 LXX similar formula. Idiom emphasizes ordinary-humanity — John is greatest among-all-humans-ever-born, yet kingdom-members exceed him.

MAT 11:14.notes: ELIJAH TYPOLOGY EXPLICIT. MAL 4:5-6 (LXX 3:22-23): 'I-will-send-Elijah-the-prophet before the great and terrible day of-the-LORD, who-will-restore-hearts.' Jesus identifies John-as-fulfillment. 1 KGS 17-19 narrate the historical Elijah (powerful-prophet, wilderness-ministry, leather-girdle at 2 KGS 1:8 matching John's at MAT 3:4). 2 KGS 2:1-17 Elijah taken-to-heaven-without-death (grounds the 'will-return' expectation). Two-variants of Elijah-typology in early-Judaism: (a) bodily-return (some rabbinic + contemporary Jewish), (b) spirit-and-power (NT position — Luke 1:17 explicitly). Matthew + Mark 9:12-13 affirm (b). John 1:21 John denies (a); Jesus affirms (b) — not contradictory.

MAT 11:19.notes: DOUBLE ALLUSION. (1) phagos kai oinopotes echoes DEU 21:20 LXX (rebellious-son charge: symbolokopon oinofluGei 'carousing + drunkard') — the CAPITAL-APOSTASY-CHARGE requiring stoning-by-elders. Accusers applying death-worthy-Torah-apostasy charge to Son-of-Man. Prefigures Jesus's eventual crucifixion-framing. (2) edikaiothe he sofia apo ton ergon autes = Wisdom-personification from PRO 8:12-36 + 9:1-6 LXX (Wisdom-as-woman calling-for-disciples) + SIR 24 LXX (Wisdom-speaks-autobiographically). Wisdom-vindicated-by-her-works = Jesus's ministry + disciples + miracles = vindicating-proof. TEXTUAL NOTE: SBLGNT reads ergon (works) per Aleph B* W; Byz/TR reads teknon (children) harmonizing with LUK 7:35. Word-choice variant.

MAT 11:21.notes: TYRE-SIDON-as-wicked-paradigm + SACKCLOTH-ASHES-repentance-sign. (1) ISA 23 (Tyre-oracle destruction-for-commercial-pride); EZK 26-28 (extended-Tyre-Sidon-oracle-doom); JOL 3:4-8 LXX (against-Tyre-Sidon for slave-trade). These are archetypal-wicked-Gentile-cities. (2) sakkos kai spodos (sackcloth-and-ashes) = ancient repentance-sign per JON 3:5-6 (Nineveh-king repents in sackcloth + ashes), DAN 9:3 (Daniel prays-for-Israel in sackcloth + ashes), EST 4:1-3 (Mordecai), 1 MAC 3:47. Jesus's argument: Tyre-Sidon would have done-what-archetypal-Nineveh did.

MAT 11:23.notes: MAJOR CITATION + BACKGROUND. (1) 'ascending-to-heaven -> descending-to-Hades' = direct lexical-echo ISA 14:13-15 LXX (eis ton ouranon anabesomai... katabese de eis haden) — originally against-Babylonian-king-hubris. Jesus applies Babylon-oracle-of-judgment to Capernaum, equating Capernaum's-rejection-of-Messiah with Babylon's-imperial-arrogance. (2) GEN 19:24-28 Sodom-destruction-background: God-destroyed Sodom for wickedness; Jesus claims even-Sodom would-have-repented if miracles-happened-there. Counterfactual exceeds the Tyre-Sidon comparison in v.21.

MAT 11:25.notes: ROLE-REVERSAL ECHO. ISA 29:14 LXX: apolo ten sofian ton sofon kai ten synesin ton syneton krypso — VERBATIM LEXEME-PAIR sofon + syneton (same two words as Jesus uses). In Isaiah, God-hides-wisdom-from-Jerusalem-elite as judgment; in Jesus, God-reveals-to-humble because-wise-reject. Matthean-ROLE-REVERSAL: Jesus turns Isaiah's woe against-wise into his-own-ministry-pattern. DAN 2:19-23 LXX Daniel's-prayer after receiving revelation-of-hidden-mysteries ('he reveals-deep-and-secret-things'). Jesus uses same-revelation-vocabulary. GEN 14:19 LXX title 'kyrios tou ouranou kai tes ges' from Melchizedek's-blessing to Abraham = Lord-Creator-title. Jesus's prayer addresses God with Abrahamic-cosmic-creator-title.

MAT 11:27.notes: JOHANNINE-THUNDERBOLT. All-things-given-over-to-me (Panta moi paredothe) echoes DAN 7:14 LXX ('edothe auto exousia' — authority-given-to-Son-of-Man). JER 31:34 LXX 'they-shall-all-know-me' (new-covenant-knowledge-of-God) parallels Father-Son mutual-exclusive-knowledge structure. SYNOPTIC-PARALLEL LUK 10:22. Stylistically-Johannine (cf. JHN 3:35, 10:15, 14:9-11) — the passage has more-Johannine-feel than anything-else in the Synoptics, earning its classical-name 'Johannine thunderbolt.' CHRISTOLOGICAL CLAIM: Jesus claims (a) unique-mutual-knowledge with Father, (b) authority-to-reveal-Father selectively. Both (a) and (b) are divine-prerogatives — the passage grounds high-Christology in Jesus's own self-identification.

MAT 11:29.notes: MAJOR CITATION. euresete anapausin tais psykhais hymon = NEAR-VERBATIM JER 6:16 LXX 'kai euresete hagnismon tais psykhais hymon' (some LXX-MSS actually read anapausin in Jer 6:16, making the match EXACT in those manuscripts). MT reads nafshekhem marga ('rest for your souls' — anapausin preferred over hagnismon). CONTEXT of Jer 6:16: YHWH invites Israel-to-return to ancient-paths-and-find-rest — BUT-Israel-REFUSES. Jesus inverts: he IS the-path-of-rest; his yoke replaces the ignored-ancient-invitation. Jesus-as-YHWH-voice. Christological high-watermark equivalent to MAT 7:23's Psalm 6:8 citation (Jesus-speaks-as-YHWH-Judge). Also-cross-references ZEC 9:9 LXX (praus meek-king, Matthean-Christology triple-occurrence 5:5 + 11:29 + 21:5) and SIR 51:23-27 LXX (wisdom-teacher's invitation + yoke + rest — explicit-precedent for Jesus-as-wisdom-teacher-inviting-disciples).

MAT 11:5.notes: Six-item Messianic-signs-list: blind-see / lame-walk / lepers-cleansed / deaf-hear / dead-raised / poor-evangelized. Items 1,2,4 match ISA 35:5-6 LXX near-verbatim (tuflon + cholos + kofon). Item 6 (ptoxoi euaggelizontai) matches ISA 61:1 LXX verbatim (euaggelisasthai ptoxois). Items 3 (lepers) and 5 (dead-raised) EXCEED Isaiah's prophecy — Jesus's ministry-signs surpass even what was promised. Jesus's answer to John IS the self-evident Messianic-claim: what Isaiah foretold is happening + more.

MAT 12:18.notes: LONGEST-OT-QUOTE in Matt. First Servant Song (Isa 42:1-4). Matthew's Greek DIVERGES from both MT and LXX — likely a Matthean-paraphrase or Greek-revision (kaige-tradition?). Key-divergences: MT אֶתְמָךְ-בּוֹ 'I uphold him' → LXX ἀντιλήψομαι → Matt ᾑρέτισα 'I chose'; MT רוּחִי עָלָיו 'my spirit upon him' → Matt future-tense θήσω τὸ πνεῦμά μου ἐπ' αὐτόν 'I will put my spirit on him.' CHRISTOLOGICAL-FOUNDATION: identifies Jesus as Isaianic-Servant. Servant-meekness-motif fulfilled in v.15 Jesus's silent-withdrawal. HAPAX αἱρετίζω (v.18) in this pericope.

MAT 12:19.notes: Continuation of Isa 42:1-4 Servant Song quoted across vv.18-21. v.19 = Isa 42:2 'οὐ κεκράξεται οὐδὲ ἀνήσει, οὐδὲ ἀκουσθήσεται ἔξω ἡ φωνὴ αὐτοῦ' (LXX). Matthew preserves the meek-Servant-motif. HAPAX ἐρίζω (NT-unique) appears in this verse. See MAT 12:18 entry for full Isa-42:1-4 citation discussion.

MAT 12:20.notes: Continuation of Isa 42:1-4 Servant Song. v.20 = Isa 42:3-4 'κάλαμον τεθλασμένον οὐ συντρίψει καὶ λίνον καπνιζόμενον οὐ σβέσει' (LXX form varies). Matthew's ἕως ἂν ἐκβάλῃ εἰς νῖκος τὴν κρίσιν paraphrases Isa 42:3c ('ἕως ἂν ἐκβάλῃ εἰς νῖκος τὴν κρίσιν'). HAPAX τύφομαι (NT-unique) in this verse. See MAT 12:18 entry.

MAT 12:21.notes: Closing of Isa 42:1-4 Servant-Song citation. v.21 = Isa 42:4b. Matthew's Greek DIVERGES from LXX: LXX Isa 42:4 reads καὶ ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματι αὐτοῦ ἔθνη ἐλπιοῦσιν; Matt has τῷ ὀνόματι αὐτοῦ ἔθνη ἐλπιοῦσιν (drops ἐπί). Matthean-editorial-shaping emphasizes Gentile-mission. See MAT 12:18 entry.

MAT 12:39.notes: 'Evil-and-adulterous-generation' reflects standard Prophetic-trope for spiritual-unfaithfulness/idolatry as marital-adultery. Hos 1-3 = Hosea's-marriage-to-Gomer enacting YHWH-Israel-covenant-drama. Jer 3:6-10 = Israel-as-harlot-to-other-gods. Ezek 16 + 23 = extended adultery-metaphor for Israel/Judah. μοιχαλίς picks-up this Prophetic-vocabulary.

MAT 12:4.notes: David-at-Nob episode: fleeing Saul, David and companions eat the showbread at the tabernacle sanctuary. Jesus uses the precedent to argue exception-for-human-need over ritual-strictness. Rabbinic tradition (b. Menahot 95b-96a) knew and debated this episode.

MAT 12:40.notes: DIRECT CITATION Jonah 2:1 LXX (ἐν τῇ κοιλίᾳ τοῦ κήτους verbatim-match). CHRISTOLOGICAL-PROPHECY: Jesus's first-public-prediction-of-burial-and-resurrection. Jonah-typology: (1) descent-to-underworld; (2) deliverance-by-God; (3) subsequent-Gentile-proclamation. HAPAX κῆτος shared with LXX Jonah. 'Three-days-three-nights' Semitic-inclusive-counting (Friday partial + Saturday + Sunday early = 3). 'Heart of the earth' = burial-in-tomb/grave.

MAT 12:41.notes: Nineveh-repents at Jonah's preaching. Jesus uses the Gentile-repentance as judgment-against-his-own-unrepentant-contemporaries. Christological-escalation: 'greater-than-Jonah-is-here' = Jesus > prophet. Pairs with v.42 (Queen-of-Sheba > Solomon-seeker).

MAT 12:42.notes: Queen of Sheba visits Solomon from 'ends-of-the-earth' (Sheba = southern Arabia, Yemen region) to hear Solomon's wisdom. Jesus: Gentile-woman-seeker was more-faithful to wisdom-pursuit than Jewish-men-of-this-generation. Christological-peak: 'greater-than-Solomon' = Jesus > wisest-king. Completes triplet: Jesus > temple (v.6), > prophet (v.41), > king (v.42).

MAT 12:5.notes: Sabbath sacrifices doubled (two lambs + extra grain/drink offerings) — Torah requires priestly work on sabbath. Matthean-distinctive argument (absent Mark/Luke). Closes qal-vachomer: if priests-profane-sabbath-are-innocent because of temple-service, how-much-more disciples-serving-Jesus (greater-than-temple v.6).

MAT 12:7.notes: DIRECT CITATION Hos 6:6 LXX verbatim (ἔλεος θέλω καὶ οὐ θυσίαν). Matthean SECOND-occurrence (first Matt 9:13 table-fellowship-context). CHRISTOLOGICAL-VOICE: Jesus takes YHWH-prophetic-rebuke position, applying Hosea's indictment-of-hollow-piety to Pharisaic sabbath-scrupulosity. Interpretive payload: mercy-toward-the-hungry > ritual-separation.

MAT 13:14.notes: Matthean fulfillment-formula (ὅπως πληρωθῇ → ἀναπληροῦται αὐτοῖς ἡ προφητεία) quoting Isaiah 6:9 LXX verbatim (Ἀκοῇ ἀκούσετε καὶ οὐ μὴ συνῆτε, καὶ βλέποντες βλέψετε καὶ οὐ μὴ ἴδητε). Dative-cognate Hebrew infinitive-absolute preserved in LXX and echoed by Matthew. Parallel: Mark 4:12 (paraphrase), Luke 8:10 (paraphrase), John 12:40 (Isa 6:10 with LXX divergence), Acts 28:26-27 (full Isa 6:9-10 LXX).

MAT 13:15.notes: Continues direct quote from Isaiah 6:10 LXX (ἐπαχύνθη γὰρ ἡ καρδία τοῦ λαοῦ τούτου ... καὶ ἰάσομαι αὐτούς). Speaker-shift mid-quote from prophet to YHWH-voice (first-person ἰάσομαι). Heart-hardening as judgment-language. Same passage cited at Acts 28:26-27 (Paul to Roman Jews) and John 12:40 (divergent text-form).

MAT 13:32.notes: Mustard-seed-becoming-tree + birds-nesting-in-branches draws on multiple OT tree-empire allegories: Dan 4:12,21 (Nebuchadnezzar's cosmic-tree with birds dwelling); Ezk 17:23 (messianic-cedar planted on Israel's mountain); Ezk 31:6 (Egypt's cedar-of-Lebanon where birds nest). Jesus co-opts pagan-empire-tree imagery for God's kingdom — humble mustard becomes Daniel's cosmic-tree. κατασκηνοῦν ἐν τοῖς κλάδοις αὐτοῦ echoes LXX Dan 4:21 verbatim.

MAT 13:33.notes: Sarah's three-seahs of flour for hospitality-to-divine-visitors at Mamre (σάτα τρία - same measure). Possibly recalled as Abrahamic hospitality-feast from smallest-beginning. If intentional: kingdom-as-feast motif with patriarchal-roots. Alternative: three-seahs is simply standard festival-bread-quantity in Jesus's culture.

MAT 13:35.notes: Matthean fulfillment-formula (ὅπως πληρωθῇ τὸ ῥηθὲν διὰ τοῦ προφήτου). Matthew quotes Ps 78:2 (LXX 77:2) — Asaph-psalm, Asaph called 'the seer/prophet' in 1 Chr 25:1-2. Matthew's ἐρεύξομαι diverges from LXX's φθέγξομαι — may be independent Greek-translation of MT הביעה, or alternate-Greek-revision (Aquila-like). SBLGNT omits κόσμου after καταβολῆς (short reading); Byz/ℵ²/C include. Christological: Jesus = the psalmist-teacher revealing hidden-from-foundation things.

MAT 13:37.notes: Son-of-Man Messianic-title first used by Jesus in self-reference throughout Matt (cf. 8:20, 9:6, 11:19, 12:8, 12:32, 12:40 prior occurrences). Dan 7:13-14 describes one-like-a-son-of-man receiving eternal-kingdom-and-dominion from Ancient-of-Days. Here: Son-of-Man sows + owns-the-kingdom (v.41) — Christological high-watermark claiming Daniel's-role.

MAT 13:41.notes: Son-of-Man sends-out-his-angels and owns-his-kingdom — continues Dan 7:13-14 royal-authority theme from v.37. Matthew's formulation 'his angels' + 'his kingdom' uniquely asserts Son-of-Man's cosmic-sovereignty, echoing Daniel's one-like-a-son-of-man receiving everlasting-dominion from Ancient-of-Days. Synoptic parallel Matt 16:27, 24:31 uses same angel-sending imagery for Son-of-Man's eschatological-role.

MAT 13:42.notes: κάμινος τοῦ πυρός 'furnace-of-fire' verbatim LXX-lexeme from Dan 3:6,11 (Nebuchadnezzar's fiery-furnace threat against those refusing idol-worship). Jesus re-uses the Babylonian-execution-furnace as eschatological-judgment-image. Matthean weeping-gnashing formula (7 occurrences: 8:12; 13:42,50; 22:13; 24:51; 25:30) unique to this gospel.

MAT 13:43.notes: ἐκλάμψουσιν ὡς ὁ ἥλιος adapts Dan 12:3 LXX 'οἱ συνιέντες λάμψουσιν ὡς ἡ λαμπρότης τοῦ στερεώματος, καὶ ἀπὸ τῶν δικαίων τῶν πολλῶν ὡς οἱ ἀστέρες'. Matthew substitutes ἐκλάμψουσιν (intensified) and ὡς ὁ ἥλιος (sun-brightness, stronger than Daniel's firmament-brightness). Resurrection-glory motif — the wise/righteous shine-bright. Theme continues in 1 Cor 15:41-43, Phil 2:15.

MAT 14:14.notes: σπλαγχνίζομαι compassion + healing pattern evokes YHWH's shepherd-compassion. Cf. MT 9:36 explicit sheep-without-shepherd (Num 27:17).

MAT 14:19.notes: Feeding miracle: Elisha feeding 100 with 20 loaves + leftovers (2 Kgs 4:42-44); manna-in-wilderness (Ex 16). Five-verb Eucharistic sequence also foreshadows MT 26:26.

MAT 14:23.notes: Mountain-prayer/solitude: Moses on Sinai (Ex 24), Elijah on Horeb (1 Kgs 19). Matthean pattern: prayer precedes revelatory action (cf. MT 17:1 transfiguration-mountain).

MAT 14:25.notes: Job 9:8 LXX: περιπατῶν ἐπὶ θαλάσσης (walking on the sea) — identical phrase describing divine prerogative. Ps 77:19 path through sea. Theophany: walking-on-water is divine act.

MAT 14:27.notes: ἐγώ εἰμι divine self-identification. Ex 3:14 LXX: ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ ὤν. Isa 43:10 LXX: ἐγὼ εἰμί (in monotheistic context). Surface meaning 'it is I' + theologically-loaded echo.

MAT 14:3.notes: Herodias prohibition — Lev 20:21 forbids marrying brother's wife while brother lives. John's rebuke in v.4 appeals to this Torah statute.

MAT 14:30.notes: Peter's cry σῶσόν με (save me!) from sinking fits psalm-of-distress pattern. Ps 69:1-2 'save me O God, waters have come up to my neck'; Ps 18:16 'drew me out of many waters.'

MAT 14:32.notes: Wind-stilling as theophany. Ps 107:29 'He made the storm be still, and the waves of the sea were hushed' — divine-prerogative over sea.

MAT 14:36.notes: κράσπεδον fringe = Hebrew ציצית tzitzit. Num 15:38-40, Deut 22:12 command fringes on garment-corners as reminder of Torah. Jesus as Torah-faithful Jew wears tzitzit; touching them = seeking Torah-compliant healing-authority.

MAT 14:4.notes: John's specific rebuke 'οὐκ ἔξεστίν' (it is not lawful) invokes the Torah prohibition at Lev 20:21 against marrying a living brother's wife. Matthew preserves John's legal-halakhic framing. Prophetic-confrontation pattern (cf. 1 Kgs 21 Elijah vs. Ahab).

MAT 15:13.notes: Thematic allusion to OT planting imagery: Israel as God's planting (Isa 60:21), vineyard-song (Isa 5:2), vine-of-Jer 2:21. Jesus inverts: unfaithful teachers are plants NOT from God, will be uprooted. Not verbal citation, but recognizable OT metaphor-cluster.

MAT 15:31.notes: Echo of Isa 35:5-6 Messianic-healing catalog (blind see, deaf hear, lame leap, mute sing). Matthew's crowd-response phrasing ("glorified the God of Israel") implies Gentile audience, amplifying the Isaianic-eschatological motif.

MAT 15:4.notes: Composite citation: (1) Ex 20:12 LXX / Deut 5:16 LXX "Honor father and mother" verbatim; (2) Ex 21:17 LXX / Lev 20:9 LXX penal clause "curser shall die" verbatim. Jesus pairs the positive command and its death-penalty enforcement to underscore the gravity the Pharisees' Corban-vow tradition has nullified.

MAT 15:8.notes: Isa 29:13 LXX near-verbatim. Citation continues into v9. Hebrew MT differs — Jesus follows LXX text-tradition consistent with Matthew's LXX-preference.

MAT 15:9.notes: Continuation of Isa 29:13 LXX citation begun at v8 (teaching human precepts as doctrine).

MAT 16:13.notes: First explicit 'Son of Man' question in Matthew's Caesarea Philippi pericope. ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου evokes Daniel 7:13-14 LXX where 'one like a son of man' (ὡς υἱὸς ἀνθρώπου) approaches the Ancient of Days and receives universal eschatological dominion. The choice of Caesarea Philippi as backdrop (a Greco-Roman religious center with Pan-grotto and Augustus-temple) sharpens the contrast: Jesus asks WHO this divine-Son-of-Man-figure-from-Daniel is, in the very place where competing divine-figures are venerated.

MAT 16:16.notes: Peter's confession ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ τοῦ ζῶντος invokes Davidic-covenant Son-of-God language: 2 Sam 7:14 ('I will be his father, and he shall be my son' — Davidic dynastic-promise) and Ps 2:7 ('You are my Son, today I have begotten you' — royal-coronation Psalm). The 'living God' (θεὸς ζῶν) qualifier echoes Deut 5:26, Josh 3:10, 1 Sam 17:26,36, Hos 2:1 LXX, Ps 84:3 LXX (frequent OT formula contrasting YHWH with dead-idols). At Caesarea Philippi — center of pagan worship — this confession is theologically maximal: the true God is alive and Jesus is his Davidic-Son.

MAT 16:18.notes: πύλαι ᾅδου ('gates of Hades') is a Septuagintal formula: Job 38:17 LXX (πύλαι θανάτου, parallel πυλωροὶ ᾅδου), Ps 9:14 LXX = MT 9:13 (πυλῶν τοῦ θανάτου), Isa 38:10 LXX (ἐν πύλαις ᾅδου, Hezekiah's lament). The LXX consistently uses πύλαι θανάτου / πύλαι ᾅδου for the realm-of-the-dead and its power. Jesus's promise that these gates will not prevail against his ἐκκλησία (FIRST OCCURRENCE in Matthew, in the Gospels) asserts that even death's domain cannot withstand the messianic-community founded on Peter's confession. The κατισχύω verb (3× NT) is rare and emphatic — 'overpower, prevail-against.'

MAT 16:19.notes: δώσω σοι τὰς κλεῖδας ('I will give you the keys') alludes to Isaiah 22:22 LXX, where YHWH transfers the 'key of the house of David' from Shebna to Eliakim with the formula 'he shall open and none shall shut, he shall shut and none shall open' (δώσω τὴν κλεῖδα οἴκου Δαυὶδ ἐπὶ τὸν ὦμον αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀνοίξει καὶ οὐκ ἔσται ὁ ἀποκλείων καὶ κλείσει καὶ οὐκ ἔσται ὁ ἀνοίγων). Cf. Rev 3:7 where the resurrected-Christ explicitly takes 'the key of David' to himself. The bind/loose terminology (δέω/λύω) is technical-rabbinic-halakhic for declaring forbidden/permitted; the periphrastic future-perfect (ἔσται δεδεμένον / λελυμένον) signals heaven's prior-judgment that earth's authority recognizes.

MAT 16:21.notes: First Matthean passion-prediction. Composite allusions: (1) Isaiah 53 Suffering Servant typology — the 'man of sorrows' rejected by elders/priests/scribes, killed for many, yet vindicated; (2) Hosea 6:2 LXX 'after two days he will revive us, on the third day he will raise us up' — the third-day-resurrection pattern; (3) Jonah 1:17-2:10 — three days in the great-fish belly, parallel to Matt 12:40 where Jesus draws this typology explicitly. δεῖ ('it-is-necessary') marks divine-necessity (cf. Lukan-Matthean usage for prophesied-events). The Sanhedrin trio (πρεσβύτεροι, ἀρχιερεῖς, γραμματεῖς) names the Jewish supreme-council that will engineer the crucifixion (cf. Matt 26:57-66, 27:1-2).

MAT 16:27.notes: Composite eschatological-judgment allusions: (1) DAN 7:13-14 LXX — Son-of-Man-coming-with-clouds receiving dominion-and-glory; key-Matthean source for 'Son of Man coming in the glory of his Father' (cf. also Matt 24:30, 25:31, 26:64); (2) ZEC 14:5 LXX 'the Lord my God will come, and all the holy ones with him' — divine-coming-with-angelic-retinue; (3) PSA 61:13 LXX (MT and Eremos Ps 62:13; English Ps 62:12) 'you, O Lord, will repay each according to his deeds' (σὺ ἀποδώσεις ἑκάστῳ κατὰ τὰ ἔργα αὐτοῦ); PRO 24:12 LXX 'who will not requite each according to his deeds?' Both Psalm and Proverbs use ἀποδίδωμι κατὰ + ἔργα/πρᾶξις — the very phrase Matthew echoes in 'ἀποδώσει ἑκάστῳ κατὰ τὴν πρᾶξιν αὐτοῦ.' Cf. Rom 2:6, Rev 22:12 for NT echoes.

MAT 16:4.notes: γενεὰ πονηρὰ καὶ μοιχαλίς ('wicked and adulterous generation') invokes the OT prophetic typology of Israel-as-unfaithful-spouse — Hos 1-3 (Gomer/Israel adultery), Jer 3:6-10 ('faithless Israel committed adultery'), Ezk 16 + 23 (Jerusalem/Samaria as adulterous-sisters). The σημεῖον Ἰωνᾶ phrase recalls Matt 12:39-40, where the Jonah-typology is unpacked as death-and-resurrection (three days in fish-belly = three days in tomb). Repeats Matt 12:39 verbatim minus 'τοῦ προφήτου.'

MAT 17:10.notes: The disciples' scribal-tradition 'Elijah must come first' reflects the scribes' standard interpretation of Mal 3:23-24 LXX (MT 4:5-6): καὶ ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ ἀποστελῶ ὑμῖν Ἠλίαν τὸν Θεσβίτην πρὶν ἐλθεῖν ἡμέραν κυρίου τὴν μεγάλην καὶ ἐπιφανῆ — 'I will send you Elijah the Tishbite before the great and manifest day of the Lord comes.' Second-temple Jewish expectation read this as a pre-messianic Elijah-appearance. The disciples, having just seen Elijah on the mountain, seek clarification. Matthew's 'οἱ γραμματεῖς λέγουσιν' (the scribes say) attributes the teaching to contemporary Jewish instruction, ultimately rooted in Malachi.

MAT 17:11.notes: Jesus's 'Ἠλίας μὲν ἔρχεται καὶ ἀποκαταστήσει πάντα' echoes Mal 4:6 LXX (3:24 MT): ἀποκαταστήσει καρδίαν πατρὸς πρὸς υἱόν — 'he will restore the heart of the father to the son.' The verb ἀποκαθίστημι is the direct LXX verb-pickup. Matthew's 'πάντα' (all-things) generalizes the Malachian restoration from the specific heart-turning to the broader eschatological-restoration-of-all-things (τὴν ἀποκατάστασιν πάντων Acts 3:21). Jesus affirms the scribal reading in principle while reassigning the fulfillment to John the Baptist (v12-13).

MAT 17:17.notes: 'Ὦ γενεὰ ἄπιστος καὶ διεστραμμένη' nearly verbatim echoes Deut 32:5 LXX (Song of Moses): γενεὰ σκολιὰ καὶ διεστραμμένη — 'a crooked and perverse generation.' Deut 32:20 LXX adds γενεὰ ἐξεστραμμένη ἐστίν υἱοί οἷς οὐκ ἔστιν πίστις ἐν αὐτοῖς — 'a perverse generation, sons in whom there is no faith.' Matthew's addition of 'διεστραμμένη' over Mark 9:19 sharpens the Deut 32 echo: Jesus positions himself as new-Moses rebuking wilderness-unfaithful-generation. The ἄπιστος adjective parallels Deut 32:20's οὐκ ... πίστις. Matthean new-Moses / new-Exodus typology — this generation of Israel is being judged as the wilderness generation was, with Jesus taking Moses's place.

MAT 17:2.notes: Two OT echoes layer in Matthew's transfiguration: (a) Exod 34:29 LXX δεδόξασται ἡ ὄψις τοῦ προσώπου αὐτοῦ — Moses's face-glow after Sinai theophany. Matthew's 'ἔλαμψεν τὸ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ ὡς ὁ ἥλιος' is Matthean-unique over Mark and deliberately intensifies the Moses-parallel. (b) Dan 7:9 LXX τὸ ἔνδυμα αὐτοῦ ὡσεὶ χιὼν λευκόν — white-as-snow garment of the Ancient of Days. Matthew's 'ἱμάτια αὐτοῦ ἐγένετο λευκὰ ὡς τὸ φῶς' invokes the same apocalyptic-enthronement-glory imagery. Matthew's Jesus is BOTH new-Moses (face-glory) AND Ancient-of-Days figure (white-clothing-of-divine-glory) — double typology.

MAT 17:3.notes: Moses (Exod 24:15-18) and Elijah (1 Kgs 19:8-13) each had mountain-top encounters with God on Sinai/Horeb — the same mountain-tradition. Their joint appearance at Jesus's mountain-transfiguration creates a mountain-theophany-inclusio. Secondary: Moses+Elijah both represent categories (Law+Prophets) that Jesus fulfills — Matthew 5:17 programmatic. No direct verbal citation; a sustained narrative-typological echo.

MAT 17:4.notes: Peter's 'ποιήσω τρεῖς σκηνάς' (I will build three shelters) invokes σκηνή — the tabernacle-construction vocabulary of Exod 25-40 (LXX σκηνή for 'tent of meeting') and the Feast of Booths (Sukkot, Lev 23:39-43, LXX ἑορτὴ τῶν σκηνῶν). Peter's impulse is Torah-shaped: where God's glory dwells, a tabernacle must be built. Matthew preserves this Jewish-religious-instinct; Jesus's non-response redirects from localized-dwelling to the greater reality of divine presence in Christ himself. No verbal citation, but a theological-vocabulary echo worth database recording.

MAT 17:5.notes: Four OT threads converge in the voice-from-cloud: (1) Ps 2:7 LXX υἱός μου εἶ σύ — 'you are my son' (royal-messianic adoption). (2) Isa 42:1 LXX ὁ ἀγαπητός μου ὃν ᾑρέτισα, προσεδέξατο αὐτὸν ἡ ψυχή μου — 'my beloved, in whom my soul takes pleasure' (servant-song). These two combine behind 'ὁ υἱός μου ὁ ἀγαπητός, ἐν ᾧ εὐδόκησα' — established at Matt 3:17 and Mark 1:11 baptism, repeated here. (3) Deut 18:15 LXX αὐτοῦ ἀκούσεσθε — 'you shall listen to him' — Matthew's + Mark's addition 'ἀκούετε αὐτοῦ' at transfiguration directly quotes this prophet-like-Moses passage, identifying Jesus as the Moses-foretold prophet. (4) Exod 40:34-35 LXX ἐπεσκίαζεν ἐπ' αὐτὴν ἡ νεφέλη — 'the cloud overshadowed it' (Shekinah glory on tabernacle). Jesus's transfiguration is a new-Sinai + new-tabernacle moment.

MAT 17:6.notes: Prophetic face-down-in-fear response to direct theophany: Ezek 1:28 'I saw the appearance... and when I saw it I fell on my face'; Dan 10:9 'I fell on my face in a deep sleep.' The disciples' ἔπεσαν ἐπὶ πρόσωπον αὐτῶν καὶ ἐφοβήθησαν σφόδρα is typical-OT-prophetic-theophanic-response. Matthean addition over Mark/Luke deliberately locates the disciples in the prophetic tradition — they have just experienced a direct divine speech-theophany and respond with appropriate prostrate-fear. No verbal citation, but formulaic-scriptural response-pattern.

MAT 18:10.notes: Royal-court idiom of 'seeing the face of the king' — Est 1:14 LXX 'οἱ βλέποντες τὸ πρόσωπον τοῦ βασιλέως' (seven princes of Persia with direct royal access); Tob 12:15 'I am Raphael, one of the seven holy angels who stand in the presence of God' (Second-Temple angelology). Jesus transfers this privileged-court-access imagery to guardian-angels of 'little ones,' establishing that the seemingly-insignificant have the highest-possible divine-court representation. Also background: Ps 91:11 angel-protection; Dan 10-12 nation-angels; 1 Enoch 40.

MAT 18:13.notes: Isa 62:5 LXX 'ὡς εὐφραίνεται νυμφίος ἐπὶ νύμφῃ, οὕτως εὐφρανθήσεται κύριος ἐπὶ σοί' (as the bridegroom rejoices over the bride, so shall your God rejoice over you) — divine-joy-over-restoration motif. Background only; Matthew does not cite or echo lexically, but the theological pattern of divine-exultant-joy-over-recovered-people parallels the shepherd-rejoicing-over-one-found-sheep.

MAT 18:16.notes: Direct citation of Deut 19:15b LXX 'ἐπὶ στόματος δύο μαρτύρων καὶ ἐπὶ στόματος τριῶν μαρτύρων στήσεται πᾶν ῥῆμα' — Matthew compresses LXX's double-mention to 'ἐπὶ στόματος δύο μαρτύρων ἢ τριῶν σταθῇ πᾶν ῥῆμα' while preserving key-lexemes στόματος/μαρτύρων/σταθῇ/πᾶν ῥῆμα verbatim. Deuteronomic witness-law (Deut 17:6, 19:15) applied to church-discipline. Also re-cited: 2 Cor 13:1, 1 Tim 5:19, Heb 10:28.

MAT 18:20.notes: Jewish-rabbinic Shekhinah-tradition: Pirkei Avot 3:2 (attrib. R. Hananiah ben Teradion, c.135 AD) 'when two sit together and study Torah, the Shekhinah rests between them'; 3:6 'ten who sit together to study — Shekhinah among them.' Though the compilation is post-NT, the tradition likely reflects earlier oral-tradition. Jesus displaces the Shekhinah-slot by naming HIMSELF as the divine-presence-among-two-or-three — Christological claim to occupy YHWH's presence-function with his community. Matthean inclusio-frame: Matt 1:23 'Emmanuel / God-with-us' + Matt 28:20 'I am with you always' bracket the gospel; 18:20 is the keystone.

MAT 18:22.notes: Gen 4:24 LXX Lamech-song 'ἑβδομηκοντάκις ἑπτά' (77-fold-vengeance: 'If Cain is avenged sevenfold, truly Lamech 77-fold') — canonical text of escalating-human-vengeance in primeval-history. Jesus deliberately cites the same numeric-phrase to INVERT it: exponential-vengeance becomes exponential-forgiveness. CHRISTOLOGICAL: Jesus reverses the curse-of-Cain-line by establishing a counter-line of unlimited-mercy. Number 77 chosen specifically (not 70x7=490) to match Lamech's LXX-phrase precisely — Matthew expects audience to hear the echo.

MAT 18:30.notes: Amos 2:6 LXX 'they sell the righteous for silver, the needy for a pair of sandals' + Amos 8:6 similar + 2 Kgs 4:1 widow's-family-seized-for-debt — OT-prophetic background condemning creditor-cruelty. Matthew does not lexically cite but the MORAL-LOGIC of prophetic-denunciation of debt-imprisonment underlies the parable's moral-force.

MAT 18:31.notes: Gen 4:10 LXX 'φωνὴ αἵματος τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ σου βοᾷ πρός με ἐκ τῆς γῆς' (the voice of your brother's blood cries out to me from the ground) — Abel's blood-crying-out paradigm + Exod 2:23 LXX Israel's-groaning-ascending-to-God. Background for the mercy-refused is mercy-revealed-to-the-higher-authority principle — injustice does not stay hidden but reaches the Sovereign. The σύνδουλοι's report to the king models the way-the-oppressed's-cry reaches God.

MAT 18:33.notes: Exod 34:6 LXX core-theophany 'κύριος ὁ θεὸς οἰκτίρμων καὶ ἐλεήμων, μακρόθυμος καὶ πολυέλεος καὶ ἀληθινός' (the Lord, merciful and compassionate, long-suffering and abundant-in-mercy and true) + Lev 11:44-45 imitatio-Dei principle 'be holy as I am holy.' Jesus (through the parable-king) applies mercy-reciprocity: those who-received-mercy must-extend-mercy (cf. Matt 5:7 Beatitude; Luke 6:36 'be merciful as your Father is merciful'). The parable dramatizes Matt 6:14-15's Lord's-Prayer-appendix: 'if you forgive men their trespasses, your Father will also forgive you; but if you do not forgive men their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses.'

MAT 18:5.notes: Prov 19:17 LXX 'ὁ ἐλεῶν πτωχὸν δανίζει θεῷ' (one who shows mercy to the poor lends to God) — divine-identification-with-marginal. Jesus here claims that reception-of-little-ones-in-his-name = reception-of-him. Christological high-watermark: Jesus takes YHWH-position as the one-with-whom-the-marginal-are-identified. Pattern culminates in Matt 25:40 'whatever you did for one of the least of these my brothers, you did for me.'

MAT 19:18.notes: DIRECT citation of Decalogue commandments 6-9 verbatim-LXX in Matthean-Exodus-order (murder, adultery, theft, false-witness). Exod 20:13-16 LXX = Deut 5:17-20 LXX (identical wording). Matthew presents the four second-tablet-neighbor-prohibitions. Mark 10:19 adds 'Do-not-defraud' (μὴ ἀποστερήσῃς) — not-from-Decalogue but from Deut 24:14 or Lev 19:13 re wages-of-hired-servant; Matthew omits this. Luke 18:20 follows Matthew-order.

MAT 19:19.notes: DIRECT composite citation: (1) Exod 20:12 LXX / Deut 5:16 LXX 'Τίμα τὸν πατέρα καὶ τὴν μητέρα' — 5th commandment; Matthew drops the 'σου' (your) possessive. (2) Lev 19:18 LXX 'ἀγαπήσεις τὸν πλησίον σου ὡς σεαυτόν' — the love-neighbor commandment Jesus pairs with the Shema as the greatest-commandments at Matt 22:37-40. MATTHEAN-ONLY ADDITION: Mark 10:19 / Luke 18:20 list only the neighbor-harm-prohibitions (no 5th commandment, no Lev-19:18). Matthew UNIQUELY ADDS the love-your-neighbor here, pre-echoing 22:37-40 and setting up the v.21 sell-all-and-give-to-poor test as a direct-neighbor-love check. Lev 19:18 is also cited at Matt 5:43, 22:39, Mark 12:31, Luke 10:27, Rom 13:9, Gal 5:14, Jas 2:8.

MAT 19:26.notes: Jesus's statement 'παρὰ θεῷ πάντα δυνατά' (with-God-all-things-possible) wed (1) Gen 18:14 LXX 'μὴ ἀδυνατεῖ παρὰ τῷ θεῷ ῥῆμα' (Is-anything-impossible-with-God? — said to Sarah about Isaac's conception) and (2) Job 42:2 LXX 'οἶδα ὅτι πάντα δύνασαι' (Job's confession 'I know that you can do all things'). Matthew's wording combines both: παρὰ-θεῷ-πάντα-δυνατά weds Gen 18's παρὰ-θεῷ with Job 42's πάντα-δυνατά. SOTERIOLOGICAL-PIVOT: Jesus declares salvation a divine-work not a human-achievement — a foundational grace-theology text.

MAT 19:4.notes: DIRECT citation of Gen 1:27 LXX 'ἄρσεν καὶ θῆλυ ἐποίησεν αὐτούς' — Jesus's creational-basis for marriage-indissolubility. Matthew preserves LXX wording verbatim. Jesus's rhetorical-strategy bypasses Deut-24 (Pharisees' proof-text) to ground marriage in Gen-1-2 creation-order. Paired with 19:5 GEN 2:24 as double-witness (cf. Deut 19:15 two-witnesses-standard).

MAT 19:5.notes: DIRECT citation of Gen 2:24 LXX 'ἕνεκεν τούτου καταλείψει ἄνθρωπος τὸν πατέρα αὐτοῦ καὶ τὴν μητέρα καὶ προσκολληθήσεται πρὸς τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἔσονται οἱ δύο εἰς σάρκα μίαν.' Matthew has κολληθήσεται (simple) where LXX has προσκολληθήσεται (compound); otherwise verbatim. Jesus re-anchors Gen 2:24's 'for-this-reason' backward-referent to Gen 1:27 (v.4 citation) unifying the argument. The 'one flesh' metaphor covers bodily, emotional, social, and covenantal union — not narrowly-sexual. Also cited at 1 Cor 6:16, Eph 5:31.

MAT 1:1.notes: βίβλος γενέσεως verbatim echoes LXX Gen 2:4 (αὕτη ἡ βίβλος γενέσεως οὐρανοῦ καὶ γῆς) and LXX Gen 5:1 (αὕτη ἡ βίβλος γενέσεως ἀνθρώπων). Matthew frames the Jesus-story as a new creation / new Adam / new humanity by borrowing the Septuagintal title-formula. This is the first of many Matthean Genesis-Exodus typological echoes. See also γένεσις at 1:18 (inclusio-ring with the phrase at 1:1).

MAT 1:20.notes: Matthew κατ ὄναρ (in a dream) motif — unique to Matthew among the evangelists, used 6x (1:20; 2:12, 13, 19, 22; 27:19) — typologically echoes the patriarch Joseph-of-Egypt, who receives prophetic dreams in Gen 37 (own dreams of preeminence) and interprets dreams in Gen 40-41 (cupbearer-baker; Pharaoh). Both Josephs are: (a) chosen by divine dream-revelation; (b) preservers of the people of God through Egyptian-exile phases; (c) key protector-figures in the Messianic line (OT-Joseph preserves Israel in Egypt via Gen 45; NT-Joseph preserves infant Messiah in Egypt via Matt 2:13-15). Matthew deliberately uses the Greek name Ἰωσήφ for both, heightening the typological echo. No direct verbal citation, but a sustained narrative-typological pattern worth database recording.

MAT 1:21.notes: σώσει τὸν λαὸν αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν αὐτῶν thematically echoes Ps 129:8 LXX (MT Ps 130:8): καὶ αὐτὸς λυτρώσεται τὸν Ἰσραὴλ ἐκ πασῶν τῶν ἀνομιῶν αὐτοῦ. σώζω and λυτρόω are semantically adjacent (save / redeem); ἁμαρτία and ἀνομία (sin / iniquity) overlap in LXX usage. Matthew recasts the Psalm redemption-promise as programmatic statement of Jesus mission. The angels name-etymology (Ἰησοῦς = YHWH-saves) makes the psalm echo explicit — Jesus IS the one who fulfills this psalm.

MAT 1:23.notes: DIRECT OT CITATION, Matthew first fulfillment-formula quotation (ἵνα πληρωθῇ at v.22). LXX Isa 7:14: ἰδοὺ ἡ παρθένος ἐν γαστρὶ ἕξει καὶ τέξεται υἱόν, καὶ καλέσεις τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ Εμμανουηλ. Matthew matches LXX verbatim except changes 2nd-sg. καλέσεις (you [sg.] will call) to 3rd-pl. καλέσουσιν (they will call) — shift from Ahaz specific naming to community-wide acclamation of Jesus as God-with-us. MT/LXX divergence: Heb. עַלְמָה (almah, young woman of marriageable age, implicitly but not strictly virgin). LXX παρθένος (virgin, technical sense). Matthew cites LXX specifically because παρθένος supports the virginal-conception narrative. INCLUSIO: Ἐμμανουήλ (God with us) at 1:23 forms Christological bookend with Matt 28:20 (ἐγὼ μεθ ὑμῶν εἰμι — I am with you). HAPAX: Ἐμμανουήλ (Matt 1:23 only in NT).

MAT 1:9.notes: The three-generation span Uzziah → Jotham → Ahaz → Hezekiah in Matthew genealogy roughly covers Isaiah prophetic ministry (Isa 1:1 names all four kings). Not a direct citation at v.9, but a historical-setting note: Matthew embeds the Isaianic prophetic era within the genealogy so that his later Isa 7:14 fulfillment-citation at v.23 stands on narrative-historical ground. Classified as background_allusion since no verbal borrowing at v.9; only ancestral placement of the Isaiah-era kings.

MAT 20:15.notes: SEMITIC-IDIOM "evil eye" (ὀφθαλμὸς πονηρός) for envy/stinginess grounded in: (1) Deut 15:9 LXX πονηρεύσηται ὁ ὀφθαλμός σου ("your eye becomes evil") — the sabbatical-year Mosaic warning not to begrudge the poor when the release-year approaches; (2) Prov 23:6 LXX μὴ συνδείπνει ἀνδρὶ βασκάνῳ (with-a-begrudging-eye-man do-not-eat); (3) Prov 28:22 LXX σπεύδει πλουτεῖν ἀνὴρ βάσκανος (a-man-with-an-evil-eye-hastens-to-be-rich). The idiom contrasts ὀφθαλμὸς ἁπλοῦς / ἀγαθός (Matt 6:22 "single/good eye" = generous heart) with πονηρός (envious/stingy heart). Jesus's parable-master rebukes the grumbling worker for envy-of-another's-gift — same vocabulary Jesus uses at Matt 6:22-23 (light-of-body-is-eye). Thematic-allusion, not citation.

MAT 20:18.notes: DIVINE-PASSIVE παραδοθήσεται ("will-be-handed-over") echoes Isa 53:6 LXX "κύριος παρέδωκεν αὐτὸν ταῖς ἁμαρτίαις ἡμῶν" and Isa 53:12 LXX "παρεδόθη εἰς θάνατον ἡ ψυχὴ αὐτοῦ" — the Suffering-Servant hand-over pattern. Matthew's third passion-prediction frames Jesus's betrayal as Servant-Song fulfillment. The same verb παραδίδωμι recurs v.19 παραδώσουσιν (active — chief-priests hand-to-Gentiles), completing the double-handoff.

MAT 20:19.notes: Jesus's prediction of Gentile-crucifixion "numbered with transgressors" (Isa 53:12 LXX "ἐν τοῖς ἀνόμοις ἐλογίσθη") anticipates Roman-execution under Gentile-magistrate. SBLGNT σταυρόω first-time on Jesus's lips here (expanding on 16:21/17:22-23 which used generic ἀποκτείνω "kill"). The mocking-scourging-crucifying triplet fulfilled in Matt 27:26-38. Thematic-background, not direct-citation — but frames the passion within the Servant-Song pattern.

MAT 20:21.notes: The mother's request for her sons to sit "at your right hand and at your left hand in your kingdom" invokes Ps 110:1 LXX "κάθου ἐκ δεξιῶν μου" (sit-at-my-right) — the Messianic-enthronement-oracle Jesus himself applies to υἱὸς Δαυίδ at Matt 22:44. The mother's THEOLOGY is correct (Jesus WILL be enthroned as Davidic-Messiah per Ps 110) but her TIMING and REQUEST are mistaken (Jesus does not assign honor-positions; Father prepares them per v.23). Matthew's Jesus confirms his enthronement at 25:31 ("καθίσει ἐπὶ θρόνου δόξης αὐτοῦ") and 26:64 ("ἐκ δεξιῶν καθήμενον τῆς δυνάμεως"). Thematic-allusion.

MAT 20:22.notes: The "cup" (ποτήριον) Jesus is about-to-drink activates multiple OT cup-of-wrath texts: (1) Ps 75:8 LXX "ποτήριον ἐν χειρὶ κυρίου οἴνου ἀκράτου πλῆρες κεράσματος" (cup-in-YHWH's-hand full-of-unmixed-wine); (2) Isa 51:17, 22 LXX "τὸ ποτήριον τοῦ θυμοῦ" (the-cup-of-wrath) — Jerusalem drinks then wrath transferred to her persecutors; (3) Jer 25:15-28 LXX cup-of-wrath served to all-nations; (4) Ezk 23:31-34 cup-of-Samaria-Jerusalem judgment. Jesus drinks the cup his people deserved — substitutionary-judgment imagery re-confirmed at Gethsemane (Matt 26:39, 42 "πάτερ μου, εἰ δυνατόν, παρελθάτω ἀπ' ἐμοῦ τὸ ποτήριον τοῦτο"). Thematic-allusion — not a specific-verbatim-quote but a RICH OT-figure-cluster Matthew expects readers to hear.

MAT 20:28.notes:
FOUNDATIONAL CHRISTOLOGICAL SAYING. Three layers of OT background:
(1) Isa 53:10-12 LXX Servant-Song: "τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ" (his-soul/life, cf. Matt τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ); "παρεδόθη εἰς θάνατον"; "ἁμαρτίας πολλῶν ἀνήνεγκεν" (many-many ΠΟΛΛΩΝ-ΠΟΛΛΟΙΣ echoing ἀντὶ πολλῶν here); "ἐδικαίωσεν δίκαιον εὖ δουλεύοντα πολλοῖς". Matthew's λύτρον + ψυχή + πολλῶν = deliberate Servant-Song compression.
(2) Exo 21:30 LXX — λύτρα for a bull-goring-victim (ransom-price paid by owner).
(3) Num 18:15-16 LXX — λύτρον for firstborn-redemption (5 shekels).
(4) Ps 49:8 LXX "τίς δώσει ἐξίλασμα τῇ ψυχῇ αὐτοῦ" (who-will-give-ransom-for-his-soul) — rhetorical-impossibility: a human cannot pay-ransom for his brother.
λύτρον only 2x NT (here + Mark 10:45 verbatim). ἀντί = SUBSTITUTIONARY-preposition (in-place-of, not just ὑπέρ on-behalf-of) — cornerstone of Protestant penal-substitutionary-atonement doctrine. "Many" (πολλῶν) is the Servant-Song corporate-beneficiary marker, not a limitation (cf. ὁ πολύς Semitic inclusive-idiom).

MAT 20:30.notes: Υἱὸς Δαυίδ = Davidic-Messiah vocative rooted in: (1) 2 Sam 7:12-13 LXX Davidic-covenant promise; (2) Isa 11:1-10 LXX shoot-from-stump-of-Jesse oracle; (3) Jer 23:5-6 LXX righteous-branch-of-David; (4) Ps 89:3-4 LXX covenant-with-David-established-forever. The two blind-men publicly confess Jesus as Davidic-Messiah — the same confession made earlier by Canaanite-woman (Matt 15:22) but here in RUN-UP to Jerusalem triumphal-entry (21:9 "Ὡσαννὰ τῷ υἱῷ Δαυίδ"). Irony: the blind SEE Messianic-identity; the sighted crowd rebukes them (v.31). Repeated at v.31. Thematic-allusion.

MAT 21:13.greek_matches: LXX (Isa verbatim minus πᾶσιν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν; Jer as allusive-embedding)
MAT 21:13.notes: Isa 56:7 LXX ὁ οἶκός μου οἶκος προσευχῆς κληθήσεται — Matthew drops LXX πᾶσιν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν (for all nations); Mark 11:17 retains it. Isa 56 is universal-invitation passage — all peoples welcomed to temple-prayer; Matthew's omission doesn't cancel but compresses. Second half adapts Jer 7:11 LXX μὴ σπήλαιον λῃστῶν ὁ οἶκός μου — Jer 7 is famous Temple-Sermon denouncing temple-as-false-refuge. Jesus's composite-citation implicitly threatens temple-destruction (Jer 7 → exile) while calling back to temple-purpose (Isa 56 → universal prayer). Christological: Jesus speaks as YHWH ("my house"). Quote-nesting: outer « » Jesus-speech, inner ‹ › Isa 56 citation.

MAT 21:16.greek_matches: LXX (= Ps 8:3 MT; Matthew follows LXX κατηρτίσω αἶνον against MT יִסַּדְתָּ־עֹז established-strength)
MAT 21:16.notes: CHRISTOLOGICAL HIGH-WATERMARK. Jesus applies to himself a Psalm-verse originally addressed to YHWH by the Psalmist. Ps 8 celebrates Creator-God whose-praise is proclaimed by infants; Jesus legitimizes children's Hosanna-to-Son-of-David by citing this psalm — IMPLYING that the praise rightly belongs to him AS GOD. Matthew-specific-divergence from MT: Matthew's αἶνος (praise) follows LXX; MT has עֹז (strength-citadel). Per NT usage, LXX-form fits Christian-application of praise-legitimation better. Quote-block: « » outer Jesus-reply, inner ‹ › Ps 8 citation.

MAT 21:32.notes: Prov 8:20 LXX ἐν ὁδοῖς δικαιοσύνης περιπατῶ (Wisdom walks in ways-of-righteousness); Prov 16:31 LXX ὁδὸς δικαιοσύνης (way-of-righteousness). Matthew's ἐν ὁδῷ δικαιοσύνης describes John's prophetic-calling — OT Wisdom-Literature idiom for righteous-life. Not direct-citation but idiomatic-echo from Proverbs.

MAT 21:33.greek_matches: LXX (verbatim vineyard-construction-vocabulary: ἐφύτευσεν ἀμπελῶνα, φραγμόν, ληνόν, πύργον)
MAT 21:33.notes: Parable of Wicked Tenants opens with direct-verbal-echoes of Isaiah's Vineyard-Song (Isa 5:1-7). Every Greek noun matches LXX-Isaiah exactly: φυτεύω + ἀμπελών, φραγμός περιτίθημι, ληνὸν ὀρύσσω, πύργον οἰκοδομέω. Hearers would recognize Isaiah's framework immediately — Isaiah 5 indicts Israel for bad-grapes-from-good-vineyard; Jesus's parable redirects the indictment from the vineyard itself (Isa) to its TENANTS (priests/leaders). Matthean redactional-shift of Isaianic-judgment-tradition. Sets up v.43 pronouncement that kingdom will be transferred ἔθνει.

MAT 21:34.notes: Isa 5:2 LXX ἤλπιζεν ἵνα ποιήσῃ σταφυλήν (expected-to-produce grapes). Matthew's owner-sending-slaves to collect fruit (καρποὶ ἀπό) echoes Isaianic vineyard-harvest-expectation. Linked with MAT 21:33 (main Isa 5:1-2 allusion) but v.34-specific expectation-to-receive-fruit. Not separate citation — extension of 21:33 allusion-frame.

MAT 21:42.notes: CHRISTOLOGICAL HIGH-WATERMARK. Jesus identifies himself as the rejected-stone-become-cornerstone. SAME Psalm 118 whose v.26 the crowds quoted at v.9 — closed-Christological-loop for the chapter: (a) entering Messiah is blessed-one (Ps 118:26, v.9), (b) rejected-stone becomes cornerstone (Ps 118:22-23, v.42). Ps 118 is HALLEL (Passover psalm). Original referent likely Israel-as-nation-rejected-by-superpowers-but-vindicated-by-YHWH; Jesus reapplies individually: himself as rejected-by-builders (= chief priests), vindicated-by-God. NT re-use widespread: Acts 4:11, 1 Pet 2:7, Rom 9:33 (partial). Stone-metaphor preserved per uW figs-metaphor. Christological center: death-and-resurrection are Jesus's rejection-and-vindication.

MAT 21:44.notes: Double-image stone-judgment: (1) ISA 8:14-15 LXX stone-of-stumbling λίθου προσκόμματι over which Israel-will-fall-and-be-shattered (συντριβήσονται); Matthew's συνθλασθήσεται cognate-violence. (2) DAN 2:34-35, 44-45 stone cut-from-mountain-without-hands that STRIKES the-statue (representing earthly-kingdoms) and grinds-it-to-chaff (λικμήσει echoes Daniel's grinding-chaff-motif). Combined: Jesus is both stumbling-stone (those who reject him fall-and-shatter, Isa) and judging-stone (at eschaton falls-on-nations-and-crushes, Dan). TEXTUAL NOTE: v.44 is INCLUSION-VARIANT — SBLGNT/NA28/BSB INCLUDE (supported by ℵ, B, C, L, W, Z, majority MSS); Western-text D + OL + Syriac OMIT (probably accidental homoioteleuton). Per uW and mainstream-critical-consensus, include without brackets.

MAT 21:5.notes: Opens with verbatim Isa 62:11 LXX εἴπατε τῇ θυγατρὶ Σιών, continues with Zech 9:9 LXX for king-on-donkey. Matthew drops LXX's "Rejoice greatly, daughter of Zion; shout, daughter of Jerusalem" and "righteous and saving" — compressed for narrative-flow. πραΰς preserved from LXX (MT עָנִי afflicted/humble); ἐπιβεβηκώς retained. The poetic-parallelism of one-animal (donkey + colt = poetic synonyms in Hebrew) Matthew reads as TWO actual animals (v.2, 7), distinctive-Matthean-exegesis. Composite-citation confirms Matthean-method of blending-prophetic-sources.

MAT 21:8.notes: 2 Kings 9:13 LXX: Israelites spread their garments (ἱμάτια) under Jehu as he was anointed king-of-Israel by Elisha's messenger. Matthew's crowd-gesture with spread-cloaks for Jesus echoes this royal-anointing-scene. Not a verbal-citation but cultural-gesture-parallel: royal acclamation via garment-spreading.

MAT 21:9.greek_matches: LXX (verbatim εὐλογημένος ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἐν ὀνόματι κυρίου)
MAT 21:9.notes: Crowd's Hallel-acclamation as Jesus enters Jerusalem. Ps 118 is the final Hallel-psalm sung at Passover (Pss 113-118). Originally pilgrim-welcome-formula; crowds apply to Jesus as ὁ ἐρχόμενος (the coming-one = Messianic title, cf. Matt 11:3). Combined with Hosanna (transliteration of Heb הוֹשִׁיעָה־נָּא "save now") and υἱῷ Δαυίδ Messianic-title, crowd affirms Jesus as Davidic-Messiah. Quote-block inside crowd-speech.

MAT 22:21.notes: Jesus's εἰκών-argument implicitly leverages GEN 1:26-27 LXX κατ' εἰκόνα theological-anthropology. The coin bears Caesar's εἰκών, so render it to Caesar; but humans bear God's εἰκών, so render THEMSELVES to God. The theological-depth is not on the surface but embedded — Jesus plays on εἰκών-as-ownership-marker, a point scribal hearers would have caught. Second-temple Jewish use of GEN 1:26-27 in ethical-political argumentation attested in rabbinic sources (m.Sanh 4:5: each human bears divine-image).

MAT 22:24.greek_matches: LXX (DEU 25:5-6 levirate-law + GEN 38:8 Onan's σπέρμα-ἀνίστημι phrase)
MAT 22:24.notes: Sadducees' paraphrase-summary of Mosaic levirate-law. Primary source DEU 25:5-6 LXX establishes the institution (brother marries widow for sake of deceased-brother's-name-continuation); secondary echo GEN 38:8 LXX (Judah to Onan: ἀνάστησον σπέρμα τῷ ἀδελφῷ σου = raise up seed for your brother — verbatim phrase Sadducees use here). Sadducees cite Torah since they rejected authority of Prophets+Writings — strategic use of their-accepted-canon.

MAT 22:32.greek_matches: LXX verbatim (EXO 3:6 LXX: ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ θεὸς τοῦ πατρός σου, θεὸς Αβρααμ καὶ θεὸς Ισαακ καὶ θεὸς Ιακωβ)
MAT 22:32.notes: KEY EXEGETICAL CRUX. Jesus's proof-of-resurrection from Pentateuch (Sadducees' accepted canon). Argument hinges on PRESENT-TENSE ἐγώ εἰμι spoken to Moses ~500 years after patriarchs died. If they ceased to exist at death, God could not be in ongoing covenantal relationship with them. Resurrection (not mere soul-immortality) required because covenant was with whole person. Rabbinic argument-from-verb-tense (qal vaḥomer-style inference) impressed crowds (v.33). Matthew's quotation uses singular θεός per ὁ θεὸς Ἀβραὰμ καὶ ὁ θεὸς Ἰσαὰκ καὶ ὁ θεὸς Ἰακώβ, triple-repetition-pattern standard in LXX EXO 3:6, 3:15, 3:16.

MAT 22:37.greek_matches: LXX (with Matthean-διάνοια variation from LXX δυνάμεως or διανοίας depending on MS)
MAT 22:37.notes: The Shema (DEU 6:4-9) foundational Jewish-daily-confession. LXX DEU 6:5 MS tradition: some MSS have καρδία/ψυχή/δύναμις (heart/soul/strength, matching MT לבב/נפש/מאד); other MSS have διανοία (mind). Matthew has καρδία/ψυχή/διάνοια three-term (Mark 12:30 has four-term including ἰσχύς; Luke 10:27 also four-term).
