2CO 7:6.notes: Echo of LXX Isa 49:13 'ἠλέησεν ὁ θεὸς τὸν λαὸν αὐτοῦ καὶ τοὺς ταπεινοὺς τοῦ λαοῦ αὐτοῦ παρεκάλεσεν' (God had mercy on his people and comforted the lowly among them). Pauline-application: God's-comfort-of-the-downcast manifest through Titus's arrival.

2CO 8:15.notes: Direct quotation of LXX Exod 16:18. Greek 'Ὁ τὸ πολὺ οὐκ ἐπλεόνασεν, καὶ ὁ τὸ ὀλίγον οὐκ ἠλαττόνησεν' adapts the first clause’s word order and substitutes ὀλίγον for Rahlfs’s ἔλαττον. Original context: manna-equality miracle in wilderness — those who gathered much had no excess; those who gathered little had no shortage. Pauline-application: God-orchestrated-economic-equity through community-giving.

2CO 8:21.notes: Pauline-allusion to LXX Prov 3:4 'προνοοῦ καλὰ ἐνώπιον κυρίου καὶ ἀνθρώπων' (take thought for what is good before the Lord and people). Pauline-double-accountability principle for financial-administration.

2CO 9:7.notes: The Greek addition at Proverbs 22:8a says God blesses a cheerful giver. Paul condenses the description of the giver and says that God loves such a person. This addition is absent from the Hebrew text underlying Thai Proverbs. The comparison is recorded in the citation registry.

2CO 9:9.notes: Direct quotation of LXX Ps 111:9 (= MT/Hebrew Ps 112:9). Greek 'Ἐσκόρπισεν, ἔδωκεν τοῖς πένησιν, ἡ δικαιοσύνη αὐτοῦ μένει εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα' follows Rahlfs through αἰῶνα, where Paul stops; the psalm continues τοῦ αἰῶνος. Original-context: the righteous-man who fears the Lord and gives to the poor — his righteousness endures forever. Pauline-application: God-empowered-generosity produces lasting-righteousness.

2CO 9:10.notes: Composite allusion: 'supplies seed to the sower and bread for food' echoes LXX Isa 55:10 (the rain-and-seed-and-bread-for-food provision). 'increase the harvest of your righteousness' echoes LXX Hos 10:12 (σπείρατε ἑαυτοῖς εἰς δικαιοσύνην, τρυγήσατε εἰς καρπὸν ζωῆς — 'sow for yourselves righteousness, reap fruit-of-life'). Hosea’s closing words, γενήματα δικαιοσύνης ὑμῖν, are especially close to Paul’s τὰ γενήματα τῆς δικαιοσύνης ὑμῶν. Pauline-OT-imagery cluster for divine-provision and harvest-of-righteousness.

2CO 10:17.notes: Pauline-paraphrase of Jer 9:23 in Rahlfs and Hebrew (9:24 in common English numbering): 'ἐν τούτῳ καυχάσθω ὁ καυχώμενος, συνίειν καὶ γινώσκειν...'. Paul abbreviates 'ἐν τούτῳ' to 'ἐν κυρίῳ' for direct-Christological-application. Same OT-quote Paul cites at 1 Co 1:31. Pauline-anti-self-boasting principle.

2CO 10:18.notes: Pauline-conceptual-echo of 1 Sam 16:7 ('the Lord looks at the heart' — God's evaluation differs from human-self-evaluation). Pauline-aphorism: only divine-commendation counts as approval.

2CO 11:3.notes: Pauline-allusion to Genesis 3 narrative — serpent deceiving Eve through cunning. Pauline-typology: rival-apostles' deceptive-rhetoric parallels the serpent's deception of Eve. ψευδαπόστολοι at v.13 → satanic-pattern-mimicry continues at vv.14-15 (Satan as angel-of-light).

2CO 11:24.notes: Paul reports five occasions on which he received forty lashes less one. Deuteronomy 25:3 sets an upper limit of forty. The later Mishnah (Makkot 3:10) attests the forty-less-one interpretation. Paul gives no location for these five punishments.

2CO 13:1.notes: Paul quotes Deuteronomy 19:15. The Greek law repeats “on the mouth of” and “witnesses” with the second number. Paul shortens that repetition, retains καί and uses the future σταθήσεται. Matthew 18:16 has “or” and a subjunctive in its purpose clause. First Timothy 5:19 gives a shorter witness requirement. The citation is registered.

ROM 1:17.notes: The citation from Habakkuk 2:4 has no possessive with “faith” in Romans 1:17 or Galatians 3:11. Thai โดยความเชื่อ likewise leaves the possessor unstated. In Rahlfs Greek Habakkuk μου follows πίστεως (“my faithfulness”). In Hebrew Habakkuk the suffix means “his.” In Hebrews 10:38 μου follows δίκαιος (“my righteous one”). These texts establish differences in wording while leaving open which exemplar Paul used.

ROM 1:23.notes: Lexical echo of Psalm 106:20 LXX (Ps 105:20 LXX): καὶ ἠλλάξαντο τὴν δόξαν αὐτῶν ἐν ὁμοιώματι μόσχου ἔσθοντος χόρτον (golden-calf incident). Paul reuses ἀλλάσσω + δόξα + ἐν ὁμοιώματι. Secondary echo of Jer 2:11 LXX: ὁ δὲ λαός μου ἠλλάξαντο τὴν δόξαν αὐτοῦ. Paul universalizes Israel's golden-calf idolatry-pattern to all humanity — this is the move that makes ch.1 a universal-condemnation argument grounded in OT precedent.

ROM 2:6.notes: Paraphrase combining Psalm 62:13 LXX (Ps 61:13: σὺ ἀποδώσεις ἑκάστῳ κατὰ τὰ ἔργα αὐτοῦ) and Proverbs 24:12 LXX (ὃς ἀποδίδωσιν ἑκάστῳ κατὰ τὰ ἔργα αὐτοῦ). The same OT principle appears at Mat 16:27, 2 Tim 4:14, Rev 2:23, 22:12. Paul uses it as the foundation of impartial-judgment (vv.6-11). BSB English brackets it with quotation marks even though Paul does not introduce it with γέγραπται.

ROM 2:24.notes: Direct quotation of Isaiah 52:5 LXX (τὸ ὄνομά μου δι' ὑμᾶς διὰ παντὸς βλασφημεῖται ἐν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν), introduced by καθὼς γέγραπται postpositive. Paul adapts: (1) shifts μου ('my name') to τοῦ θεοῦ ('God's name') for diatribe-third-person framing; (2) drops διὰ παντός ('continually'). Theological move: in Isa 52:5 the Gentile-blasphemy concerns Israel's-suffering; in Paul, the blasphemy is BECAUSE-OF Israel's-hypocrisy — Paul universalizes/inverts.

ROM 2:29.notes: Paul uses the noun phrase περιτομὴ καρδίας, “circumcision of the heart.” Greek Deuteronomy 10:16 and Jeremiah 4:4 speak of circumcising hardness of heart. In Hebrew Deuteronomy 30:6 the LORD circumcises the heart, while the Greek says he will cleanse it. These are related images with different wording. โดยพระวิญญาณ interprets ἐν πνεύματι as referring to the Spirit, supported by the contrast with letter. The absence of an article does not settle this by itself.

ROM 2:15.notes: The object described as written in their hearts is τὸ ἔργον τοῦ νόμου, “the work of the law,” งานของธรรมบัญญัติ. Conscience bears witness and thoughts accuse or defend. Jeremiah 31:33 (Greek 38:33) promises that God will write his law on the heart. The imagery permits comparison, but the objects and settings differ. Romans does not explicitly identify an inversion or fulfillment of Jeremiah’s promise.

ROM 2:19.notes: Possible-allusion to Isaiah 42:6 (δέδωκά σε εἰς διαθήκην γένους εἰς φῶς ἐθνῶν) + Isaiah 49:6 (τέθεικά σε εἰς φῶς ἐθνῶν). The 'guide-for-blind / light-for-those-in-darkness' formula echoes Isaiah's servant-as-light-to-nations theme. Paul lists this as the JEWISH SELF-CONCEPTION which vv.21-24 will challenge as failing in practice.

ROM 3:4.notes: Direct quote of Psalm 51:4 LXX (Ps 50:6 LXX), introduced by καθὼς γέγραπται. David's confession after Bathsheba (Ps 51 superscription). Paul cites the LXX-form (which differs slightly from Hebrew MT). Used by Paul to argue that God is JUST in judging the sinner — even when human-unfaithfulness is the object of judgment.

ROM 3:10.notes: The opening of the chain recalls Psalms 14 and 53 (Greek 13 and 52). Ecclesiastes 7:20 also speaks of a righteous person, with its own qualification about doing good without sinning. Romans 3:10 gives a shorter universal negative. The Thai closes this opening quotation after verse 12. In the Rahlfs text of Psalm 13 an expansion after verse 3 parallels the later part of Paul’s chain. That parallel by itself does not identify an earlier collection or the direction of borrowing.

ROM 3:11.notes: Greek Psalm 13:2 has κύριος, the Lord, looking down from heaven. The parallel in Greek Psalm 52:3 has ὁ θεός, God. Both ask whether anyone understands or seeks God. Paul gives two negative statements and Thai repeats ไม่มีผู้. The parallels are Psalm 14:2 and Psalm 53:3 in the Hebrew numbering.

ROM 3:12.notes: Greek Psalm 13:3 and the parallel at 52:4 describe all turning aside and no one doing good. The Thai closes the first quotation after ไม่มีแม้แต่คนเดียว.

ROM 3:13.notes: The throat and tongue lines excerpt part of Greek Psalm 5:10 (Thai 5:10, common English 5:9). Earlier clauses of the psalm verse are outside the excerpt. The venom under the lips comes from Greek Psalm 139:4 (Thai 140:4, common English 140:3). Thai marks these as two separate quotations.

ROM 3:14.notes: Greek Psalm 9:28 (Thai and common English 10:7) speaks of an individual and includes deceit. Romans uses a plural relative, changes the order and retains cursing and bitterness. ปากของพวกเขา represents the plural reference.

ROM 3:15.notes: Begins Isaiah-segment of catena: Isaiah 59:7 LXX (οἱ δὲ πόδες αὐτῶν ἐπὶ πονηρίαν τρέχουσιν ταχινοὶ ἐκχέαι αἷμα). Paul condenses: ταχινοί → ὀξεῖς (synonym 'sharp/swift'). Possible secondary echo of Proverbs 1:16 LXX (same Hebrew-MT origin). Body-progression continues: feet.

ROM 3:16.notes: Isaiah-segment continues: Isaiah 59:7c LXX — exact-quote: σύντριμμα καὶ ταλαιπωρία ἐν ταῖς ὁδοῖς αὐτῶν.

ROM 3:17.notes: Closes Isaiah-segment: Isaiah 59:8a LXX (ὁδὸν εἰρήνης οὐκ οἴδασιν). Paul: aorist ἔγνωσαν (vs LXX-perfect οἴδασιν) — same sense.

ROM 3:18.notes: Greek Psalm 35:2 (Thai 36:2, common English 36:1) speaks of “his eyes.” Romans has plural αὐτῶν, reflected in ดวงตาของพวกเขา. This closes the scriptural chain.

ROM 3:20.notes: Paul echoes Greek Psalm 142:2 (Psalm 143:2), where no living person will be justified before God. Paul says “no flesh” and adds “from works of law.” The future passive is expressed by จะถูกประกาศว่าชอบธรรม. Compare the no-flesh and works-of-law wording of Galatians 2:16. Galatians 3:11 quotes Habakkuk 2:4.

ROM 3:29.notes: Echoes the Shema (Deut 6:4 LXX: ἄκουε Ισραηλ κύριος ὁ θεὸς ἡμῶν κύριος εἷς ἐστιν). Paul appeals to monotheism — 'God is one' — as the basis for arguing that God justifies BOTH Jews and Gentiles by the same faith. Same Shema-echo used by Paul at v.30 (εἷς ὁ θεός), Gal 3:20, 1 Cor 8:6, 1 Tim 2:5.

ROM 4:3.notes: FOUNDATIONAL TEXT for Pauline-justification-by-faith. Genesis 15:6 LXX (καὶ ἐπίστευσεν Αβραμ τῷ θεῷ καὶ ἐλογίσθη αὐτῷ εἰς δικαιοσύνην) — Paul-exact-quote. Repeated at Rom 4:9 (paraphrase), 4:22 (verbatim); Gal 3:6 (verbatim); Jas 2:23 (verbatim, with opposite-emphasis). The single most important OT-text for Pauline-justification-doctrine. λογίζομαι 'reckon/credit' is the chapter's-theme-verb.

ROM 4:7.notes: Direct quote of Psalm 32:1 LXX (Ps 31:1 LXX). David's-blessedness-of-forgiven. Paul cites David alongside Abraham as second-OT-witness to justification-by-faith (rabbinic two-witnesses-method).

ROM 4:8.notes: Continuation of Ps 32 quote (v.7). Direct quote of Psalm 32:2 LXX (Ps 31:2 LXX). λογίσηται aorist-subjunctive 'NOT-count' — connects David's-imagery to the chapter's λογίζομαι theme.

ROM 4:9.notes: Paul-paraphrase of Gen 15:6 (cf v.3). Same-text in re-deployed-form: 'faith-was-credited-to-Abraham-as-righteousness.' Sets up the WHEN question (vv.10-12).

ROM 4:17.notes: Direct quote of Genesis 17:5 LXX (πατέρα πολλῶν ἐθνῶν τέθεικά σε). God's-renaming-of-Abram-to-Abraham (Heb 'av-hamon = father-of-multitudes). Paul reads ἐθνῶν as 'NATIONS / GENTILES' for the universal-fatherhood claim. The Gen 17 chapter ALSO contains the circumcision-mandate; Paul deliberately cites the FATHERHOOD-promise (v.5) AHEAD-OF the circumcision-commandment to confirm the chronological-priority of faith.

ROM 4:18.notes: Direct quote of Genesis 15:5 LXX (Οὕτως ἔσται τὸ σπέρμα σου). God's-promise-to-Abraham about offspring numerous-as-stars. Same Gen 15 chapter as the foundational-v.6-citation. Abraham's hope-against-hope is the paradigm of Christian-resurrection-faith.

ROM 4:22.notes: The selected διό is expressed by เพราะฉะนั้น. The WH main text, Tregelles, NA28 and RP also include καί. Paul repeats the reckoning clause of Genesis 15:6, already quoted in 4:3, and applies it to Abraham. The complete Genesis verse also speaks of his believing.

ROM 7:7.notes: Direct quote of the 10th commandment (Exodus 20:17 LXX / Deuteronomy 5:21 LXX). Paul cites the BARE prohibition (οὐκ ἐπιθυμήσεις 'do not covet') without the explicit objects ('your neighbor's house, wife, etc.') — universalizing the prohibition to inner-desire-as-such. The 10th commandment is the only Decalogue-commandment whose violation can be entirely-internal (as opposed to outwardly-observable acts), making it Paul's chosen exemplar for Law's-revelatory-function: exposing inner-sin.

ROM 7:11.notes: Paul says sin deceived him, ἐξηπάτησέν με. In Greek Genesis 3:13 Eve says the serpent deceived her, ἠπάτησέν με. The verbs are related, with the prefix ἐξ- in Romans and the same first-person object in both. The verbal echo alone does not identify Paul’s speaker with Adam or Eve.

ROM 8:32.notes: OT-ECHO of Genesis 22:16 LXX (Akedah/binding-of-Isaac): οὐκ ἐφείσω τοῦ υἱοῦ σου τοῦ ἀγαπητοῦ. Profound-typology: where Abraham was permitted-to-spare-Isaac, God-the-Father did-NOT-spare-the-Son. Paul reuses φείδομαι in same-construction. The Akedah is the OT-typological-mirror of the Cross.

ROM 8:33.notes: Echoes Isaiah 50:8 LXX (Servant's-confidence: τίς ὁ κρινόμενός μοι ... ὁ δικαιῶν με). Paul applies the Servant's-individual-confidence to the corporate-elect. Same δικαιόω verb, courtroom-vindication setting.

ROM 8:36.notes: Direct quote of Psalm 44:22 LXX (Ps 43:23 LXX): Ἕνεκεν σοῦ θανατούμεθα ὅλην τὴν ἡμέραν, ἐλογίσθημεν ὡς πρόβατα σφαγῆς — Paul-exact-quote. The Psalm is a corporate-Israel-lament under-persecution; Paul applies-corporate-Christian. Sets up the seven-fold-suffering catalog of v.35 within the OT-Psalmist's-suffering-tradition.

ROM 8:34.notes: Echoes Psalm 110:1 LXX (Ps 109:1 LXX) — Christ-at-God's-right-hand. The most-quoted-OT-text in the NT (cf Mat 22:44; Mark 12:36; Luke 20:42; Acts 2:34-35; Heb 1:13). Pauline-application: enthroned-Christ-as-intercessor.

ROM 8:20.notes: Echo of Genesis 3:17-19's creation-curse (the ground 'cursed because of you'; thorns and thistles; creation's-frustration). Paul universalizes the Edenic-curse: ALL creation was subjected to ματαιότης ('futility') — not by its own choice, but because-of-the-Subjector (= God, mainstream-evangelical reading). Paul reads creation's-cursed-state as temporary, oriented-toward-eschatological-restoration (v.21).

ROM 9:7.notes: Direct quote of Genesis 21:12 LXX — God's word that 'through Isaac' the line of promise will be established. The first OT-precedent for election-within-election: Abraham had Ishmael, but God elected Isaac as the line.

ROM 9:9.notes: Paul conflates Genesis 18:10 + 18:14 LXX — God's promise to Abraham about Sarah's miraculous conception of Isaac. Paul cites the promise to ground the 'children of promise' category in Sarah's-supernatural-conception.

ROM 9:12.notes: Direct quote of Genesis 25:23 LXX — God's pre-natal prophecy to Rebecca about Esau and Jacob ('the older shall serve the younger'). Foundational text for unconditional-election: spoken before the twins were born or had done good or evil.

ROM 9:13.notes: Direct quote of Malachi 1:2-3 LXX. God's-retrospective-statement (post-Israel/Edom-history). Hebraic-comparative ('loved-more / preferred-not') translated by LXX into strong-Greek-form ἀγαπάω/μισέω. Paul cites the strong form — God's electing-love vs Esau's-non-election.

ROM 9:15.notes: Direct quote of Exodus 33:19 LXX. God-to-Moses after the golden-calf incident. Foundational sovereign-mercy formula. Used by Paul as proof-text for unconditional-mercy (= mercy not contingent on human merit).

ROM 9:17.notes: Paul personifies Scripture as speaking to Pharaoh, พระคัมภีร์กล่าว. Within the quotation God speaks as “I.” Romans has active ἐξήγειρά σε, “I raised you up,” where Greek Exodus 9:16 has passive διετηρήθης, “you were preserved.” The first purpose clause uses ὅπως and δύναμις in Romans where Greek Exodus has ἵνα and ἰσχύς. The second purpose, proclamation of God’s name throughout the earth, corresponds closely.

ROM 9:20.notes: Greek Isaiah 29:16 supplies the image and wording of a formed object addressing the one who formed it. Isaiah 45:9 asks a related question about clay and the potter. Romans turns from the language of forming to the verb for making in its question “Why did you make me like this?” The Thai similarly moves from ปั้น to สร้าง.

ROM 9:25.notes: Direct quote of Hosea 2:23 LXX (Hos 2:25 LXX) — God's promise of restoration: 'I will call those who were not my people, my people.' In Hosea-context, the unfaithful-Israel restored. Paul-bold-application: extends to Gentile-inclusion.

ROM 9:26.notes: Direct quote of Hosea 1:10 LXX (Hos 2:1 LXX). The 'sons of the living God' — restored-status of Hosea's-rejected-children, applied corporately. Paired with v.25's Hos 2:23 quote for the Gentile-inclusion warrant.

ROM 9:27.notes: Romans adapts Greek Isaiah 10:22. Paul speaks of the number of Israel’s sons and uses ὑπόλειμμα for the remnant where Greek Isaiah has κατάλειμμα. Both speak of a remnant being saved.

ROM 9:28.notes: Paul condenses the wording of Greek Isaiah 10:22–23 about completing and cutting short the matter. Romans has κύριος on the earth, where Greek Isaiah has God’s title and refers to the whole inhabited world. The wording of the citation varies within Romans as well.

ROM 9:29.notes: Romans follows the Greek of Isaiah 1:9 closely in naming the Lord Sabaoth and the seed left to us. Thai Romans has จอมทัพ and เชื้อสาย, while Thai Isaiah has จอมโยธา and ผู้รอดชีวิต, reflecting its own source.

ROM 9:33.notes: Romans combines Zion and believing from Isaiah 28:16 with the stumbling stone and rock of offense from Isaiah 8:14 in a single saying. First Peter 2:6–8 also draws on both Isaiah passages, but quotes them separately with Psalm 118:22 between them. The two authors use related material in different arrangements.

ROM 9:3.notes: Echoes Exodus 32:32 LXX — Moses' offer to be 'blotted-out' from God's book for Israel's-sake after the golden-calf incident. Paul echoes Moses' shepherd-heart in his ἀνάθεμα-wish: willing to be cursed for the sake of his Jewish kinsmen. Hyperbolic-rhetorical, not literally-attainable, but conveys the depth of pastoral-love.

ROM 10:5.notes: In the selected Greek the person practicing the righteousness that comes from law will live by it. The final feminine singular αὐτῇ refers back to righteousness. WH also has the singular. NA28 and RP explicitly say “do them” and “live by them,” resembling Greek Leviticus 18:5. The Thai now expresses the singular reading.

ROM 10:6.notes: “Do not say in your heart” echoes Deuteronomy 9:4. The question about ascending to heaven draws on 30:12. Paul relates it to bringing Christ down. The Thai marks the speech of righteousness with single quotation marks and the question inside it with double quotation marks.

ROM 10:7.notes: Deuteronomy 30:13 asks about crossing the sea. Romans asks about descending into the abyss and explains it in terms of bringing Christ up from the dead.

ROM 10:8.notes: Deuteronomy 30:14 places the word very near, in the mouth and heart. The Greek of Deuteronomy also mentions the hands and doing it. Romans retains the word’s nearness, mouth and heart, and identifies it with the message of faith proclaimed.

ROM 10:11.notes: Re-cite of Isaiah 28:16 LXX (cf 9:33). Paul adds πᾶς ('every-one') to make universality-explicit, opening the door for v.12's Jew-Gentile-equality-statement.

ROM 10:13.notes: Direct quote of Joel 2:32 LXX (Joel 3:5 LXX). The κύριος in Joel-LXX = YHWH; Paul applies it Christologically (continuous with v.9's κύριον Ἰησοῦν) — Christ-as-κύριος receives the prayer-formerly-directed-to-YHWH. Foundation-text for Christian-prayer-to-Jesus. Acts 2:21 cites the same Joel passage with same Christological application.

ROM 10:15.notes: Direct quote (compressed) of Isaiah 52:7 LXX. Original-LXX has 'feet-of-the-one-bringing-good-news-of-peace, the-one-bringing-good-news-of-good-things'; Paul condenses to 'feet-of-good-news-bringers.' The famous-feet-of-evangelists text. Foundational-mission-text.

ROM 10:16.notes: Direct quote of Isaiah 53:1 LXX. The opening of the famous-suffering-servant-passage. Paul applies Isaiah's-lament about-Israel's-unbelief in the gospel-message. The ἀκοή ('what-is-heard / message') becomes the gospel-report.

ROM 10:18.notes: Direct quote of Psalm 19:4 LXX (Ps 18:5 LXX). Originally about creation-as-universal-witness; Paul re-applies to gospel's-universal-proclamation. Pauline-creative-application of natural-revelation Psalm to special-revelation gospel-spread.

ROM 10:19.notes: Direct quote of Deuteronomy 32:21 LXX (Moses' Song-of-witness). God's prophetic-warning that-disobedient-Israel will-be-provoked-to-jealousy by-a-no-people. Paul applies: Gentile-conversion is the means-of-Israel's-jealousy. Theme developed in ch.11.

ROM 10:20.notes: Direct quote of Isaiah 65:1 LXX. God-revealed-himself-to-those-not-seeking — Pauline-application: Gentile-conversion. Paul calls Isaiah's-statement ἀποτολμάω 'bold-speech' (NT-HAPAX) — provocative-prophetic-revelation.

ROM 10:21.notes: Direct quote of Isaiah 65:2 LXX. God's-pleading-posture toward-unfaithful-Israel ('all-day-stretched-out-hands'). Closes ROM 10 with divine-pathos that prepares-for-ch.11's-restoration-question. Counter-balances v.20's Gentile-find-by-non-seekers with v.21's Israel-rejection-of-pleading-God.

ROM 11:3.notes: Elijah speaks of the prophets before the altars here. In the Septuagint (LXX), 1 Kings 19:10 and 14 put the altars first, mention the sword and describe the threat to his life in fuller wording. Paul condenses the complaint.

ROM 11:4.notes: Paul quotes God saying “I have kept for myself” seven thousand. Rahlfs Greek 1 Kings 19:18 reads καταλείψεις, second-person future active, “you will leave.” The Thai Kings text, like the Hebrew, has God speaking in the first person. The Thai Romans เราได้สงวนไว้สำหรับเราเอง reflects the first person and the explicit “for myself.”

ROM 11:8.notes: Composite-quotation fusing Deut 29:4 LXX + Isa 29:10 LXX. Both texts speak of Israel's-dulled-perception (eyes-not-seeing, ears-not-hearing). Paul fuses them to characterize Israel's-current-hardening.

ROM 11:9.notes: Direct quote of Psalm 69:22-23 LXX (Ps 68:23-24 LXX). Imprecatory-Psalm-of-David applied to Israel's-rejection. Four-fold catalog (snare/trap/stumbling/retribution) followed by darkened-eyes + bent-back in v.10.

ROM 11:10.notes: Continues Psalm 69:23 LXX (Ps 68:24 LXX). συγκάμπτω 'bend-down-with' is NT-HAPAX.

ROM 11:26.notes: Romans says the deliverer comes “from Zion,” จากศิโยน. Greek Isaiah 59:20 speaks of coming “on account of Zion.” The words about turning ungodliness from Jacob lead into the covenant language of Isaiah 59:21.

ROM 11:27.notes: The covenant wording recalls Isaiah 59:21. “When I take away their sins” recalls Greek Isaiah 27:9, where the sin is singular. Paul uses a plural with “their.” Greek Jeremiah 38:33–34 (Hebrew 31:33–34) also associates covenant and forgiveness but speaks of no longer remembering sins.

ROM 11:34.notes: Paul adapts the questions of Greek Isaiah 40:13. Isaiah joins them with καί, orders the adviser pronoun differently and continues with a clause about instructing the Lord. Romans uses ἤ, “or,” and ends with the question about his adviser. First Corinthians 2:16 retains the instruction question in its own form.

ROM 11:35.notes: The question about giving first and being repaid corresponds to Hebrew Job 41:3 (common English 41:11) and its Thai rendering. Greek Job 41:3 in Rahlfs asks about resisting and enduring. Romans shifts from God speaking as “I” to speaking about him. The Greek repayment verb is passive. Thai เพื่อพระองค์จะทรงตอบแทน expresses repayment with God as the agent.

ROM 11:1.notes: Echo of Psalm 94:14 LXX (Ps 93:14 LXX): οὐκ ἀπώσεται κύριος τὸν λαὸν αὐτοῦ ('the Lord will not cast off his people'). Paul's μὴ ἀπώσατο ὁ θεὸς τὸν λαὸν αὐτοῦ uses the same ἀπωθέω verb. Foundation-text for the 'God-has-not-rejected-Israel' argument of ROM 11.

ROM 11:11.notes: Echo of Deut 32:21 (Moses' Song; cited verbatim at 10:19) — the make-Israel-jealous theme. παραζηλόω here completes the strategy: Gentile-conversion provokes-Israel-to-jealousy, leading-to-eventual-restoration.

ROM 12:19.notes: Greek Deuteronomy 32:35 in Rahlfs reads “on a day of vengeance I will repay.” Romans and Hebrews 10:30 instead have “vengeance is mine” and an emphatic “I will repay.” Romans follows this with “says the Lord.” Hebrews presents the speaker as known and leaves the author of the letter unnamed.

ROM 12:20.notes: Direct quote of Proverbs 25:21-22 LXX. Feed-your-enemy + heap-burning-coals. The 'burning coals' metaphor is interpretively-debated: (1) shame-leading-to-repentance (Augustine, mainstream-evangelical); (2) divine-judgment-coals (minority); (3) Egyptian-ritual-of-repentance-carrying-burning-coals-on-head (some scholars). Most evangelical-readings favor (1).

ROM 12:16.notes: Echo of Proverbs 3:7 LXX 'be-not-wise-in-your-own-eyes.' Pauline-Wisdom-tradition-application to humility-imperative.

ROM 12:17.notes: Echo of Proverbs 20:22 LXX (do-not-say 'I-will-recompense-evil'). Combined with Pauline-Jesus-tradition-echo (Mat 5:38-39) — non-retaliation-ethics.

ROM 13:9.notes: The selected text lists adultery, murder, theft and coveting in the relative order of Greek Deuteronomy 5. Greek Exodus 20 places theft before murder. Both Greek law texts give objects for coveting, omitted here. The following love command draws on Leviticus 19:18. Thai อย่าลักทรัพย์ renders the prohibition of theft.

ROM 14:11.notes: Romans adapts Greek Isaiah 45:23 for every knee bowing and every tongue confessing to God. The oath “as I live, says the Lord” has a close verbal parallel in Greek Isaiah 49:18. Isaiah 45:23 itself uses different oath wording. Philippians 2:10–11 uses the knee and tongue imagery with a confession of Jesus as Lord. Romans says τῷ θεῷ, แด่พระเจ้า.

ROM 15:3.notes: Paul applies the reproach directed at God to Christ’s bearing it. The quoted clause occurs in Thai Psalm 69:10 and Greek Psalm 68:10. Common English numbering gives Psalm 69:9.

ROM 15:9.notes: The praise among the nations comes from Thai Psalm 18:50 (common English 18:49, Greek 17:50), also paralleled in 2 Samuel 22:50. Both Greek Old Testament parallels contain the vocative κύριε, omitted in Romans. In the second line the Psalm has the closer wording, whereas Greek 2 Samuel includes a preposition before the reference to the name.

ROM 15:10.notes: The exhortation to nations to rejoice with his people corresponds to the Greek clause in Deuteronomy 32:43, expressed here by จงชื่นชมยินดีร่วมกับชนชาติของพระองค์.

ROM 15:11.notes: Greek Psalm 116:1 (Psalm 117:1 in Hebrew and Thai) commands praise in the second person in both clauses. The selected Romans has third-person ἐπαινεσάτωσαν in the second clause, reflected in ให้ประชาชนทั้งสิ้น. RP has the psalm’s first-clause order and a second-person command in the second clause.

ROM 15:12.notes: Paul closes this sequence with Isaiah 11:10 in Greek: the root of Jesse will rule the nations, who will hope in him.

ROM 15:21.notes: The quotation closely follows the final clause of Greek Isaiah 52:15. Isaiah 52:13–15 opens the passage about the servant that continues into chapter 53. Paul applies the words about seeing and understanding to his work among those who have yet to hear.

ROM 16:20.notes: Romans has God crushing Satan under the believers’ feet, with συντρίψει. Greek Genesis 3:15 uses forms of τηρέω with head and heel. The Thai Genesis uses language of wounding. The shared imagery allows a thematic connection, but the two passages differ in verb, agent and recipient.

PHP 1:19.notes: Job 13:16 in Greek begins καὶ τοῦτό μοι ἀποβήσεται εἰς σωτηρίαν. Philippians has ὅτι after ‘I know.’ The shared wording begins with τοῦτό and ends with σωτηρίαν. Paul's confidence amid imprisonment recalls Job's hope of vindication.

PHP 2:10.notes: Isa 45:23 LXX 'ἐμοὶ κάμψει πᾶν γόνυ' — Paul deliberately applies to Christ what YHWH says of himself. Same OT-text Paul cites at Rom 14:11 (where it's directly attributed to κύριος). Pauline-Christological-application — high-Christology in confession-form. The κύριος-Ἰησοῦς-Χριστός confession in v.11 makes the divine-name-application explicit.

PHP 2:11.notes: In Greek Isaiah 45:23 God says ἐμοὶ κάμψει πᾶν γόνυ, followed by ἐξομολογήσεται πᾶσα γλῶσσα τῷ θεῷ. Romans 14:11 instead places πᾶσα γλῶσσα before ἐξομολογήσεται. Philippians 2:10–11 uses κάμψῃ and ἐξομολογήσηται under ἵνα and identifies what each tongue confesses: Jesus Christ is Lord.

PHP 2:15.notes: Greek Deuteronomy 32:5 uses the nominative γενεὰ σκολιὰ καὶ διεστραμμένη and describes blemished children (τέκνα μωμητά). Philippians uses genitives after μέσον and describes the believers as God's blameless children living among that generation.

PHP 3:21.notes: The subjection line occurs at Greek Psalm 8:7 (8:6 in common English numbering). The psalm addresses God and mentions the figure’s feet. Philippians uses an infinitive and says Christ can subject all things to himself. First Corinthians 15:27, Ephesians 1:22 and Hebrews 2:8 also take up the psalm's language of subjection.

PHP 4:18.notes: Greek Leviticus 1:9, 13 and 17 use the fragrant-aroma expression ὀσμὴ εὐωδίας. Paul applies that imagery to the Philippians' gift and describes it further as an acceptable sacrifice pleasing to God.

COL 1:6.notes: Lexical-cluster echo of LXX Gen 1:22, 28 'αὐξάνεσθε καὶ πληθύνεσθε' (be-fruitful-and-multiply) — the creation-blessing-mandate. Paul's pair καρποφορούμενον καὶ αὐξανόμενον (bearing-fruit + growing) deliberately echoes the Gen-creation-language but applied to the gospel-message itself. The thematic move: gospel = new-creation-vitality; the gospel's spread mirrors the original creation-blessing's spread. The same pair recurs at v.10 applied to the believer's life — believer-life-as-new-creation-organism. Allusion-not-citation: the lexical-pair αὐξάνω is one of the two Gen-creation-mandate verbs; πληθύνω is replaced by καρποφορέω in Paul's adaptation.

COL 2:22.notes: Echo of Isa 29:13 LXX 'διδάσκοντες ἐντάλματα ἀνθρώπων καὶ διδασκαλίας' (teaching commandments of men and doctrines). Paul's phrase 'τὰ ἐντάλματα καὶ διδασκαλίας τῶν ἀνθρώπων' borrows the same lexical-pair (ἐντάλματα ἀνθρώπων + διδασκαλίας) — the standard NT-anti-pharisaic borrowing. Same Isa 29:13 echo Jesus deploys at Mark 7:7 / Matt 15:9 against Pharisees-tradition. Pauline-application: against the Colossian-heretics' human-tradition-based asceticism.

COL 3:1.notes: Echo of Ps 110:1 LXX 'κάθου ἐκ δεξιῶν μου' (sit at my right hand) — the most-quoted OT verse in the NT. Paul's phrase 'ἐν δεξιᾷ τοῦ θεοῦ καθήμενος' (Christ seated at God's right hand) directly evokes the Ps 110:1 enthronement-language. Same pattern: Heb 1:13, Mark 12:36, Acts 2:34-35, Eph 1:20. Christological-application: the messianic enthronement is the present-state of Christ post-resurrection.

COL 3:10.notes: Echo of Gen 1:26-27 LXX 'κατ’ εἰκόνα ἡμετέραν' (in our image). Paul's 'κατ’ εἰκόνα τοῦ κτίσαντος αὐτόν' (in the image of the one who created him/it) borrows the same image-of-Creator language but applies it to NEW-CREATION: the new-self being recreated in the image of Christ-the-Creator (cf. COL 1:15 εἰκὼν τοῦ θεοῦ). Pauline-Christological adaptation of Gen-creation-anthropology to redeemed-humanity.

EPH 1:20.notes: Echo of Ps 110:1 LXX 'κάθου ἐκ δεξιῶν μου' (sit at my right hand). Paul's 'καθίσας ἐν δεξιᾷ αὐτοῦ ἐν τοῖς ἐπουρανίοις' borrows the seated-at-right-hand enthronement language. Same Christological-application as COL 3:1. The most-quoted OT verse in the NT — also at Heb 1:13, Mark 12:36, Acts 2:34-35.

EPH 1:22.notes: The underlying line is Greek Psalm 8:7 (8:6 in common English numbering). The psalm addresses God in the second person with ὑπέταξας and has ὑποκάτω with genitive feet. Ephesians has third-person ὑπέταξεν and ὑπό with accusative feet. First Corinthians 15:27 closely parallels this wording, and Philippians 3:21 shares the subjection theme.

EPH 1:11.notes: Echo of LXX Deut 32:9 'καὶ ἐγενήθη μερὶς κυρίου λαὸς αὐτοῦ Ιακωβ, σχοίνισμα κληρονομίας αὐτοῦ Ισραηλ' (the LORD's portion was his people; Jacob was the apportioned-allotment of his inheritance). Pauline-application: the OT-pattern of Israel as God's chosen-portion-and-inheritance is now extended to all-believers (including Gentiles in Christ). The HAPAX κληρόω (be-allotted-as-portion) at EPH 1:11 evokes the same κλῆρος (lot/portion) lexical-family. Same theme reappears in EPH 1:14 (κληρονομία, inheritance) + EPH 1:18 (κληρονομία ἐν τοῖς ἁγίοις, inheritance in the saints).

EPH 2:13.notes: Echo of Isa 57:19 LXX 'εἰρήνην ἐπ’ εἰρήνην τοῖς μακρὰν καὶ τοῖς ἐγγὺς οὖσιν' (peace upon peace to those far and to those near). Paul's μακρὰν / ἐγγύς language directly evokes the Isa 57:19 prophecy — far+near peace-promise. The same OT-text is then quoted more fully at EPH 2:17 (the more direct quotation).

EPH 2:17.notes: Greek Isaiah 57:19 places the two peace words together and addresses those far and near, ending the description with οὖσιν. Ephesians 2:17 adds Christ's coming and proclamation and addresses ‘you’ who were far. SBLGNT repeats ‘peace’ before those near; Robinson–Pierpont omits the second occurrence. Isaiah's following promise of healing is not repeated here.

EPH 2:20.notes: Echo of Isaiah 28:16 LXX 'ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ ἐμβάλλω εἰς τὰ θεμέλια Σιων λίθον ... ἀκρογωνιαῖον' (behold I lay-as-foundation in Zion a stone ... a cornerstone). Paul's ἀκρογωνιαῖος + θεμέλιος pair directly evokes the Isaian-cornerstone-prophecy. Combined-allusion-with Ps 118:22 LXX (rejected-stone-becomes-head-of-the-corner) — both texts treat-Christ-as-the-foundational-cornerstone of God's-people. Same OT-cluster at 1Pe 2:6-8.

EPH 4:8.notes: The citation adapts Greek Psalm 67:19 (English 68:18, Eremos Thai 68:19). The psalm addresses “you” throughout: you ascended, took captives and received gifts among humanity. Ephesians begins with a participle, then says he took captives and gave gifts to people. ทรงนำเชลยไปเป็นเชลย repeats เชลย but นำ…ไป conveys leading the captives away. The Targum also speaks of giving. That agreement leaves the historical route open. WH, Tregelles and RP include καί before “gave,” while SBLGNT and NA28 omit it. Thai และ joins the actions naturally.

EPH 4:25.notes: The allusion to Zechariah 8:16 recalls its command to speak truth and its concern for just judgments. Greek Zechariah uses πρός with an accusative for speaking to one’s neighbor. Ephesians uses μετά with a genitive for speaking with one’s neighbor. ต่อ identifies the neighbor addressed in Thai. Putting away falsehood recalls putting off the old self in 4:22, and the reason given here is that we are members of one another.

EPH 4:26.notes: Verbatim citation of Rahlfs Psalm 4:5 (4:4 in common English numbering) 'ὀργίζεσθε καὶ μὴ ἁμαρτάνετε' (be angry and do not sin). Two-word-imperatival-pair preserved exactly. Pauline-application: anger-itself is not sinful, but anger-leading-to-sin is. The practical-extension follows: don't-let-the-sun-set-on-anger.

EPH 4:24.notes: Echo of Gen 1:26-27 LXX 'κατ’ εἰκόνα ἡμετέραν' (in our image). Paul's 'τὸν κατὰ θεὸν κτισθέντα' (the [new man] created according to God) borrows the image-of-God-creation language but applies it to NEW-CREATION: the new-self being created-in-God's-image. Same Pauline-Christological adaptation as COL 3:10 (which makes the εἰκών language explicit).

EPH 4:30.notes: The allusion to Isaiah 63:10 connects human conduct with God’s Holy Spirit. Greek Isaiah has παρώξυναν, “they provoked,” whereas Ephesians uses λυπεῖτε, “grieve.” The Thai passages share เศร้าเสียพระทัย, and ทรงเศร้าเสียพระทัย here expresses the Spirit’s grief. The sealing recalls 1:13–14 and looks ahead to the day of redemption.

EPH 5:2.notes: Echo of LXX Lev cultic-formula 'ὀσμὴ εὐωδίας' (fragrant-aroma) — same Levitical-burnt-offering language used at PHP 4:18 (already in DB). Paul applies the Levitical-cultic-language to Christ's-cross as the supreme accepted-burnt-offering to God. Lev 1:9 cited as canonical-locus though the formula recurs throughout Pentateuch.

EPH 5:31.notes: Ephesians quotes Genesis 2:24 closely, with a different introduction, implicit possessives with the parents and, in the selected edition, a dative for the wife. Matthew 19:5 and Mark 10:7–8 also use the one-flesh saying. Ephesians 5:32 relates it to Christ and the church.

EPH 5:33.notes: Echo of Lev 19:18 LXX 'ἀγαπήσεις τὸν πλησίον σου ὡς σεαυτόν' (love your neighbor as yourself). Paul's 'ἀγαπάτω ὡς ἑαυτόν' (love as yourself) borrows the OT-love-command structure but applies it to husband-wife relations specifically. The Mosaic-love-command extended to marriage.

EPH 6:2.notes: The command follows Exodus 20:12 in Rahlfs. Deuteronomy 5:16 also has σου after μητέρα. Ephesians reads: 'τίμα τὸν πατέρα σου καὶ τὴν μητέρα.' Pauline-noting that this is uniquely-the-first-commandment-with-promise. The promise-clause continues at v.3.

EPH 6:3.notes: Paul adapts the promise in Rahlfs Exodus 20:12 and Deuteronomy 5:16. He replaces ἵνα μακροχρόνιος γένῃ with ἔσῃ μακροχρόνιος and omits the description of the land that the Lord gives. Ephesians reads 'ἵνα εὖ σοι γένηται καὶ ἔσῃ μακροχρόνιος' (that-it-may-go-well and you-be-long-lived). Paul applies the original-Israel-promise to the Christian-readers.

EPH 6:14.notes: Echo of Isa 11:5 LXX 'ἔσται δικαιοσύνῃ ἐζωσμένος τὴν ὀσφὺν αὐτοῦ' (girded-with-righteousness-around-his-waist) — Messianic-armor-prophecy. Combined with Isa 59:17 echo for the breastplate-of-righteousness. Paul applies the Messianic-and-divine-warrior armor to the believer.

EPH 6:15.notes: Greek Isaiah 52:7 has ὡς πόδες εὐαγγελιζομένου ἀκοὴν εἰρήνης, a messenger bringing news of peace. Romans 10:15 has ὡραῖοι οἱ πόδες and refers to people bringing good things. Ephesians 6:15 brings together feet, readiness and the gospel of peace in its armor imagery.

EPH 6:17.notes: Direct lexical-borrowing of Isa 59:17 LXX 'περικεφαλαίαν σωτηρίου' (helmet-of-salvation) — God-as-divine-warrior imagery. Same OT-text Paul echoes at 1Th 5:8 (already in DB). The breastplate-of-righteousness in v.14 is from-the-same Isa 59:17 verse.

1TI 1:9-10.notes: Vice list (parents/murder/sex/theft/false-witness) deliberately mirrors the second half of the Decalogue (commandments 5-9). Not a verbal citation but a structural echo: Paul reorders the commandments thematically to argue the law DOES condemn these specific evils — direct rebuttal to the false-teachers' law-misuse in v.7.

1TI 2:5.notes: Echoes the Shema (LXX Deut 6:4 'κύριος ὁ θεὸς ἡμῶν κύριος εἷς ἐστιν'). Pauline-monotheism formula 'εἷς θεός' draws on Israel's foundational creedal-confession, but extends it Christologically with 'εἷς μεσίτης' (one mediator) — preserving monotheism while adding Christological-uniqueness.

1TI 4:4.notes: Pauline-creational-affirmation echoing Genesis 1's repeated 'καλόν / טוֹב' refrain (esp. Gen 1:31 'καλὰ λίαν'). 'Every creation of God is good' directly inverts the false-teachers' food-asceticism by recalling God's-original-creational-evaluation.

HEB 6:14.notes: Greek Genesis 22:17 promises blessing to Abraham and multiplication of his offspring. Hebrews 6:14 says σε (“you”) after both verbs and prints Εἰ μήν where Rahlfs Genesis has ἦ μήν. Thai retains the second-person object.

HEB 6:7.notes: OT-allusion: GEN 1:11-12 LXX (‘βοτάνη χόρτου σπεῖρον σπέρμα’ — vegetation creation-ordinance, the βοτάνη-keyword). DEU 11:11 LXX thematic-parallel (‘land-drinks-rain-from-heaven’). GEN 27:27 LXX echo (‘a-field-which-the-LORD-blessed’ — the-good-land-blessed-from-heaven motif). Frames the-vv.7-8 farming-analogy (good-land-blessed) within-creation-and-promised-land typology.

HEB 6:8.notes: OT-allusion DIRECT-VERBAL: GEN 3:17-18 LXX ‘ἀκάνθας καὶ τριβόλους ἀνατελεῖ σοι’ — the-ground-cursed-after-Adam's-fall ‘will-bring-forth thorns-and-thistles for-you.’ The-doublet ἀκάνθας-καὶ-τριβόλους in HEB 6:8 verbatim-matches GEN 3:18 LXX. Author uses-Adam's-curse imagery for-the-fruitless-apostate's-end. Possible-secondary-echo: ISA 5:1-7 LXX vineyard-song (Israel-as-fruitless-vineyard cursed-with-thorns).

HEB 7:1.notes: OT ALLUSION GEN 14:17-20 (Melchizedek + Abraham encounter). Author paraphrases the Genesis narrative — Melchizedek as king of Salem + priest of God Most High meeting Abraham returning from defeating the four-kings coalition. HAPAX κοπή. Ground of the typological argument that runs through HEB 7.

HEB 7:2.notes: OT ALLUSION GEN 14:18-20 (the tithing + name-translation). Hebrew name-wordplay malki-tsedek = king-of-righteousness; Salem ↔ shalom = peace. Author treats both etymologies as theologically-loaded prefigurations of the Messiah-king of righteousness + peace.

HEB 7:3.notes: OT ALLUSION GEN 14:18-20 (silentium-scripturae argument: no parents, genealogy, birth, or death recorded for Melchizedek). PSA 110:4 echo (priest-forever). THREE HAPAXES (ἀπάτωρ ἀμήτωρ ἀγενεαλόγητος) + a fourth (ἀφομοιόω). Typological linkage: Melchizedek made-like the Son, not the reverse.

HEB 7:5.notes: OT ALLUSION NUM 18:21-24 (the Levitical tithe-law commanding the Levites to collect tithes from the rest of Israel — Aaronic priests as recipients). HAPAX Λευιτικός awaiting v.11.

HEB 7:14.notes: OT ALLUSION GEN 49:10 (the Judah-prophecy: scepter shall not depart from Judah) + ISA 11:1 (rod from the stem of Jesse) + 2 SAM 7:12-13 (Davidic-line covenant). The ἀνατέλλω metaphor (sun-rising) possibly echoes ISA 60:1, MAL 4:2 messianic-dawn imagery. Author argues from common-knowledge (πρόδηλον) that Jesus is from Judah, not Levi.

HEB 7:17.notes: DIRECT CITATION PSA 110:4 LXX [PSA 109:4]. Σὺ ἱερεὺς εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα κατὰ τὴν τάξιν Μελχισέδεκ — third occurrence in HEB (after 5:6, 5:10) and the load-bearing OT-text for the chapter argument. Thai matches the corpus-locked formula at HEB 5:6 exactly.

HEB 7:21.notes: Greek Psalm 109:4 (English 110:4) contains the oath, the priesthood for ever and the phrase about the order of Melchizedek. Here Hebrews quotes the oath and the priesthood, ending before the Melchizedek phrase in the selected text. The Byzantine text includes that phrase. Verse 17 quotes the priesthood and the Melchizedek phrase.

HEB 8:1.notes: OT ECHO PSA 110:1 (sit at my right hand) — author returns to the right-hand-of-Majesty motif from HEB 1:3. Thai inclusio with HEB 1:3 phrasing 'ทรงประทับเบื้องขวา.'

HEB 8:5.notes: The quotation follows Greek Exodus 25:40 with πάντα (“everything”) added and δειχθέντα in place of δεδειγμένον for the pattern shown to Moses. Acts 7:44 recounts the instruction in indirect speech. Both passages speak of the pattern.

HEB 8:8.notes: Hebrews introduces the Jeremiah 31:31–34 oracle (Greek 38:31–34). At its opening, Hebrews uses συντελέσω with ἐπί and the two houses, where Greek Jeremiah has διαθήσομαι with datives. Second Corinthians 3:6 shares the new-covenant phrase. Romans 11:27 opens with language from Isaiah 59:21.

HEB 8:9.notes: Continues JER 31:32 LXX [JER 38:32 LXX]. Exodus-imagery (God grasping hand to lead out of Egypt). ἀμελέω rare (5x NT). The argument-pivot: the people's failure in the old covenant required the new.

HEB 8:10.notes: Greek Jeremiah 38:33 (English 31:33) pairs διδοὺς with δώσω. Hebrews uses the participle without that second finite verb and has ἐπιγράψω for inscribing the laws on hearts. The promise still places the laws within the people.

HEB 8:11.notes: Continues JER 31:34a LXX [JER 38:34a LXX]. Quote-within-quote (γνῶθι τὸν κύριον). Universal-internal-knowledge of God among the covenant-people. Cf. 1 JN 2:20, 27 (Spirit-given direct-knowledge).

HEB 8:12.notes: Concludes JER 31:34b LXX [JER 38:34b LXX]. The forgiveness-promise as basis-of-covenant. Cross-reference HEB 10:17-18 (re-quoted) + 9:14 (clearing-the-conscience). Climactic-element of the new-covenant: forgiveness-as-precondition-of-Spirit-internalization.

HEB 8:2.notes: OT LEXICAL ECHO: HAPAX πήγνυμι echoes LXX tent-pitching technical-vocabulary (EXO 33:7 ἔπηξεν τὴν σκηνήν αὐτοῦ + NUM 1:51 πηγνυόντες τὴν σκηνήν). The Lord-as-Tabernacle-builder framing aligns with EXO 33:7 LXX. ทรงตั้งขึ้น Thai-rendering captures the technical-set-up sense.

HEB 9:2.notes: OT ALLUSION EXO 25:23-40 LXX (lampstand + table + showbread instructions); LEV 24:5-9 (12 loaves on the table). λυχνία + τράπεζα + πρόθεσις-τῶν-ἄρτων technical-tabernacle-vocabulary.

HEB 9:3.notes: OT ALLUSION EXO 26:31-33 LXX (the inner curtain dividing Holy Place from Most Holy Place). καταπέτασμα-τὸ-δεύτερον = the inner veil. Naming convention Ἅγια Ἁγίων follows LXX Holy-of-Holies usage.

HEB 9:4.notes: Hebrews places the jar, Aaron’s staff and the tablets in the ark. Exodus 16:33–34 and Numbers 17 concern preservation of the manna and staff, while Deuteronomy 10:5 expressly places the tablets inside. At the dedication of Solomon’s temple, 1 Kings 8:9 records only the tablets inside. These accounts describe different occasions.

HEB 9:5.notes: OT ALLUSION EXO 25:17-22 LXX (cherubim of glory overshadowing the mercy-seat). HAPAXES Χερουβίν + κατασκιάζω. ἱλαστήριον in HEB-9-physical-context = the cover-of-the-ark (Mercy Seat = พระที่นั่งกรุณา); distinct-rendering from ROM 3:25 propitiatory-Christological.

HEB 9:7.notes: OT ALLUSION LEV 16 (Day of Atonement: high priest entering Most Holy Place once a year with blood for own + people's sins) + LEV 4:2-3, 5:14-19 (sacrifices for ἀγνοήματα = unintentional sins). HAPAX ἀγνόημα. Echoes HEB 5:1-3, 7:27.

HEB 9:13.notes: OT ALLUSION LEV 16:14-19 (Day of Atonement: blood of bull + goats sprinkled for purification) + NUM 19:1-10 (red heifer rite: ashes mixed with water for ritual-defilement). HAPAXES δάμαλις + καθαρότης. The two rituals together represent the LEV-system's external-physical purification.

HEB 9:19.notes: The selected Greek mentions calves. NA28 brackets the additional words “and of goats,” included in the English comparison. Exodus 24:7–8 records reading the book and sprinkling the people. Hebrews also mentions sprinkling the book.

HEB 9:20.notes: Greek Exodus 24:8 opens “Behold,” says that the Lord made the covenant, and closes by referring to the words. Hebrews opens “This,” says God commanded it, and leaves off that closing phrase. Matthew 26:28 includes γάρ in the words over the cup. Mark 14:24 has no γάρ.

HEB 9:21.notes: Leviticus 8:10–11 describes anointing the tent and sprinkling the altar with oil. Verse 19 uses ram blood around the altar. Leviticus 16:14–19 uses animal blood in the inner sanctuary and at the altar, and includes the tent in the rite. Hebrews describes sprinkling the tent and its vessels with blood.

HEB 9:22.notes: OT FOUNDATION LEV 17:11 (life of the flesh in the blood; blood makes atonement on the altar). HAPAX αἱματεκχυσία (only NT — bloodshedding). σχεδόν 'nearly' acknowledges exceptions like LEV 5:11-13 (grain-offering for the poor). The verse encapsulates the Levitical-sacrificial principle.

HEB 9:25.notes: OT ALLUSION LEV 16 — high priest enters Most Holy Place annually with blood-of-another (sacrificial-animal). Pointed contrast with HEB 9:12 (Christ enters with own-blood once-for-all).

HEB 9:28.notes: OT ALLUSION ISA 53:12 LXX (καὶ αὐτὸς ἁμαρτίας πολλῶν ἀνήνεγκεν — 'he bore the sins of many'). HEB 9:28 ἅπαξ προσενεχθεὶς εἰς τὸ πολλῶν ἀνενεγκεῖν ἁμαρτίας echoes the Servant Song. Cross-reference 1 PE 2:24.

HEB 10:5.notes: DIRECT CITATION PSA 40:6 LXX [PSA 39:7 LXX] BEGINS HERE — extends through v.7. The LXX has σῶμα κατηρτίσω μοι ('a body you prepared for me') where MT-Hebrew has 'ears you have dug for me' — author follows LXX which is foundational for the incarnation Christology. Christ-as-Davidic-figure speaks the psalm as his incarnation-formula.

HEB 10:6.notes: Greek Psalm 39:7 (English 40:6) has a singular burnt offering and says “you did not ask.” Hebrews uses plural burnt offerings and says “you did not take pleasure.”

HEB 10:7.notes: Hebrews draws on Greek Psalm 39:8–9 (English 40:7–8). The Psalm says “my God” and “I desired” before continuing with the law within. Hebrews addresses God, places doing his will as the purpose of coming, and stops there.

HEB 10:13.notes: The footstool image evokes Greek Psalm 109:1 (English 110:1). Hebrews 1:13 quotes God addressing the Son directly. Here the enemies are made a footstool for his feet, with a passive verb and third-person references.

HEB 10:16.notes: Compared with Greek Jeremiah 38:33 and Hebrews 8:10, this quotation puts hearts before mind and uses ἐπί for both locations.

HEB 10:17.notes: Compared with Greek Jeremiah 38:34 and Hebrews 8:12, the mercy clause is omitted, lawless acts appear alongside sins, and the remembering verb is μνησθήσομαι rather than μνησθῶ. The Thai speech introduction supplies the connection with verse 15.

HEB 10:27.notes: OT ALLUSION ISA 26:11 LXX (ζῆλος λήμψεται ... καὶ νῦν πῦρ τοὺς ὑπεναντίους ἔδεται — fire-consuming-adversaries). HAPAX ἐκδοχή. The vivid-imagery contrasts with v.22 draw-near.

HEB 10:28.notes: Deuteronomy 17:2–7 requires multiple witnesses in a capital case concerning worship of other gods. Deuteronomy 19:15 generalizes the requirement to accusations of wrongdoing. Hebrews recalls the rule while speaking of death under Moses’ law.

HEB 10:30.greek_matches: TWO DIRECT CITATIONS (DEU 32:35 Targum/Heb-form; DEU 32:36 LXX-direct)
HEB 10:30.notes: TWO DIRECT CITATIONS from the Song of Moses. DEU 32:35 (Vengeance is mine, I will repay) — HEB matches ROM 12:19 form (closer to MT/Targum than LXX). DEU 32:36 LXX-direct (The Lord will judge his people). Both citations appeal to God-as-judge.

HEB 10:37.notes: DIRECT CITATION ISA 26:20 LXX (μικρὸν ὅσον ὅσον — yet a little while) + HAB 2:3 LXX (ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἥξει καὶ οὐ χρονίσει — the coming one will come and will not delay). Combined-citation merging Isaiah's 'little while' with Habakkuk's 'coming one' — Christological-application of the soon-coming-Messiah.

HEB 10:38.notes: DIRECT CITATION HAB 2:4 LXX. The Greek text reorders the Hab 2:4 LXX clauses (HEB has 'my righteous one will live by faith' first, then 'if he shrinks back, my soul takes no pleasure'). ROM 1:17 + GAL 3:11 use Hab 2:4 differently (without 'my'). HEB preserves μου, making God the explicit speaker. Foundational text for NT pistis-language.

HEB 10:26.notes: OT ALLUSION NUM 15:30-31 (intentional sin with high-hand vs unintentional sin) — the Mosaic-system explicitly excluded deliberate-defiant sin from atonement. ἑκουσίως (deliberately) echoes the Numbers distinction. The author warns that those who reject Christ after knowing him forfeit the only sacrifice that could cover such intentional rejection.

HEB 11:3.notes: OT ALLUSION GEN 1 (creation by divine word). 'God said' creation-by-fiat foundational doctrine; sets up creatio-ex-nihilo implication.

HEB 11:4.notes: OT ALLUSION GEN 4:1-10 (Cain + Abel + Abel's blood crying out). Echoes HEB 12:24 'the blood of Abel.' uW figs-personification on the speaking-blood.

HEB 11:5.notes: Hebrew Genesis 5:22, 24 describes walking with God. Greek Genesis uses the language of pleasing God, which Hebrews develops. For Enoch’s removal Hebrews has διότι, where the Greek of Genesis 5:24 has ὅτι.

HEB 11:7.notes: OT ALLUSION GEN 6-9 (Noah's ark and the flood). Noah's faith-built ark + condemned the world + heir of righteousness-by-faith.

HEB 11:8.notes: Genesis 12:4–5 names Haran as the place of departure and Canaan as the destination in the narrative. Hebrews emphasizes that Abraham obeyed without yet knowing where he was going.

HEB 11:9.notes: OT ALLUSION GEN 23 (Abraham buying burial-site as resident-alien); GEN 26 + 28 (Isaac + Jacob nomadic-pilgrim life).

HEB 11:11.notes: OT ALLUSION GEN 17:15-21 + 18:9-15 + 21:1-7 (Sarah's conception promise + fulfillment). uW textual-issue: Sarah-vs-Abraham as subject — SBLGNT supports Sarah-subject reading.

HEB 11:12.notes: OT ALLUSION combined formula: GEN 15:5 (stars-of-heaven) + GEN 22:17, 32:12 (sand-of-seashore). Innumerable-descendants promise.

HEB 11:13.notes: Greek Genesis 23:4 and Psalm 38:13 (English 39:12) pair πάροικος with παρεπίδημος. Hebrews pairs ξένος with παρεπίδημος. The Thai distinguishes คนแปลกหน้า and คนต่างถิ่น. The earlier texts provide a related image.

HEB 11:17.notes: OT ALLUSION GEN 22:1-19 (Aqedah / binding of Isaac). Imperfect προσέφερεν marks the act-was-in-progress-but-not-completed.

HEB 11:18.notes: DIRECT CITATION GEN 21:12 LXX (Ἐν Ἰσαὰκ κληθήσεταί σοι σπέρμα — verbatim). Same quote-formula at ROM 9:7. The contrast: God-promised line-through-Isaac + God-tested by-asking-Isaac as offering.

HEB 11:19.notes: OT ALLUSION GEN 22:5 (Abraham's promise to return with Isaac) + 22:13 (ram in thicket). Author's typological reading: Isaac-back-from-death = type of resurrection (ἐν παραβολῇ).

HEB 11:20.notes: OT ALLUSION GEN 27 (Isaac blessing Jacob then Esau). Inverted-order (younger before older) = the faith-element.

HEB 11:21.notes: DIRECT CITATION (LXX-form) GEN 47:31. uW textual-issue: LXX 'staff' (ῥάβδος) vs MT 'bed' (מטה — same Hebrew consonants, different vowels: matteh/mittah). HEB follows LXX. Jacob-worshiped-while-dying acknowledging God's faithfulness.

HEB 11:22.notes: OT ALLUSION GEN 50:24-25 (Joseph's deathbed prophecy + bone-instructions) + EXO 13:19 (fulfillment 400 years later when Israel left Egypt).

HEB 11:23.notes: Hebrews says Moses’ parents hid him and did not fear the edict. Hebrew Exodus 2:2 names his mother hiding him for three months. Acts 7:20 calls him beautiful to God.

HEB 11:24.notes: Exodus 2:10–15 narrates Moses’ adoption and his going out to his people. Hebrews describes the adult Moses as refusing to be called the son of Pharaoh’s daughter. Exodus records no speech of renunciation.

HEB 11:27.notes: OT ALLUSION EXO 2:14-15 (Moses' first flight from Egypt) OR EXO 12-14 (Moses leading Israel out) — uW chapter-intro flags both readings as possible.

HEB 11:28.notes: OT ALLUSION EXO 12 (Passover institution + blood on doorposts + destroying-angel passing-over Israelite firstborn).

HEB 11:29.notes: OT ALLUSION EXO 14 (Red Sea miracle: Israel passes through dry, Egyptians drowned).

HEB 11:30.notes: OT ALLUSION JOS 6 (Jericho-walls falling after seven days of marching).

HEB 11:31.notes: OT ALLUSION JOS 2 + 6:22-25 (Rahab + the Israelite spies). Cross-reference JAS 2:25 (parallel-faith-tradition).

HEB 11:32.notes: OT ALLUSION cluster: JDG 6-8 (Gideon), JDG 4-5 (Barak), JDG 13-16 (Samson), JDG 11-12 (Jephthah), 1-2 Sam (David, Samuel), prophets generally.

HEB 11:33.notes: OT ALLUSION cluster: kingdoms-conquered (David's wars, Joshua); justice-administered (Samuel as judge); promises-gained (David's throne); lions'-mouths-shut (DAN 6 — Daniel).

HEB 11:34.notes: OT ALLUSION cluster: DAN 3 (3 Hebrew youths in fiery furnace) + various-OT escape-narratives (David, Elijah, Elisha) + military-victories.

HEB 11:35.notes: OT ALLUSION 1 KGS 17:17-24 (Elijah + widow's son) + 2 KGS 4:18-37 (Elisha + Shunammite's son) + 2 Maccabees 6-7 (Eleazar + the seven brothers + their mother — the Maccabean-martyrs whose torture-by-rack matches τυμπανίζω).

HEB 11:36.notes: OT ALLUSION prophetic-imprisonments (Jeremiah, Micaiah, etc.). HAPAX ἐμπαιγμός.

HEB 11:37.notes: OT ALLUSION 2 KGS 2:13-14 (Elijah's mantle = μηλωτή sheepskin-cloak) + traditional Isaiah-martyrdom (sawn-in-two per Ascension-of-Isaiah / Lives of the Prophets) + general OT-prophetic-sufferings.

HEB 11:38.notes: OT ALLUSION 1 KGS 18-19 (Elijah hiding in cave + Obadiah hiding 100 prophets in caves at 1 KGS 18:4) + 2 Maccabees 5:27 (Maccabean hiding in mountains).

HEB 12:5.notes: Greek Proverbs 3:11 addresses the learner as “son.” Hebrews has “my son.” The parental exhortation speaks about the Lord in third person.

HEB 12:6.notes: The Greek of Proverbs 3:12 provides the wording about chastening and scourging that Hebrews quotes. The Hebrew form, reflected in Thai Proverbs, compares the Lord with a father who delights in his son.

HEB 12:12.notes: OT ALLUSION ISA 35:3 LXX (ἰσχύσατε χεῖρες ἀνειμέναι, καὶ γόνατα παραλελυμένα — eschatological-restoration imagery: strengthen-feeble-hands + weak-knees). HAPAX παρίημι in HEB.

HEB 12:13.notes: OT ALLUSION PRO 4:26 LXX (ὀρθὰς τροχιὰς ποίει σοῖς ποσίν — make-straight-tracks-for-feet). HAPAX τροχιά. Concludes the exhortation-cluster (vv.12-13).

HEB 12:15.notes: OT ALLUSION DEU 29:18 LXX (ῥίζα ἄνω φύουσα ἐν χολῇ καὶ πικρίᾳ — root-springing-up-in-gall-and-bitterness). uW figs-metaphor: bitterness as corrosive-corruption in community.

HEB 12:17.notes: OT ALLUSION GEN 27:30-40 (Esau-weeping-after-losing-blessing-from-Isaac). HAPAX μετέπειτα. The warning: irrevocability-of-some-rejections.

HEB 12:18.notes: The mountain is implicit in the selected text, while the Byzantine text names it and has a different darkness term. The reference is Sinai. Deuteronomy 4:11–12 recalls the burning mountain, thick darkness, storm and voice. Compare Exodus 19.

HEB 12:19.notes: OT ALLUSION EXO 20:18-19 (Israelites asking Moses to be their mediator at Sinai — too-fearful-to-hear-directly).

HEB 12:20.notes: Greek Exodus 19:12 prohibits touching the mountain. Verse 13 includes both animals and people and gives stoning or shooting as penalties. Hebrews brings the animal case together with stoning and uses θηρίον for the animal.

HEB 12:21.notes: Greek Deuteronomy 9:19 places Moses’ fear in his intercession after the golden calf. Hebrews uses the expression “I am afraid” in its Sinai description and adds “and trembling.”

HEB 12:24.notes: OT ALLUSION GEN 4:10 (Abel's-blood-crying-out-for-vengeance). Christ's blood-speaks-better than-Abel's = forgiveness-vs-vengeance. Cross-reference HEB 11:4.

HEB 12:26.notes: Greek Haggai 2:6 names heaven, earth, sea and dry land. Hebrews starts with earth, follows with heaven, and omits sea and dry land. Its explicit “not only … but also” makes the contrast prominent.

HEB 12:29.notes: DIRECT CITATION DEU 4:24 LXX (πῦρ καταναλίσκον — consuming-fire). HAPAX καταναλίσκω. Closes HEB 12. Divine-fire-imagery balances the festal-Mt-Zion (v.22) with judgment-aware reverence.

HEB 13:2.notes: OT ALLUSION GEN 18 (Abraham hosting three angelic visitors) + GEN 19 (Lot hosting two angels). Hospitality-to-strangers as unwitting-angel-hosting.

HEB 13:5.notes: The promise recalls Deuteronomy 31:6, 8 and Joshua 1:5. Greek Deuteronomy says in third person that God will not abandon his people. Joshua addresses his hearer in first person, with different verb forms. Hebrews has two first-person verbs and emphatic negatives.

HEB 13:6.notes: The selected wording, like Greek Psalm 117:6 (English 118:6), goes directly from the Lord as helper to “I will not fear.” NA28 brackets καί (“and”) before the latter clause.

HEB 13:11.notes: OT ALLUSION LEV 16:27 (sin-offering bodies burned outside camp on Day of Atonement). Sets up the v.12 typology of Christ suffering outside-the-gate.

HEB 13:15.notes: Greek Psalm 49:14 (English 50:14) uses θυσίαν αἰνέσεως, a sacrifice of praise. Greek Hosea 14:3 has καρπὸν χειλέων ἡμῶν, the fruit of our lips. Hebrews describes these lips as acknowledging God’s name.

HEB 13:20.notes: OT ALLUSION cluster: ISA 63:11 LXX (the bringing-up-the-shepherd-of-the-sheep formula) + ZEC 9:11 (blood of the covenant) + EZK 34 (good-shepherd discourse). The benediction draws together Hebrews' major Christological themes — Christ as great-Shepherd + mediator of new (eternal) covenant.

HEB 13:12.notes: OT TYPOLOGY LEV 16:27 (Day-of-Atonement bodies-burned-outside-camp). Christ-suffered-outside-Jerusalem-walls typologically-fulfills the LEV-pattern. Cross-reference v.11.

MAT 27:24.notes: Pilate washes his hands and disclaims responsibility for bloodshed. The elders in Deuteronomy wash their hands and declare that they did not shed the blood. The scenes differ: Pilate is publicly involved in the trial.

MAT 27:25.notes: The crowd’s answer takes responsibility in the idiom of blood falling upon someone. Compare David’s statement to the man in 2 Samuel 1:16 that his blood is on his own head.

MRK 10:4.notes: The speakers say Moses permitted writing a certificate of divorce and dismissing a wife. Greek Deuteronomy 24:1 has βιβλίον ἀποστασίου and describes giving the document to her and sending her away. Deuteronomy 24:1–4 sets out conditions and then a prohibition about later remarriage. Mark summarizes part of that sequence as permission.

JHN 1:1.notes: John 1:1 and Greek Genesis 1:1 share ἐν ἀρχῇ. The Word and creation themes develop the allusion; the clauses that follow the common opening differ.
